sanskrit_iast: oṃ brahma ha vā idam agra āsīt svayaṃbhv ekam eva tadaikṣata mahad vai yakṣam yad ekam evāsmi hantāhaṃ mad eva manmātraṃ dvitīyaṃ devaṃ nirmimā iti tad abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasya śrāntasya taptasya saṃtaptasya lalāṭe sneho yad ārdram ājāyata tenānandat tad abravīt mahad vai yakṣaṃ suvedam avidam aham iti tad yad abravīt mahad vai yakṣaṃ suvedam avidam aham iti tasmāt suvedo 'bhavat taṃ vā etaṃ suvedaṃ santaṃ sveda ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ ||
meaning: ओं ब्रह्म ह वा इदम् अग्र आसीत् स्वयंभ्व् एकम् एव तदैक्षत महद् वै यक्षम् यद् एकम् एवास्मि हन्ताहं मद् एव मन्मात्रं द्वितीयं देवं निर्मिमा इति तद् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तस्य श्रान्तस्य तप्तस्य संतप्तस्य ललाटे स्नेहो यद् आर्द्रम् आजायत तेनानन्दत् तद् अब्रवीत् महद् वै यक्षं सुवेदम् अविदम् अहम् इति तद् यद् अब्रवीत् महद् वै यक्षं सुवेदम् अविदम् अहम् इति तस्मात् सुवेदो ऽभवत् तं वा एतं सुवेदं सन्तं स्वेद इत्य् आचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवा भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षद्विषः ||
text_mt:
Oṃ. In the beginning this [universe] was Brahman alone, self-existent, one only.
It reflected:
'Great indeed is the wondrous being that I am alone.
Come, let me fashion from myself alone a second god of my own measure.'
It toiled over it, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated itself.
As it was toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, moisture—what was wet—arose on its brow.
It rejoiced at that.
It said:
'Great indeed is the wondrous being that I have easily found [suvedam]!'
Because it said:
'Great indeed is the wondrous being that I have easily found [suvedam]!'
therefore it became sweat [suveda].
Him who is this sweat [suveda] they cryptically call sveda [perspiration];
for the gods are fond of the cryptic, as it were, and detest the direct. || 1

sanskrit_iast: sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyad bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat tasya śrāntasya taptasya saṃtaptasya sarvebhyo romagartebhyaḥ pṛthaksvedadhārāḥ prāsyandanta tābhir anandat tad abravīt ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃ ca ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ janayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃ ca ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ āpsyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃ ceti tad yad abravīt ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃ ceti tasmād dhārā abhavan tad dhārāṇāṃ dhārātvaṃ yac cāsu dhriyate tad yad abravīt ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ janayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃ ceti tasmāj jāyā abhavan taj jāyānāṃ jāyātvaṃ yac cāsu puruṣo jāyate yac ca putraḥ pun nāma narakam anekaśatatāram tasmāt trātīti putras tat putrasya putratvam tad yad abravīt ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ āpsyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃ ceti tasmād āpo 'bhavan tad apām aptvam āpnoti vai sa sarvān kāmān yān kāmayate ||
meaning: स भूयो ऽश्राम्यद् भूयो ऽतप्यद् भूय आत्मानं समतपत् तस्य श्रान्तस्य तप्तस्य संतप्तस्य सर्वेभ्यो रोमगर्तेभ्यः पृथक्स्वेदधाराः प्रास्यन्दन्त ताभिर् अनन्दत् तद् अब्रवीत् आभिर् वा अहम् इदं सर्वं धारयिष्यामि यद् इदं किं च आभिर् वा अहम् इदं सर्वं जनयिष्यामि यद् इदं किं च आभिर् वा अहम् इदं सर्वं आप्स्यामि यद् इदं किं चेति तद् यद् अब्रवीत् आभिर् वा अहम् इदं सर्वं धारयिष्यामि यद् इदं किं चेति तस्माद् धारा अभवन् तद् धाराणां धारात्वं यच् चासु ध्रियते तद् यद् अब्रवीत् आभिर् वा अहम् इदं सर्वं जनयिष्यामि यद् इदं किं चेति तस्माज् जाया अभवन् तज् जायानां जायात्वं यच् चासु पुरुषो जायते यच् च पुत्रः पुन् नाम नरकम् अनेकशततारम् तस्मात् त्रातीति पुत्रस् तत् पुत्रस्य पुत्रत्वम् तद् यद् अब्रवीत् आभिर् वा अहम् इदं सर्वं आप्स्यामि यद् इदं किं चेति तस्माद् आपो ऽभवन् तद् अपाम् अप्त्वम् आप्नोति वै स सर्वान् कामान् यान् कामयते ||
text_mt: He laboured further, he performed ascetic heat further, he heated himself completely further. From all the hair-pores of him, weary, heated, and completely heated, separate streams of sweat flowed forth. He rejoiced in them. He said: 'By these indeed shall I sustain all this, whatsoever exists here. By these indeed shall I generate all this, whatsoever exists here. By these indeed shall I obtain all this, whatsoever exists here.' Because he said: 'By these indeed shall I sustain all this, whatsoever exists here,' therefore they became streams. That is the stream-nature of streams, and that in them [everything] is sustained. Because he said: 'By these indeed shall I generate all this, whatsoever exists here,' therefore they became wives. That is the wife-nature of wives, and that in them a man is born, and that [he is] a son. Hell of many hundreds of depths is called Put. Because he saves from that, he is a son. That is the son-nature of a son. Because he said: 'By these indeed shall I obtain all this, whatsoever exists here,' therefore they became waters. That is the water-nature of waters.

sanskrit_iast: tā apaḥ sṛṣṭvānvaikṣata tāsu svāṃ chāyām apaśyat tām asyekṣamāṇasya svayaṃ reto 'skandat tad apsu pratyatiṣṭhat tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tāḥ śrāntās taptāḥ saṃtaptāḥ sārdham eva retasā dvaidham abhavan tāsām anyatarā atilavaṇā apeyā asvādvyas tā aśāntā retaḥ samudraṃ vṛtvātiṣṭhan athetarāḥ peyāḥ svādvyaḥ śāntās tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tābhyaḥ śrāntābhyas taptābhyaḥ saṃtaptābhyo yad reta āsīt tad abhṛjjyata tasmād bhṛguḥ samabhavat tad bhṛgor bhṛgutvam bhṛgur iva vai sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: ता अपः सृष्ट्वान्वैक्षत तासु स्वां छायाम् अपश्यत् ताम् अस्येक्षमाणस्य स्वयं रेतो ऽस्कन्दत् तद् अप्सु प्रत्यतिष्ठत् तास् तत्रैवाभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् ताः श्रान्तास् तप्ताः संतप्ताः सार्धम् एव रेतसा द्वैधम् अभवन् तासाम् अन्यतरा अतिलवणा अपेया अस्वाद्व्यस् ता अशान्ता रेतः समुद्रं वृत्वातिष्ठन् अथेतराः पेयाः स्वाद्व्यः शान्तास् तास् तत्रैवाभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् ताभ्यः श्रान्ताभ्यस् तप्ताभ्यः संतप्ताभ्यो यद् रेत आसीत् तद् अभृज्ज्यत तस्माद् भृगुः समभवत् तद् भृगोर् भृगुत्वम् भृगुर् इव वै स सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
He obtains indeed all desires that he desires.

Having created these waters, it looked towards them.
In them it saw its own reflection.
As it was looking at it, semen discharged spontaneously from it.
That rested upon the waters.
Right there it toiled over them, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated them.
Toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, they, along with the semen, became divided into two.
One [portion] of them was very salty, undrinkable, unpalatable;
they, unpacified, encompassed the semen and stood as the ocean.
Then the other [portion] was drinkable, palatable, pacified.
Right there it toiled over them, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, the semen that was there was roasted [abhṛjjyata].
Therefore Bhṛgu came into being.
That is the Bhṛguness of Bhṛgu.
Like Bhṛgu indeed does he shine in all the worlds, who knows thus. || 3

sanskrit_iast: sa bhṛguṃ sṛṣṭvāntaradhīyata sa bhṛguḥ sṛṣṭaḥ prāṅ aijata taṃ vāg anvavadat vāyo vāya iti sa nyavartata sa dakṣiṇāṃ diśam aijata taṃ vāg anvavadat mātariśvan mātariśvann iti sa nyavartata sa pratīcīṃ diśam aijata taṃ vāg anvavadat pavamāna pavamāneti sa nyavartata sa udīcīṃ diśam aijata taṃ vāg anvavadat vāta vāteti tam abravīt na nv avidam aham iti na hīti athārvāṅ enam etāsv evāpsv anviccheti tad yad abravīd athārvāṅ enam etāsv evāpsv anviccheti tad atharvābhavat tad atharvaṇo 'tharvatvam tasya ha vā etasya bhagavato 'tharvaṇa ṛṣer yathaiva brahmaṇo lomāni yathāṅgāni yathā prāṇa evam evāsya sarva ātmā samabhavat tam atharvāṇaṃ brahmābravīt prajāpateḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā pālayasveti tad yad abravīt prajāpateḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā pālayasveti tasmāt prajāpatir abhavat tat prajāpateḥ prajāpatitvam atharvā vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpatir iva vai sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: स भृगुं सृष्ट्वान्तरधीयत स भृगुः सृष्टः प्राङ् ऐजत तं वाग् अन्ववदत् वायो वाय इति स न्यवर्तत स दक्षिणां दिशम् ऐजत तं वाग् अन्ववदत् मातरिश्वन् मातरिश्वन्न् इति स न्यवर्तत स प्रतीचीं दिशम् ऐजत तं वाग् अन्ववदत् पवमान पवमानेति स न्यवर्तत स उदीचीं दिशम् ऐजत तं वाग् अन्ववदत् वात वातेति तम् अब्रवीत् न न्व् अविदम् अहम् इति न हीति अथार्वाङ् एनम् एतास्व् एवाप्स्व् अन्विच्छेति तद् यद् अब्रवीद् अथार्वाङ् एनम् एतास्व् एवाप्स्व् अन्विच्छेति तद् अथर्वाभवत् तद् अथर्वणो ऽथर्वत्वम् तस्य ह वा एतस्य भगवतो ऽथर्वण ऋषेर् यथैव ब्रह्मणो लोमानि यथाङ्गानि यथा प्राण एवम् एवास्य सर्व आत्मा समभवत् तम् अथर्वाणं ब्रह्माब्रवीत् प्रजापतेः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पालयस्वेति तद् यद् अब्रवीत् प्रजापतेः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पालयस्वेति तस्मात् प्रजापतिर् अभवत् तत् प्रजापतेः प्रजापतित्वम् अथर्वा वै प्रजापतिः प्रजापतिर् इव वै स सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
Having emitted Bhṛgu, he vanished. Bhṛgu, having been emitted, moved eastward. Voice addressed him from behind: 'O Vāyu! O Vāyu!' He turned back; he moved toward the southern quarter. Voice addressed him from behind: 'O Mātariśvan! O Mātariśvan!' He turned back; he moved toward the western quarter. Voice addressed him from behind: 'O Pavamāna! O Pavamāna!' He turned back; he moved toward the northern quarter. Voice addressed him from behind: 'O Vāta! O Vāta!' He said to it: 'Have I not indeed found him?' 'Not indeed,' [Voice replied], 'now seek him downward in these very waters.' In that it said, 'now seek him downward in these very waters' (athārvāṅ enam), thereby he became Atharvan. That is the Atharvan-nature of Atharvan. Just as were the hairs of Brahman, as were his limbs, as was his breath, even so the whole body of this venerable seer Atharvan came into being. Brahman said to that Atharvan: 'O Prajāpati, having created creatures, protect them.' In that he said, 'O Prajāpati, having created creatures, protect them,' therefore he became Prajāpati.

That is the Prajāpati-nature of Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast: tam atharvāṇam ṛṣim abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād daśatayān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn niramimataikarcān dvyṛcāṃs tṛcāṃs caturṛcān pañcarcānt ṣaḍarcānt saptarcān aṣṭarcān navarcān daśarcān iti tān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo daśatayān ātharvaṇān ārṣeyān niramimataikādaśān dvādaśāṃs trayodaśāṃś caturdaśān pañcadaśān ṣoḍaśānt saptadaśān aṣṭādaśān navadaśān viṃśān iti tān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn ātharvaṇāṃś cārṣeyān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo yān mantrān apaśyat sa ātharvaṇo vedo 'bhavat tam ātharvaṇaṃ vedam abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād om iti mana evordhvam akṣaram udakrāmat sa ya icchet sarvair etair atharvabhiś cātharvaṇaiś ca kurvīyety etayaiva tan mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitair atharvabhiś cātharvaṇaiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute ||
meaning: तम् अथर्वाणम् ऋषिम् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तस्माच् छ्रान्तात् तप्तात् संतप्ताद् दशतयान् अथर्वण ऋषीन् निरमिमतैकर्चान् द्व्यृचांस् तृचांस् चतुरृचान् पञ्चर्चान्त् षडर्चान्त् सप्तर्चान् अष्टर्चान् नवर्चान् दशर्चान् इति तान् अथर्वण ऋषीन् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यो दशतयान् आथर्वणान् आर्षेयान् निरमिमतैकादशान् द्वादशांस् त्रयोदशांश् चतुर्दशान् पञ्चदशान् षोडशान्त् सप्तदशान् अष्टादशान् नवदशान् विंशान् इति तान् अथर्वण ऋषीन् आथर्वणांश् चार्षेयान् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यो यान् मन्त्रान् अपश्यत् स आथर्वणो वेदो ऽभवत् तम् आथर्वणं वेदम् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तस्माच् छ्रान्तात् तप्तात् संतप्ताद् ओम् इति मन एवोर्ध्वम् अक्षरम् उदक्रामत् स य इच्छेत् सर्वैर् एतैर् अथर्वभिश् चाथर्वणैश् च कुर्वीयेत्य् एतयैव तन् महाव्याहृत्या कुर्वीत सर्वैर् ह वा अस्यैतैर् अथर्वभिश् चाथर्वणैश् च कृतं भवति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् एवम् एतया महाव्याहृत्या कुरुते ||
text_mt:
Atharvan indeed is Prajāpati.

Like Prajāpati indeed he shines in all worlds, who knows thus.

Over that seer Atharvan it toiled, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated him.
From him, toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, it fashioned tenfold Atharvan seers: of one verse, of two verses, of three verses, of four verses, of five verses, of six verses, of seven verses, of eight verses, of nine verses, and of ten verses.
Over those Atharvan seers it toiled, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, it fashioned tenfold descendant Atharvans [ātharvaṇa-ārṣeyas]: of eleven, of twelve, of thirteen, of fourteen, of fifteen, of sixteen, of seventeen, of eighteen, of nineteen, and of twenty [verses].
Over those Atharvan seers and descendant Atharvans it toiled, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, the mantras that it saw became the Atharvaveda.
Over that Atharvaveda it toiled, exerted ascetic heat, thoroughly heated it.
From it, toiled, heated, thoroughly heated, the upward syllable 'Oṃ' arose, which was mind itself.
If one should wish: 'May I perform with all these Atharvans and Ātharvaṇas,' one should perform with this very great sacred utterance.
Indeed, performed by all these Atharvans and Ātharvaṇas it becomes for him who knows thus, and who, knowing thus, performs thus with this great sacred utterance. || 5

sanskrit_iast: sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyad bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat sa ātamata eva trīṃl lokān niramimīta pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ divam iti sa khalu pādābhyām eva pṛthivīṃ nirmamimīta udarād antarikṣaṃ mūrdhno divam sa tāṃs trīṃl lokān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas trīn devān niramimīta agniṃ vāyum ādityam iti sa khalu pṛthivyā evāgniṃ niramimītāntarikṣād vāyuṃ diva ādityam sa tāṃs trīn devān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas trīn vedān niramimīta ṛgvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam iti agner ṛgvedaṃ vāyor yajurvedaṃ ādityāt sāmavedam sa tāṃs trīn vedān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas tisro mahāvyāhṛtīr niramimīta bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti bhūr ity ṛgvedād bhuva iti yajurvedāt svar iti sāmavedāt sa ya icchet sarvair etais tribhir vedaiḥ kurvīyety etābhir eva tan mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitais tribhir vedaiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etābhir mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurute ||
meaning: स भूयो ऽश्राम्यद् भूयो ऽतप्यद् भूय आत्मानं समतपत् स आतमत एव त्रींल् लोकान् निरमिमीत पृथिवीम् अन्तरिक्षं दिवम् इति स खलु पादाभ्याम् एव पृथिवीं निर्ममिमीत उदराद् अन्तरिक्षं मूर्ध्नो दिवम् स तांस् त्रींल् लोकान् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यस् त्रीन् देवान् निरमिमीत अग्निं वायुम् आदित्यम् इति स खलु पृथिव्या एवाग्निं निरमिमीतान्तरिक्षाद् वायुं दिव आदित्यम् स तांस् त्रीन् देवान् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यस् त्रीन् वेदान् निरमिमीत ऋग्वेदं यजुर्वेदं सामवेदम् इति अग्नेर् ऋग्वेदं वायोर् यजुर्वेदं आदित्यात् सामवेदम् स तांस् त्रीन् वेदान् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यस् तिस्रो महाव्याहृतीर् निरमिमीत भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति भूर् इत्य् ऋग्वेदाद् भुव इति यजुर्वेदात् स्वर् इति सामवेदात् स य इच्छेत् सर्वैर् एतैस् त्रिभिर् वेदैः कुर्वीयेत्य् एताभिर् एव तन् महाव्याहृतिभिः कुर्वीत सर्वैर् ह वा अस्यैतैस् त्रिभिर् वेदैः कृतं भवति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् एवम् एताभिर् महाव्याहृतिभिः कुरुते ||
text_mt:
He toiled further, he generated heat further, he thoroughly heated himself further.
He, having heated himself thoroughly, created the three worlds: the earth, the intermediate space, [and] heaven.
From his feet indeed he created the earth,
from his belly the intermediate space, from his head heaven.
He toiled over these three worlds, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created three gods:
Agni, Vāyu, [and] Āditya.
From the earth indeed he created Agni, from the intermediate space Vāyu, from heaven Āditya.
He toiled over these three gods, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created the three Vedas: the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, [and] the Sāmaveda—
the Ṛgveda from Agni, the Yajurveda from Vāyu, the Sāmaveda from Āditya.
He toiled over these three Vedas, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created the three great sacred utterances: bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ—
bhūr from the Ṛgveda, bhuvaḥ from the Yajurveda, svaḥ from the Sāmaveda.
If one wishes, 'May I perform with all these three Vedas,' one should perform it with just these great sacred utterances.
It is performed for him with all these three Vedas, whoever knows this and, knowing thus, performs thus with these great sacred utterances. || 6

sanskrit_iast: tā yā amū retaḥ samudraṃ vṛtvātiṣṭhaṃs tāḥ prācyo dakṣiṇācyaḥ pratīcya udīcyaḥ samavadravanta tad yat samavadravanta tasmāt samudra ucyate tā bhītā abruvan bhagavantam eva vayaṃ rājānaṃ vṛṇīmaha iti yac ca vṛtvātiṣṭhaṃs tad varaṇo 'bhavat taṃ vā etaṃ varaṇaṃ santaṃ varuṇa ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ sa samudrād amucyata sa mucyur abhavat taṃ vā etaṃ mucyuṃ santaṃ mṛtyur ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣas taṃ varuṇaṃ mṛtyum abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasya śrāntasya taptasya saṃtaptasya sarvebhyo 'ṅgebhyo raso 'kṣarat so 'ṅgaraso 'bhavat taṃ vā etaṃ aṅgarasaṃ santam aṅgirā ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ ||
meaning: ता या अमू रेतः समुद्रं वृत्वातिष्ठंस् ताः प्राच्यो दक्षिणाच्यः प्रतीच्य उदीच्यः समवद्रवन्त तद् यत् समवद्रवन्त तस्मात् समुद्र उच्यते ता भीता अब्रुवन् भगवन्तम् एव वयं राजानं वृणीमह इति यच् च वृत्वातिष्ठंस् तद् वरणो ऽभवत् तं वा एतं वरणं सन्तं वरुण इत्य् आचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवा भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षद्विषः स समुद्राद् अमुच्यत स मुच्युर् अभवत् तं वा एतं मुच्युं सन्तं मृत्युर् इत्य् आचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवा भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षद्विषस् तं वरुणं मृत्युम् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तस्य श्रान्तस्य तप्तस्य संतप्तस्य सर्वेभ्यो ऽङ्गेभ्यो रसो ऽक्षरत् सो ऽङ्गरसो ऽभवत् तं वा एतं अङ्गरसं सन्तम् अङ्गिरा इत्य् आचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवा भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षद्विषः ||
text_mt:
Those [waters] which surrounded that ocean of semen stood; they flowed together from the east, from the south, from the west, [and] from the north.
Because they flowed together (samavadravanta), therefore it is called an ocean (samudra).
They, frightened, said:
'We choose (vṛṇīmahe) the venerable one as king.'
And because they stood surrounding (vṛtvā), that became Varaṇa.
Being this Varaṇa, they speak of him cryptically as Varuṇa.
For the gods love the cryptic, as it were, and hate the direct.
He was released (amucyata) from the ocean.
He became Mucyu.
Being this Mucyu, they speak of him cryptically as Mṛtyu.
For the gods love the cryptic, as it were, and hate the direct.
He toiled over that Varuṇa-Mṛtyu, he generated heat over him, he thoroughly heated him.
As he was toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, sap (rasa) flowed from all his limbs (aṅga).
It became limb-sap (aṅgarasa).
Being this aṅgarasa, they speak of him cryptically as Aṅgiras.
For the gods love the cryptic, as it were, and hate the direct. || 7

sanskrit_iast: tam aṅgirasam ṛṣim abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād viṃśino 'ṅgirasa ṛṣīn niramimīta tān viṃśino 'ṅgirasa ṛṣīn abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo daśatayān āṅgirasān ārṣeyān niramimīta ṣoḍaśino 'ṣṭādaśino dvādaśina ekarcān dvyṛcāṃs tṛcāṃś caturṛcān pañcarcān ṣaḍarcān saptarcān iti tān aṅgirasa ṛṣīn āṅgirasāṃś cārṣeyān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo yān mantrān apaśyat sa āṅgiraso vedo 'bhavat tām āṅgirasaṃ vedam abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptāj janad iti dvaitam akṣaraṃ vyabhavat sa ya icchet sarvair etair aṅgirobhiś cāṅgirasaiś ca kurvīyety etayaiva tan mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitair aṅgirobhiś cāṅgirasaiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute ||
meaning: तम् अङ्गिरसम् ऋषिम् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तस्माच् छ्रान्तात् तप्तात् संतप्ताद् विंशिनो ऽङ्गिरस ऋषीन् निरमिमीत तान् विंशिनो ऽङ्गिरस ऋषीन् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यो दशतयान् आङ्गिरसान् आर्षेयान् निरमिमीत षोडशिनो ऽष्टादशिनो द्वादशिन एकर्चान् द्व्यृचांस् तृचांश् चतुरृचान् पञ्चर्चान् षडर्चान् सप्तर्चान् इति तान् अङ्गिरस ऋषीन् आङ्गिरसांश् चार्षेयान् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यो यान् मन्त्रान् अपश्यत् स आङ्गिरसो वेदो ऽभवत् ताम् आङ्गिरसं वेदम् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तस्माच् छ्रान्तात् तप्तात् संतप्ताज् जनद् इति द्वैतम् अक्षरं व्यभवत् स य इच्छेत् सर्वैर् एतैर् अङ्गिरोभिश् चाङ्गिरसैश् च कुर्वीयेत्य् एतयैव तन् महाव्याहृत्या कुर्वीत सर्वैर् ह वा अस्यैतैर् अङ्गिरोभिश् चाङ्गिरसैश् च कृतं भवति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् एवम् एतया महाव्याहृत्या कुरुते ||
text_mt:
He toiled over that sage Aṅgiras, he generated heat over him, he thoroughly heated him.
From him, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created the twenty-fold Aṅgiras sages.
He toiled over those twenty-fold Aṅgiras sages, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created the ten-fold Āṅgirasa descendants of sages: the sixteen-fold, the eighteen-fold, the twelve-fold, the one-verse, two-verse, three-verse, four-verse, five-verse, six-verse, [and] seven-verse ones.
He toiled over those Aṅgiras sages and Āṅgirasa descendants of sages, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, the mantras which he saw became the Āṅgirasa Veda.
He toiled over that Āṅgirasa Veda, he generated heat over it, he thoroughly heated it.
From it, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, the dual syllable janat arose.
If one wishes, 'May I perform with all these Aṅgirases and Āṅgirasas,' one should perform it with just this great sacred utterance.
It is performed for him with all these Aṅgirases and Āṅgirasas, whoever knows this and, knowing thus, performs thus with this great sacred utterance. || 8

sanskrit_iast: sa ūrdhvo 'tiṣṭhat sa imāṃl lokān vyaṣṭabhnāt tasmād aṅgiraso 'dhīyāna ūrdhvas tiṣṭhati tad vrataṃ sa manasā dhyāyed yad vā ahaṃ kiṃ ca manasā dhyāsyāmi tathaiva tad bhaviṣyati tad dha sma tathaiva bhavati tad apy etad ṛcoktam śreṣṭho ha vedas tapaso 'dhi jāto brahmajyānāṃ kṣitaye saṃbabhūva | ṛjyad bhūtaṃ yad asṛjyatedaṃ niveśanam anṛṇaṃ dūram asyeti tā vā etā aṅgirasāṃ jāmayo yan menayaḥ karoti menibhir vīryaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: स ऊर्ध्वो ऽतिष्ठत् स इमांल् लोकान् व्यष्टभ्नात् तस्माद् अङ्गिरसो ऽधीयान ऊर्ध्वस् तिष्ठति तद् व्रतं स मनसा ध्यायेद् यद् वा अहं किं च मनसा ध्यास्यामि तथैव तद् भविष्यति तद् ध स्म तथैव भवति तद् अप्य् एतद् ऋचोक्तम् श्रेष्ठो ह वेदस् तपसो ऽधि जातो ब्रह्मज्यानां क्षितये संबभूव | ऋज्यद् भूतं यद् असृज्यतेदं निवेशनम् अनृणं दूरम् अस्येति ता वा एता अङ्गिरसां जामयो यन् मेनयः करोति मेनिभिर् वीर्यं य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
He stood upright.
He propped up these worlds.
Therefore an Aṅgiras studying stands upright.
He should contemplate that observance with his mind: 'Whatever I shall contemplate with my mind, just so shall it be.'
And it indeed turns out just so.
This too has been spoken in a verse: / 'The supreme Veda, born from ascetic heat, came into being for the destruction of the oppressors of Brahmans. / When this being which is to be stretched out was created, this dwelling became free from debt, far away.' / These indeed are the sisters of the Aṅgirases, which are the missive weapons (menī).
He performs heroic deed with missive weapons who knows this. || 9

sanskrit_iast: sa diśo 'nvaikṣata prācīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ pratīcīm udīcīṃ dhruvām ūrdhvām iti tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tābhyaḥ śrāntābhyas taptābhyaḥ saṃtaptābhyaḥ pañca vedān niramimīta sarpavedaṃ piśācavedam asuravedam itihāsavedaṃ purāṇavedam iti sa khalu prācyā eva diśaḥ sarpavedaṃ niramimīta dakṣiṇasyāḥ piśācavedam pratīcyā asuravedam udīcyā itihāsavedam dhruvāyāś cordhvāyāś ca purāṇavedam sa tān pañca vedān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyaḥ pañca mahāvyāhṛtīr niramimīta vṛdhat karad ruhan mahat tad iti vṛdhad iti sarpavedāt karad iti piśācavedāt ruhad ity asuravedāt mahad itītihāsavedāt tad iti purāṇavedāt sa ya icchet sarvair etaiḥ pañcabhir vedaiḥ kurvīyety etābhir eva tan mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitaiḥ pañcabhir vedaiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etābhir mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurute ||
meaning: स दिशो ऽन्वैक्षत प्राचीं दक्षिणां प्रतीचीम् उदीचीं ध्रुवाम् ऊर्ध्वाम् इति तास् तत्रैवाभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् ताभ्यः श्रान्ताभ्यस् तप्ताभ्यः संतप्ताभ्यः पञ्च वेदान् निरमिमीत सर्पवेदं पिशाचवेदम् असुरवेदम् इतिहासवेदं पुराणवेदम् इति स खलु प्राच्या एव दिशः सर्पवेदं निरमिमीत दक्षिणस्याः पिशाचवेदम् प्रतीच्या असुरवेदम् उदीच्या इतिहासवेदम् ध्रुवायाश् चोर्ध्वायाश् च पुराणवेदम् स तान् पञ्च वेदान् अभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् तेभ्यः श्रान्तेभ्यस् तप्तेभ्यः संतप्तेभ्यः पञ्च महाव्याहृतीर् निरमिमीत वृधत् करद् रुहन् महत् तद् इति वृधद् इति सर्पवेदात् करद् इति पिशाचवेदात् रुहद् इत्य् असुरवेदात् महद् इतीतिहासवेदात् तद् इति पुराणवेदात् स य इच्छेत् सर्वैर् एतैः पञ्चभिर् वेदैः कुर्वीयेत्य् एताभिर् एव तन् महाव्याहृतिभिः कुर्वीत सर्वैर् ह वा अस्यैतैः पञ्चभिर् वेदैः कृतं भवति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् एवम् एताभिर् महाव्याहृतिभिः कुरुते ||
text_mt:
He looked towards the directions: the east, the south, the west, the north, the fixed [below], and the upward [direction].
He toiled over them right there, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created five Vedas:
the serpent Veda (Sarpaveda), the goblin Veda (Piśācaveda), the demon Veda (Asuraveda), the narrative Veda (Itihāsaveda), and the antiquity Veda (Purāṇaveda).
From the eastern direction indeed he created the Sarpaveda;
from the southern, the Piśācaveda;
from the western, the Asuraveda;
from the northern, the Itihāsaveda;
and from the fixed and upward [directions], the Purāṇaveda.
He toiled over those five Vedas, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created five great sacred utterances:
vṛdhat, karat, ruhat, mahat, tat.
vṛdhat from the Sarpaveda,
karat from the Piśācaveda,
ruhat from the Asuraveda,
mahat from the Itihāsaveda,
tat from the Purāṇaveda.
If one wishes, 'May I perform with all these five Vedas,' one should perform it with just these great sacred utterances.
It is performed for him with all these five Vedas, whoever knows this and, knowing thus, performs thus with these great sacred utterances. || 10

sanskrit_iast: sa āvataś ca parāvataś cānvaikṣata tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tābhyaḥ śrāntābhyas taptābhyaḥ saṃtaptābhyaḥ śam ity ūrdhvam akṣaram udakrāmat sa ya icchet sarvābhir etābhir āvadbhiś ca parāvadbhiś ca kurvīyety etayaivā tan mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta sarvābhir ha vā asyaitābhir āvadbhiś ca parāvadbhiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute ||
meaning: स आवतश् च परावतश् चान्वैक्षत तास् तत्रैवाभ्यश्राम्यद् अभ्यतपत् समतपत् ताभ्यः श्रान्ताभ्यस् तप्ताभ्यः संतप्ताभ्यः शम् इत्य् ऊर्ध्वम् अक्षरम् उदक्रामत् स य इच्छेत् सर्वाभिर् एताभिर् आवद्भिश् च परावद्भिश् च कुर्वीयेत्य् एतयैवा तन् महाव्याहृत्या कुर्वीत सर्वाभिर् ह वा अस्यैताभिर् आवद्भिश् च परावद्भिश् च कृतं भवति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् एवम् एतया महाव्याहृत्या कुरुते ||
text_mt:
He looked towards the near regions and the far regions.
He toiled over them right there, he generated heat over them, he thoroughly heated them.
From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, the upward syllable śam arose.
If one wishes, 'May I perform with all these near regions and far regions,' one should perform it with just this great sacred utterance.
It is performed for him with all these near regions and far regions, whoever knows this and, knowing thus, performs thus with this great sacred utterance. || 11

sanskrit_iast: sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyad bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat sa manasa eva candramasaṃ niramimīta nakhebhyo nakṣatrāṇi lomabhya oṣadhivanaspatīn kṣudrebhyaḥ prāṇebhyo 'nyān bahūn devān sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyad bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat sa etaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantum ekaviṃśatisaṃsthaṃ yajñam apaśyat tad apy etad ṛcoktam agnir yajñaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantum iti athāpy eṣa prākrīḍitaḥ ślokaḥ pratyabhivadati sapta sutyāḥ sapta ca pākayajñā iti ||
meaning: स भूयो ऽश्राम्यद् भूयो ऽतप्यद् भूय आत्मानं समतपत् स मनस एव चन्द्रमसं निरमिमीत नखेभ्यो नक्षत्राणि लोमभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतीन् क्षुद्रेभ्यः प्राणेभ्यो ऽन्यान् बहून् देवान् स भूयो ऽश्राम्यद् भूयो ऽतप्यद् भूय आत्मानं समतपत् स एतं त्रिवृतं सप्ततन्तुम् एकविंशतिसंस्थं यज्ञम् अपश्यत् तद् अप्य् एतद् ऋचोक्तम् अग्निर् यज्ञं त्रिवृतं सप्ततन्तुम् इति अथाप्य् एष प्राक्रीडितः श्लोकः प्रत्यभिवदति सप्त सुत्याः सप्त च पाकयज्ञा इति ||
text_mt: He toiled further, performed ascetic heat further, thoroughly heated himself further. / From his mind he fashioned the moon, / from his nails the constellations, / from his bodily hairs the plants and trees, / [and] from his minor vital breaths the many other gods. / He toiled further, performed ascetic heat further, thoroughly heated himself further. / He saw this threefold, seven-threaded sacrifice consisting of twenty-one forms. / This is also stated by a verse: / 'Agni [leads] the sacrifice, threefold, seven-threaded.' / And furthermore, this well-known verse refers to it: / 'Seven are the soma-pressings and seven the cooked sacrifices.'

sanskrit_iast: tam āharat tenāyajata tasyāgnir hotāsīt vāyur adhvaryuḥ sūrya udgātā candramā brahmā parjanyaḥ sadasyaḥ oṣadhivanaspatayaś camasādhvaryavaḥ viśve devā hotrakāḥ atharvāṅgiraso goptāras taṃ ha smaitam evaṃvidvāṃsaḥ pūrve śrotriyā yajñaṃ tataṃ sāvasāya ha smāhety abhivrajanti mā no 'yaṃ gharma udyataḥ pramattānām amṛtāḥ prajāḥ pradhākṣīd iti tān vā etān parirakṣakānt sadaḥprasarpakān ity ācakṣate dakṣiṇāsamṛddhān tad u ha smāha prajāpatiḥ yad vai yajñe 'kuśalā ṛtvijo bhavanty acaritino brahmacaryam aparāgyā vā tad vai yajñasya viriṣṭam ity ācakṣate yajñasya viriṣṭam anu yajamāno viriṣyate yajamānasya viriṣṭam anv ṛtvijo viriṣyante ṛtvijāṃ viriṣṭam anu dakṣiṇā viriṣyante dakṣiṇānāṃ viriṣṭam anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir viriṣyate putrapaśūnāṃ viriṣṭam anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokena viriṣyate svargasya lokasya viriṣṭam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo virisyate yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: तम् आहरत् तेनायजत तस्याग्निर् होतासीत् वायुर् अध्वर्युः सूर्य उद्गाता चन्द्रमा ब्रह्मा पर्जन्यः सदस्यः ओषधिवनस्पतयश् चमसाध्वर्यवः विश्वे देवा होत्रकाः अथर्वाङ्गिरसो गोप्तारस् तं ह स्मैतम् एवंविद्वांसः पूर्वे श्रोत्रिया यज्ञं ततं सावसाय ह स्माहेत्य् अभिव्रजन्ति मा नो ऽयं घर्म उद्यतः प्रमत्तानाम् अमृताः प्रजाः प्रधाक्षीद् इति तान् वा एतान् परिरक्षकान्त् सदःप्रसर्पकान् इत्य् आचक्षते दक्षिणासमृद्धान् तद् उ ह स्माह प्रजापतिः यद् वै यज्ञे ऽकुशला ऋत्विजो भवन्त्य् अचरितिनो ब्रह्मचर्यम् अपराग्या वा तद् वै यज्ञस्य विरिष्टम् इत्य् आचक्षते यज्ञस्य विरिष्टम् अनु यजमानो विरिष्यते यजमानस्य विरिष्टम् अन्व् ऋत्विजो विरिष्यन्ते ऋत्विजां विरिष्टम् अनु दक्षिणा विरिष्यन्ते दक्षिणानां विरिष्टम् अनु यजमानः पुत्रपशुभिर् विरिष्यते पुत्रपशूनां विरिष्टम् अनु यजमानः स्वर्गेण लोकेन विरिष्यते स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य विरिष्टम् अनु तस्यार्धस्य योगक्षेमो विरिस्यते यस्मिन्न् अर्धे यजन्त इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt: He brought it. / He sacrificed with it. / Of it, Agni was the Hotṛ priest; / Vāyu, the Adhvaryu priest; / Sūrya, the Udgātṛ priest; / the Moon, the brahman priest; / Parjanya, the Sadasya priest; / plants and trees, the Camasādhvaryu priests; / the All-Gods, the subordinate Hotṛ priests; / [and] the Atharvāṅgirases were the protectors. / Having known this thus, the ancient learned Brahmins used to approach that extended sacrifice having resolved: / 'May this offered hot milk draft not burn the immortal progeny of us who are heedless.' / Truly they call these [priests] the protectors, who glide into the assembly, rich in sacrificial fees. / And regarding this Prajāpati said: / 'Indeed, when in a sacrifice the officiating priests are unskilful, have not observed Vedic studentship, or are incompetent, / that indeed they call a flaw of the sacrifice. / Following a flaw of the sacrifice, the sacrificer is injured; / following the injury of the sacrificer, the officiating priests are injured; / following the injury of the officiating priests, the sacrificial fees are injured; / following the injury of the sacrificial fees, the sacrificer is injured in his sons and cattle; / following the injury of his sons and cattle, the sacrificer is injured in the heavenly world; / following the injury of the heavenly world, the welfare and security of that region in which they sacrifice is injured.' Thus the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ ha smaitam evaṃvidvāṃsaṃ brahmāṇaṃ yajñaviriṣṭī vā yajñaviriṣṭino vety upādhāveran namas te astu bhagavan yajñasya no viriṣṭaṃ sandhehīti tad yatraiva viriṣṭaṃ syāt tatrāgnīn upasamādhāya śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā pṛthivyai śrotrāyeti trir evāgnīnt samprokṣati triḥ paryukṣati triḥ kārayamānam ācāmayati ca saṃprokṣati ca yajñavāstu va samprokṣati athāpi vedānāṃ rasena yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ sandhīyate tad yathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ saṃdadhyāt suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena lohaṃ lohena sīsaṃ sīsena trapv evam evāsya yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhīyate yajñasya saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ saṃdhīyate yajamānasya saṃdhitim anv ṛtvijaḥ saṃdhīyante ṛtvijāṃ saṃdhitim anu dakṣiṇāḥ saṃdhīyante dakṣiṇānāṃ saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhiḥ saṃdhīyate putrapaśūnāṃ saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokena saṃdhīyate svargasya lokasya saṃdhitim anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemaḥ saṃdhīyate yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: तं ह स्मैतम् एवंविद्वांसं ब्रह्माणं यज्ञविरिष्टी वा यज्ञविरिष्टिनो वेत्य् उपाधावेरन् नमस् ते अस्तु भगवन् यज्ञस्य नो विरिष्टं सन्धेहीति तद् यत्रैव विरिष्टं स्यात् तत्राग्नीन् उपसमाधाय शान्त्युदकं कृत्वा पृथिव्यै श्रोत्रायेति त्रिर् एवाग्नीन्त् सम्प्रोक्षति त्रिः पर्युक्षति त्रिः कारयमानम् आचामयति च संप्रोक्षति च यज्ञवास्तु व सम्प्रोक्षति अथापि वेदानां रसेन यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं सन्धीयते तद् यथा लवणेन सुवर्णं संदध्यात् सुवर्णेन रजतं रजतेन लोहं लोहेन सीसं सीसेन त्रप्व् एवम् एवास्य यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संधीयते यज्ञस्य संधितिम् अनु यजमानः संधीयते यजमानस्य संधितिम् अन्व् ऋत्विजः संधीयन्ते ऋत्विजां संधितिम् अनु दक्षिणाः संधीयन्ते दक्षिणानां संधितिम् अनु यजमानः पुत्रपशुभिः संधीयते पुत्रपशूनां संधितिम् अनु यजमानः स्वर्गेण लोकेन संधीयते स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य संधितिम् अनु तस्यार्धस्य योगक्षेमः संधीयते यस्मिन्न् अर्धे यजन्त इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt: Those who have suffered a flaw in sacrifice—or he who has suffered a flaw in sacrifice—should run to that brahman priest who knows thus: / 'Homage be to you, venerable sir! / Heal the flaw of our sacrifice!' / Then wherever there should be a flaw, having added fuel to the fires there [and] having prepared pacification water, saying, 'For the earth, for the hearing,' he sprinkles the fires three times, sprinkles around [them] three times; / he has the sacrificer sip water three times and sprinkles him three times; / and he sprinkles the sacrificial ground. / Furthermore, the flaw of the sacrifice is healed by the essence of the Vedas. / Just as one would join gold with borax, silver with gold, copper with silver, lead with copper, tin with lead, exactly so is the flaw of this sacrifice healed. / Following the healing of the sacrifice, the sacrificer is healed; / following the healing of the sacrificer, the officiating priests are healed; / following the healing of the officiating priests, the sacrificial fees are healed; / following the healing of the sacrificial fees, the sacrificer is healed in his sons and cattle; / following the healing of his sons and cattle, the sacrificer is healed in the heavenly world; / following the healing of the heavenly world, the welfare and security of that region in which they sacrifice is healed. Thus the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha smāhātharvā devo vijānan yajñaviriṣṭānandānīty upaśamayeran yajñe prāyaścittiḥ kriyate 'pi ca yad u bahv iva yajñe vilomaṃ kriyate na caivāsya kā canārtir bhavati na ca yajñaviṣkandham upayāty apahanti punarmṛtyum apātyeti punārājātiṃ kāmacāro 'sya sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān brahmā bhavati yasya caivaṃvidvān brahmā dakṣiṇataḥ sado 'dhyāste yasya caivaṃvidvān brahmā dakṣiṇata udaṅmukha āsīno yajña ājyāhutīr juhotīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: तद् उ ह स्माहाथर्वा देवो विजानन् यज्ञविरिष्टानन्दानीत्य् उपशमयेरन् यज्ञे प्रायश्चित्तिः क्रियते ऽपि च यद् उ बह्व् इव यज्ञे विलोमं क्रियते न चैवास्य का चनार्तिर् भवति न च यज्ञविष्कन्धम् उपयात्य् अपहन्ति पुनर्मृत्युम् अपात्येति पुनाराजातिं कामचारो ऽस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् ब्रह्मा भवति यस्य चैवंविद्वान् ब्रह्मा दक्षिणतः सदो ऽध्यास्ते यस्य चैवंविद्वान् ब्रह्मा दक्षिणत उदङ्मुख आसीनो यज्ञ आज्याहुतीर् जुहोतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt: And on this Atharvan the god, knowing, said: 'May they appease the afflictions [and] flaws of the sacrifice.' A prāyaścitta is performed in the sacrifice, and also whatever is done contrary in the sacrifice, as it were, no affliction whatsoever befalls him, nor does he fall into sacrificial obstruction; he strikes away repeated death, he escapes rebirth; his free movement shines in all worlds—for him who knows thus, and who, knowing thus, becomes the brahman priest, and for him to whose right a brahman priest knowing thus sits presiding over the sadas, and for him to whose right a brahman priest knowing thus, seated facing north, offers the butter offerings in the sacrifice. Thus says the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: brahma ha vai brahmāṇaṃ puṣkare sasṛje sa khalu brahmā sṛṣṭaś cintām āpede kenāham ekenākṣareṇa sarvāṃś ca kāmānt sarvāṃś ca lokānt sarvāṃś ca devānt sarvāṃś ca vedānt sarvāṃś ca yajñānt sarvāṃś ca śabdānt sarvāś ca vyuṣṭīḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamāny anubhaveyam iti sa brahmacaryam acarat sa om ity etad akṣaram apaśyad dvivarṇaṃ caturmātraṃ sarvavyāpi sarvavibhvayātayāmabrahma brāhmīṃ vyāhṛtiṃ brahmadaivatām tayā sarvāṃś ca kāmānt sarvāṃś ca lokānt sarvāṃś ca devānt sarvāṃś ca vedānt sarvāṃś ca yajñānt sarvāṃś ca śabdānt sarvāś ca vyuṣṭīḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamāny anvabhavat tasya prathamena varṇenāpaḥ snehaṃ cānvabhavat tasya dvitīyena varṇena tejo jyotīṃṣy anvabhavat ||
meaning: ब्रह्म ह वै ब्रह्माणं पुष्करे ससृजे स खलु ब्रह्मा सृष्टश् चिन्ताम् आपेदे केनाहम् एकेनाक्षरेण सर्वांश् च कामान्त् सर्वांश् च लोकान्त् सर्वांश् च देवान्त् सर्वांश् च वेदान्त् सर्वांश् च यज्ञान्त् सर्वांश् च शब्दान्त् सर्वाश् च व्युष्टीः सर्वाणि च भूतानि स्थावरजङ्गमान्य् अनुभवेयम् इति स ब्रह्मचर्यम् अचरत् स ओम् इत्य् एतद् अक्षरम् अपश्यद् द्विवर्णं चतुर्मात्रं सर्वव्यापि सर्वविभ्वयातयामब्रह्म ब्राह्मीं व्याहृतिं ब्रह्मदैवताम् तया सर्वांश् च कामान्त् सर्वांश् च लोकान्त् सर्वांश् च देवान्त् सर्वांश् च वेदान्त् सर्वांश् च यज्ञान्त् सर्वांश् च शब्दान्त् सर्वाश् च व्युष्टीः सर्वाणि च भूतानि स्थावरजङ्गमान्य् अन्वभवत् तस्य प्रथमेन वर्णेनापः स्नेहं चान्वभवत् तस्य द्वितीयेन वर्णेन तेजो ज्योतींष्य् अन्वभवत् ||
text_mt: Brahman indeed created Brahmā on a lotus. / Being created, that Brahmā fell to thinking: / 'Through what single syllable might I experience all desires, all worlds, all gods, all Vedas, all sacrifices, all sounds, all dawnings, and all beings, stationary and moving?' / He practiced Vedic studentship. / He saw this syllable 'Oṃ', having two sounds, four morae, all-pervading, all-powerful, the unexhausted Brahman, the sacred utterance belonging to Brahman, having Brahman as deity. / Through it he experienced all desires, all worlds, all gods, all Vedas, all sacrifices, all sounds, all dawnings, and all beings, stationary and moving. / Through its first sound he experienced the waters and moisture. / Through its second sound he experienced heat and lights.

sanskrit_iast: tasya prathamayā svaramātrayā pṛthivīm agnim oṣadhivanaspatīn ṛgvedaṃ bhūr iti vyāhṛtiṃ gāyatraṃ chandas trivṛtaṃ stomaṃ prācīṃ diśaṃ vasantam ṛtuṃ vācam adhyātmaṃ jihvāṃ rasam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat ||
meaning: तस्य प्रथमया स्वरमात्रया पृथिवीम् अग्निम् ओषधिवनस्पतीन् ऋग्वेदं भूर् इति व्याहृतिं गायत्रं छन्दस् त्रिवृतं स्तोमं प्राचीं दिशं वसन्तम् ऋतुं वाचम् अध्यात्मं जिह्वां रसम् इतीन्द्रियाण्य् अन्वभवत् ||
text_mt: Through its first vowel-mora he experienced the earth, Agni, plants and trees, the Ṛgveda, the sacred utterance 'bhūḥ', the gāyatrī metre, the threefold chant, the eastern direction, the spring season, speech in relation to the self, [and] the tongue and taste as sense-faculties.

sanskrit_iast: tasya dvitīyayā svaramātrayāntarikṣaṃ vāyuṃ yajurvedaṃ bhuva iti vyāhṛtiṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ chandaḥ pañcadaśaṃ stomaṃ pratīcīṃ diśaṃ grīṣmam ṛtuṃ prāṇam adhyātmaṃ nāsike gandhaghrāṇam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat ||
meaning: तस्य द्वितीयया स्वरमात्रयान्तरिक्षं वायुं यजुर्वेदं भुव इति व्याहृतिं त्रैष्टुभं छन्दः पञ्चदशं स्तोमं प्रतीचीं दिशं ग्रीष्मम् ऋतुं प्राणम् अध्यात्मं नासिके गन्धघ्राणम् इतीन्द्रियाण्य् अन्वभवत् ||
text_mt: Through its second vowel-mora he experienced the intermediate space, Vāyu, the Yajurveda, the sacred utterance 'bhuvaḥ', the triṣṭubh metre, the fifteenfold chant, the western direction, the summer season, the breath in relation to the self, [and] the nostrils and smelling of odour as sense-faculties.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tṛtīyayā svaramātrayā divam ādityaṃ sāmavedaṃ svar iti vyāhṛtiṃ jāgataṃ chandaḥ saptadaśaṃ stomam udīcīṃ diśaṃ varṣā ṛtuṃ jyotir adhyātmaṃ cakṣuṣī darśanam itīndriyāny anvabhavat ||
meaning: तस्य तृतीयया स्वरमात्रया दिवम् आदित्यं सामवेदं स्वर् इति व्याहृतिं जागतं छन्दः सप्तदशं स्तोमम् उदीचीं दिशं वर्षा ऋतुं ज्योतिर् अध्यात्मं चक्षुषी दर्शनम् इतीन्द्रियान्य् अन्वभवत् ||
text_mt: Through its third vowel-mora he experienced heaven, Āditya, the Sāmaveda, the sacred utterance 'svaḥ', the jagatī metre, the seventeenfold chant, the northern direction, the rainy season, light in relation to the self, [and] the two eyes and seeing as sense-faculties.

sanskrit_iast: tasya vakāramātrayāpaś candramasam atharvavedaṃ nakṣatrāṇy om iti svam ātmānaṃ janad ity aṅgirasām ānuṣṭubhaṃ chanda ekaviṃśaṃ stomaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ śaradam ṛtuṃ mano 'dhyātmaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat ||
meaning: तस्य वकारमात्रयापश् चन्द्रमसम् अथर्ववेदं नक्षत्राण्य् ओम् इति स्वम् आत्मानं जनद् इत्य् अङ्गिरसाम् आनुष्टुभं छन्द एकविंशं स्तोमं दक्षिणां दिशं शरदम् ऋतुं मनो ऽध्यात्मं ज्ञानं ज्ञेयम् इतीन्द्रियाण्य् अन्वभवत् ||
text_mt: Through its mora of the consonant [m] he experienced the waters, the moon, the Atharvaveda, the constellations, his own self as 'Oṃ', the [sacred utterance] 'janat' belonging to the Aṅgirases, the anuṣṭubh metre, the twenty-onefold chant, the southern direction, the autumn season, the mind in relation to the self, [and] knowledge and the knowable as sense-faculties.

text_mt: Through the sound of its letter M, it pervaded itihāsa and purāṇa, dialogue, gāthās, praise of men, the Upaniṣads, instructions; the sacred utterances 'vṛdhat, karad, ruhan, mahat, tat, śam, om'; strings and assorted lyres; notes, dance, song, and instruments; the deity Caitraratha, the lightning light, the bārhata metre, the twenty-seven-fold and thirty-three-fold stomāḥ, the firm zenith direction, the cold and dewy seasons, hearing as the presiding principle over the self, and the sense faculties consisting of the hearing of sounds.

text_mt: This single-syllabled verse appeared at the beginning of the ascetic heat of Brahman, the bright essence of the Atharvan Brahmaveda. From it alone the mantras appeared. Indeed, whatever in the mantras he makes deficient, flawed, and stale through lack of ascetic heat, failure to serve, and studying on days unfit for study, that he should replenish through the splendour of the Atharvans. 'And may the mantras turn their faces to me, like embryos desiring to turn toward their mother'—he employs the syllable Oṃ at the beginning. He should replenish it with this very verse. This very [verse] is employed at the front of the sacrifice; this is at the rear; through it the sacrifice is extended on every side. And so this has been stated by a verse: 'That which is employed at the front: "In the imperishable syllable of the verse, in highest heaven..."' Therefore, whatever desire a brahmin might wish, having fasted for three nights, facing east, with speech restrained, having sat upon the sacred grass, he should repeat this syllable a thousand times. His purposes and all his undertakings succeed. Thus says the Brāhmaṇa.

text_mt: The city of Indra belonged to the streams of Vasu. The asuras besieged it. The gods were afraid: 'Who will slay these asuras?' They saw the syllable Oṃ, the eldest son of Brahman. They said to him: 'With you as our leader, let us conquer these asuras.' He said: 'What will be my return-reward?' 'Choose a boon,' [they said]. 'I choose,' [he said]. He chose a boon: 'Let not brāhmaṇas utter the sacred word without first uttering me; if they should utter it, it would be non-sacred.' 'So be it,' [they said]. Those gods were engaged in battle with the asuras on the northern half of the sacrificial ground. By means of the syllable Oṃ, the gods repelled the asuras from the Āgnīdhra hearth. In that they repelled them, therefore the syllable Oṃ is spoken first. He who does not know this syllable Oṃ would be powerless, but he who knows thus would have mastery over Brahman. Therefore the syllable Oṃ becomes a verse in a verse, a formula in a formula, a chant in a chant, a rule in a rule,

text_mt:
a praṇava in a praṇava: so says the Brāhmaṇa.

We ask about the syllable Oṃ: What is the verbal root? What is the nominal base? What is the noun or verb? What is the gender? What is the number? What is the case-ending? What is the suffix? What is the accent, prefix, particle? What indeed is the grammar? What is the phonetic modification? What is the subject of modification? Of how many morae is it? Of how many sounds? Of how many syllables? Of how many words? What is the conjunct? What is the place of articulation, internal effort, and external effort that learners pronounce? What is the metre? What is the colour? These are the prior questions. Then the subsequent ones: The mantra, the ritual manual, the brāhmaṇa, the ṛg, the yajus, the sāman—why do those who discourse on Brahman place the syllable Oṃ at the beginning?

three groups of twelve among the prior and subsequent ones.

By these we shall explain the syllable Oṃ.

Indra asked Prajāpati: 'Lord, having praised [you], I ask.' 'Ask, my child,' he said. 'What is this syllable Oṃ? Whose son is it? What is its metre? What is its colour? And how does a brahman priest become Brahman through it?' Therefore indeed, as auspicious, he took hold of the syllable Oṃ first. In the Ṛgveda, the syllable Oṃ is monosyllabic, with circumflex and acute accent. In the Yajurveda, the syllable Oṃ is monosyllabic, with threefold accent and acute. In the Sāmaveda, the syllable Oṃ is monosyllabic, with prolated long acute. In the Atharvaveda, the syllable Oṃ is monosyllabic, with short acute. With acute upon acute, having two parts, a and u, three and a half morae, with the consonant in the letter m, so they say. That which is the first mora has Brahman as its deity and is red in colour; he who constantly meditates on it would go to the state of Brahman. That which is the second mora has Viṣṇu as its deity and is black in colour; he who constantly meditates on it would go to the state of Viṣṇu. That which is the third mora has Īśāna as its deity and is tawny in colour; he who constantly meditates on it would go to the state of Īśāna. That which is the half-fourth mora has all deities as its deity, having become manifest, moves through space, resembling pure crystal in colour; he who constantly meditates on it would go to the nameless state. And the origin of the syllable Oṃ—

the learned priest who does not know it requires re-initiation.

Therefore the utterance of the Brāhmaṇa is to be respected, just as a descendant of the Lātavya lineage is a son of Brahman.

sanskrit_iast: ko dhātur iti āpṛdhātuḥ avatim apy eke rūpasāmānyād arthasāmānyaṃ nedīyas tasmād āper oṃkāraḥ sarvam āpnotīty arthaḥ kṛdantam arthavat prātipadikam adarśanam pratyayasya nāma saṃpadyate nipāteṣu cainaṃ vaiyākaraṇā udāttaṃ samāmananti tad avyayībhūtam anvarthavācī śabdo na vyeti kadā caneti sadṛśaṃ triṣu liṅgeṣu sarvāsu va vibhaktiṣu vacaneṣu ca sarveṣu yan na vyeti tad avyayam ko vikārī cyavate prasāraṇam āpnoter ākarapakārau vikāryau ādita oṃkāro vikriyate dvitīyo makāraḥ eva dvivarṇa ekākṣara om ity oṃkāro nirvṛttaḥ ||
meaning: को धातुर् इति आपृधातुः अवतिम् अप्य् एके रूपसामान्याद् अर्थसामान्यं नेदीयस् तस्माद् आपेर् ओंकारः सर्वम् आप्नोतीत्य् अर्थः कृदन्तम् अर्थवत् प्रातिपदिकम् अदर्शनम् प्रत्ययस्य नाम संपद्यते निपातेषु चैनं वैयाकरणा उदात्तं समामनन्ति तद् अव्ययीभूतम् अन्वर्थवाची शब्दो न व्येति कदा चनेति सदृशं त्रिषु लिङ्गेषु सर्वासु व विभक्तिषु वचनेषु च सर्वेषु यन् न व्येति तद् अव्ययम् को विकारी च्यवते प्रसारणम् आप्नोतेर् आकरपकारौ विकार्यौ आदित ओंकारो विक्रियते द्वितीयो मकारः एव द्विवर्ण एकाक्षर ओम् इत्य् ओंकारो निर्वृत्तः ||
text_mt:
As to "What is the verbal root?":
The verbal root is āp-.
Some [say] av- as well.
Due to similarity of form, similarity of meaning is closer.
Therefore, from āp- [comes] the sound Oṃ; "it obtains (āpnoti) everything" is the meaning, an agent noun ending in a kṛt suffix possessing meaning.
The nominal base is not visibly formed [by a standard nominal suffix].
The name of the suffix comes to be, and grammarians recite it with the acute accent among the particles; therefore it has become an indeclinable.
A word expressive of its literal sense never departs (na vyeti):
"That which remains identical in three genders, in all case-endings, and in all numbers, and does not alter, is an indeclinable (avyaya)."
What is the subject of modification that falls away?
Vowel-reduction.
The "ā" sound and "p" sound of āpnoti are the two subjects of modification.
From the beginning the sound "o" is modified;
the second is the sound "m".
Thus, consisting of two sounds and a single syllable, "om", the sound Oṃ is formed.

sanskrit_iast: katimātra iti ādes tisro mātrāḥ abhyādāne hi plavate makāraś caturthīm kiṃ sthānam iti ubhāv oṣṭhau sthānam nādānupradānakaraṇau ca dvisthānam saṃdhyakṣaram avarṇaleśaḥ kaṇṭhyo yathoktaśeṣaḥ pūrvo vivṛtakaraṇasthitaś ca dvitīyaspṛṣṭakaraṇasthitaś ca na saṃyogo vidyate ākhyātopasargānudāttasvaritaliṅgavibhaktivacanāni ca saṃsthānādhyāyina ācāryāḥ pūrve babhūvuḥ śravaṇād eva pratipadyante na kāraṇaṃ pṛcchanti athāparapakṣīyāṇāṃ kaviḥ pañcālacaṇḍaḥ paripṛcchako babhūvāṃbu pṛthagudgīthadoṣān bhavanto bruvantv iti tad vācy upalakṣayed varṇākṣarapadāṅkaśaḥ vibhaktyām ṛṣiniṣevitām iti vācaṃ stuvanti tasmāt kāraṇaṃ brūmaḥ varṇānām ayam idaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ṣaḍaṅgavidas tat tathādhīmahe kiṃ chanda iti gāyatraṃ hi chandaḥ gāyatrī vai devānām ekākṣarā śvetavarṇā ca vyākhyātā dvau dvādaśakau vargau etad vai vyākaraṇaṃ dhātvarthavacanaṃ śaikṣyaṃ chandovacanaṃ ca athottarau dvau dvādaśakau vargau vedarahasikī vyākhyātā mantraḥ kalpo brāhamaṇam ṛg yajuḥ sāmātharvāṇi eṣā vyāhṛtiś caturṇāṃ vedānām ānupūrveṇoṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti vyāhṛtayaḥ ||
meaning: कतिमात्र इति आदेस् तिस्रो मात्राः अभ्यादाने हि प्लवते मकारश् चतुर्थीम् किं स्थानम् इति उभाव् ओष्ठौ स्थानम् नादानुप्रदानकरणौ च द्विस्थानम् संध्यक्षरम् अवर्णलेशः कण्ठ्यो यथोक्तशेषः पूर्वो विवृतकरणस्थितश् च द्वितीयस्पृष्टकरणस्थितश् च न संयोगो विद्यते आख्यातोपसर्गानुदात्तस्वरितलिङ्गविभक्तिवचनानि च संस्थानाध्यायिन आचार्याः पूर्वे बभूवुः श्रवणाद् एव प्रतिपद्यन्ते न कारणं पृच्छन्ति अथापरपक्षीयाणां कविः पञ्चालचण्डः परिपृच्छको बभूवांबु पृथगुद्गीथदोषान् भवन्तो ब्रुवन्त्व् इति तद् वाच्य् उपलक्षयेद् वर्णाक्षरपदाङ्कशः विभक्त्याम् ऋषिनिषेविताम् इति वाचं स्तुवन्ति तस्मात् कारणं ब्रूमः वर्णानाम् अयम् इदं भविष्यतीति षडङ्गविदस् तत् तथाधीमहे किं छन्द इति गायत्रं हि छन्दः गायत्री वै देवानाम् एकाक्षरा श्वेतवर्णा च व्याख्याता द्वौ द्वादशकौ वर्गौ एतद् वै व्याकरणं धात्वर्थवचनं शैक्ष्यं छन्दोवचनं च अथोत्तरौ द्वौ द्वादशकौ वर्गौ वेदरहसिकी व्याख्याता मन्त्रः कल्पो ब्राहमणम् ऋग् यजुः सामाथर्वाणि एषा व्याहृतिश् चतुर्णां वेदानाम् आनुपूर्वेणों भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति व्याहृतयः ||
text_mt:
How many morae has it? / The beginning has three morae, / for at the initial utterance it is prolated; / and the m-sound forms the fourth. / What is its place of articulation? / Both lips are the place. / And having voice and emission as the effort, it has two places of articulation. / It is a diphthong; a trace of the a-sound is guttural, the remainder as stated; / the former element stands with open effort, / and the second stands with contact effort; / there is no consonant cluster. / The ancient teachers were students of the established forms of verbs, prefixes, unaccented and circumflex accents, genders, case endings, and numbers; / they understood solely by hearing and did not ask for the underlying cause. / Then, among those of the opposite side, the sage Pañcālacaṇḍa became an inquirer: 'Sirs, explain each defect of the udgītha.' / One should observe it in speech, according to sound, syllable, and word division; / they praise speech saying, '[Observe] it in grammatical division, frequented by the seers.' / Therefore we state the cause: / this will become this among the sounds. / Knowing the six auxiliary sciences of the Veda, we study it thus. / What is the metre? / The metre is indeed Gāyatrī. / For Gāyatrī is taught to the gods as monosyllabic and white in colour. / There are two groups of twelve.

This indeed is grammar, stating the meaning of the roots, phonetics, and the statement of metres.

Now the subsequent two groups of twelve are explained as the esoteric teaching of the Veda.

Mantra, ceremonial ritual, Brāhmaṇa, Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, Atharvaveda:

sanskrit_iast: asamīkṣyapravalhitāni śrūyante dvāparādāv ṛṣīṇām ekadeśo doṣapatir iha cintām āpede tribhiḥ somaḥ pātavyaḥ samāptam iva bhavati tasmād ṛgyajuḥsāmāny apakrāntatejāṃsy āsan tantra maharṣayaḥ paridevayāṃ cakrire mahac chokabhayaṃ prāptāḥ smaḥ na caitat sarvaiḥ samabhihitam te vayaṃ bhagavantam evopadhāvāma sarveṣām eva śarma bhavānīti te tathety uktvā tūṣṇīm atiṣṭhan nānupasannebhya iti upopasīdāmīti nīcair babhūvuḥ sa ebhya upanīya provāca māmikām eva vyāhṛtim ādita āditaḥ kṛṇudhvam iti evaṃ māmakā ādhīyante narte bhṛgvaṅgirovidbhyaḥ somaḥ pātavyaḥ ṛtvijaḥ parābhavanti yajamāno rajasāpadhvasyati śrutiś cāpadhvastā tiṣṭhatīti evam evottarottarād yogāt tokaṃ tokaṃ praśādhvam iti evaṃ pratāpo na parābhaviṣyatīti tathā ha tathā ha bhagavann iti pratipedira āpyāyayan te tathā vītaśokabhayā babhūvus tasmād brahmavādina oṃkāram āditaḥ kurvanti ||
meaning: असमीक्ष्यप्रवल्हितानि श्रूयन्ते द्वापरादाव् ऋषीणाम् एकदेशो दोषपतिर् इह चिन्ताम् आपेदे त्रिभिः सोमः पातव्यः समाप्तम् इव भवति तस्माद् ऋग्यजुःसामान्य् अपक्रान्ततेजांस्य् आसन् तन्त्र महर्षयः परिदेवयां चक्रिरे महच् छोकभयं प्राप्ताः स्मः न चैतत् सर्वैः समभिहितम् ते वयं भगवन्तम् एवोपधावाम सर्वेषाम् एव शर्म भवानीति ते तथेत्य् उक्त्वा तूष्णीम् अतिष्ठन् नानुपसन्नेभ्य इति उपोपसीदामीति नीचैर् बभूवुः स एभ्य उपनीय प्रोवाच मामिकाम् एव व्याहृतिम् आदित आदितः कृणुध्वम् इति एवं मामका आधीयन्ते नर्ते भृग्वङ्गिरोविद्भ्यः सोमः पातव्यः ऋत्विजः पराभवन्ति यजमानो रजसापध्वस्यति श्रुतिश् चापध्वस्ता तिष्ठतीति एवम् एवोत्तरोत्तराद् योगात् तोकं तोकं प्रशाध्वम् इति एवं प्रतापो न पराभविष्यतीति तथा ह तथा ह भगवन्न् इति प्रतिपेदिर आप्याययन् ते तथा वीतशोकभया बभूवुस् तस्माद् ब्रह्मवादिन ओंकारम् आदितः कुर्वन्ति ||
text_mt:
This is the sacred utterance of the four Vedas in successive order: Oṃ, bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ—these are the sacred utterances.

Enigmas are heard without examination.
At the beginning of the Dvāpara age, a certain group of ṛṣis, afflicted by defect, fell into anxiety here: "Soma is to be drunk by three [priests]; it is as if completed."
Therefore the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman verses had their splendour departed.
Thereupon the great ṛṣis lamented:
"We have met with great sorrow and fear;
and this has not been declared by all.
Let us hasten to the Lord himself,
[praying,] 'May you be protection for all!'"
Having said, "So be it," they stood silently.
[Thinking,] "Not for those who have not approached [as students],"
they bowed down, [saying,] "I approach as a student."
Having initiated them, he proclaimed to them:
"Place my own sacred utterance right at the beginning!
Thus mine are established. Soma is not to be drunk without those who know Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras.
The officiating priests are defeated;
the patron of the sacrifice falls into ruin through darkness;
and sacred tradition stands ruined.
Just in this way, instruct child after child through successive application!
Thus splendour will not perish."
Saying, "So be it, indeed so be it, O Lord!" they agreed, reinvigorating [themselves].
They thus became free from sorrow and fear.
Therefore the expounders of Brahman place the Oṃ-syllable at the beginning.

sanskrit_iast: kiṃ devatam iti ṛcām agnir devatam tad eva jyotiḥ gāyatraṃ chandaḥ pṛthivī sthānam agnim īḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devam ṛtvijaṃ hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvā ṛgvedam adhīyate yajuṣāṃ vāyur devatam tad eva jyotis traiṣṭubhaṃ chandaḥ antarikṣaṃ sthānam iṣe tvorje tvā vāyava stha devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatu śreṣṭhatamāya karmaṇe ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvā yajurvedam adhīyate sāmnām ādityo devatam tad eva jyotiḥ jāgataṃ chandaḥ dyauḥ sthānam agna ā yāhi vītaye gṛṇāno havyadātaye ni hotā satsi barhiṣi ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvā samāvedam adhīyate atharvaṇāṃ candramā devatam tad eva jyotiḥ sarvāṇi chandāṃsi āpaḥ sthānam śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaya ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvātharvavedam adhīyate adbhyaḥ sthāvarajaṅgamo bhūtagrāmaḥ saṃbhavati tasmāt sarvam āpomayaṃ bhūtaṃ sarvaṃ bhṛgvaṅgiromayam antaraite trayo vedā bhṛgūn aṅgirasaḥ śritā ity ab iti prakṛtir apām oṃkāreṇa ca etasmād vyāsaḥ purovāca bhṛgvaṅgirovidā saṃskṛto 'nyān vedān adhīyīta nānyatra saṃskṛto bhṛgṅgiraso 'dhīyīta sāmavede 'tha khilaśrutir brahmacaryeṇa caitasmād atharvāṅgiraso ha yo veda sa veda sarvam iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: किं देवतम् इति ऋचाम् अग्निर् देवतम् तद् एव ज्योतिः गायत्रं छन्दः पृथिवी स्थानम् अग्निम् ईऌए पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवम् ऋत्विजं होतारं रत्नधातमम् इत्य् एवम् आदिं कृत्वा ऋग्वेदम् अधीयते यजुषां वायुर् देवतम् तद् एव ज्योतिस् त्रैष्टुभं छन्दः अन्तरिक्षं स्थानम् इषे त्वोर्जे त्वा वायव स्थ देवो वः सविता प्रार्पयतु श्रेष्ठतमाय कर्मणे इत्य् एवम् आदिं कृत्वा यजुर्वेदम् अधीयते साम्नाम् आदित्यो देवतम् तद् एव ज्योतिः जागतं छन्दः द्यौः स्थानम् अग्न आ याहि वीतये गृणानो हव्यदातये नि होता सत्सि बर्हिषि इत्य् एवम् आदिं कृत्वा समावेदम् अधीयते अथर्वणां चन्द्रमा देवतम् तद् एव ज्योतिः सर्वाणि छन्दांसि आपः स्थानम् शं नो देवीर् अभिष्टय इत्य् एवम् आदिं कृत्वाथर्ववेदम् अधीयते अद्भ्यः स्थावरजङ्गमो भूतग्रामः संभवति तस्मात् सर्वम् आपोमयं भूतं सर्वं भृग्वङ्गिरोमयम् अन्तरैते त्रयो वेदा भृगून् अङ्गिरसः श्रिता इत्य् अब् इति प्रकृतिर् अपाम् ओंकारेण च एतस्माद् व्यासः पुरोवाच भृग्वङ्गिरोविदा संस्कृतो ऽन्यान् वेदान् अधीयीत नान्यत्र संस्कृतो भृग्ङ्गिरसो ऽधीयीत सामवेदे ऽथ खिलश्रुतिर् ब्रह्मचर्येण चैतस्माद् अथर्वाङ्गिरसो ह यो वेद स वेद सर्वम् इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
What is the deity? / Agni is the deity of the verses of the Ṛgveda; / that indeed is the light; / Gāyatrī is the metre; / earth is the place. / Making 'I praise Agni, the household priest, the divine minister of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ, the best bestower of treasures' the beginning, they study the Ṛgveda. / Vāyu is the deity of the Yajurveda formulas; / that indeed is the light; / Triṣṭubh is the metre; / intermediate space is the place. / Making 'For food, for strength thee; you are winds; may the divine Savitṛ impel you to the highest work' the beginning, they study the Yajurveda. / Āditya is the deity of the Sāmaveda chants; / that indeed is the light; / Jagatī is the metre; / heaven is the place. / Making 'Come, O Agni, to the feast, being praised for the giving of the offering; sit down as Hotṛ upon the sacred grass' the beginning, they study the Sāmaveda. / The Moon is the deity of the Atharvan hymns; / that indeed is the light; / all metres [are its metre]; / the waters are the place. / Making 'May the divine [waters] be for our welfare and help' the beginning, they study the Atharvaveda. / From the waters the aggregate of beings, stationary and moving, arises; / therefore every being consists of water, everything consists of Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras.

Within these, the three Vedas rest upon the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases; thus 'ap' is the fundamental nature of the waters, and through the syllable Oṃ.

Therefore Vyāsa formerly declared:

'Initiated by one who knows Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, he should study the other Vedas.

One initiated elsewhere should not study the [tradition of] Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras.'

meaning: अध्यात्मम् आत्मभैषज्यम् आत्मकैवल्यम् ओंकारः आत्मानं निरुध्य सङ्गममात्रीं भूतार्थचिन्तां चिन्तयेत् अतिक्रम्य वेदेभ्यः सर्वपरम् अध्यात्मफलं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः सवितर्कं ज्ञानमयम् इत्य् एतैः प्रश्नैः प्रतिवचनैश् च यथार्थं पदम् अनुविचिन्त्य प्रकरणज्ञो हि प्रबलो विषयी स्यात् सर्वस्मिन् वाकोवाक्य इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
And in the Sāmaveda there is a supplementary scriptural text: 'Through studentship, and from this, he who knows the Atharvāṅgirases knows everything'—so runs the Brāhmaṇa.

Regarding the self, the Oṃ-syllable is medicine for the self, absolute isolation of the self.
Restraining oneself, one should meditate upon reality, consisting merely of union.
Surpassing the Vedas, one attains the supreme fruit pertaining to the self—such is the meaning.
Having reflected upon the word in accordance with reality through these questions and answers, as full of knowledge endowed with deliberation, one who knows the context will become a powerful master in every theological dialogue. Such is the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: etad dha smaitad vidvāṃsam ekādaśākṣaṃ maudgalyaṃ glāvo maitreyo 'bhyājagāma sa tasmin brahmacaryaṃ vasato vijñāyovāca kiṃ svin maryā ayaṃ tan maudgalyo 'dhyeti yad asmin brahmacaryaṃ vasatīti tad dhi maudgalyasyāntevāsī śuśrāva sa ācāryāyāvrajyācacaṣṭe duradhīyānaṃ vā ayaṃ bhavantam avocad yo 'yam adyātithir bhavati kiṃ saumya vidvān iti trīn vedān brūte bho iti tasya saumya vipaṣṭo vijigīṣo 'ntevāsī taṃ me hvayeti tam ājuhāva tam abhyuvācāsāv iti bho iti kiṃ saumya ta ācāryo 'dhyetīti trīn vedān brūte bho iti yan nu khalu saumyāsmābhiḥ sarve vedā mukhato gṛhītāḥ kathaṃ ta evam ācāryo bhāṣate kathaṃ nu śiṣṭāḥ śiṣṭebhya evaṃ bhāṣeran yaṃ hy enam ahaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchāmi na taṃ vivakṣyati na hy enam adhyetīti sa ha maudgalyaḥ svam antevāsinam uvāca parehi saumya glāvaṃ maitreyam upasīda adhīhi bhoḥ sāvitrīṃ gāyatrīṃ caturviṃśatiyoniṃ dvādaśamithunām yasyā bhṛgvaṅgirasaś cakṣuḥ yasyāṃ sarvam idaṃ śritaṃ tāṃ bhavān prabravītv iti sa cet saumya duradhīyāno bhaviṣyaty ācāryovāca brahmacārī brahmācāriṇo sāvitrīṃ prāheti vakṣyati tat tvaṃ brūyād duradhīyānaṃ taṃ vai bhavān maudgalyam avocat sa tvā yaṃ praśnam aprākṣīn na taṃ vyavocaḥ purā saṃvatsarād ārtim āriṣyasīti ||
meaning: एतद् ध स्मैतद् विद्वांसम् एकादशाक्षं मौद्गल्यं ग्लावो मैत्रेयो ऽभ्याजगाम स तस्मिन् ब्रह्मचर्यं वसतो विज्ञायोवाच किं स्विन् मर्या अयं तन् मौद्गल्यो ऽध्येति यद् अस्मिन् ब्रह्मचर्यं वसतीति तद् धि मौद्गल्यस्यान्तेवासी शुश्राव स आचार्यायाव्रज्याचचष्टे दुरधीयानं वा अयं भवन्तम् अवोचद् यो ऽयम् अद्यातिथिर् भवति किं सौम्य विद्वान् इति त्रीन् वेदान् ब्रूते भो इति तस्य सौम्य विपष्टो विजिगीषो ऽन्तेवासी तं मे ह्वयेति तम् आजुहाव तम् अभ्युवाचासाव् इति भो इति किं सौम्य त आचार्यो ऽध्येतीति त्रीन् वेदान् ब्रूते भो इति यन् नु खलु सौम्यास्माभिः सर्वे वेदा मुखतो गृहीताः कथं त एवम् आचार्यो भाषते कथं नु शिष्टाः शिष्टेभ्य एवं भाषेरन् यं ह्य् एनम् अहं प्रश्नं पृच्छामि न तं विवक्ष्यति न ह्य् एनम् अध्येतीति स ह मौद्गल्यः स्वम् अन्तेवासिनम् उवाच परेहि सौम्य ग्लावं मैत्रेयम् उपसीद अधीहि भोः सावित्रीं गायत्रीं चतुर्विंशतियोनिं द्वादशमिथुनाम् यस्या भृग्वङ्गिरसश् चक्षुः यस्यां सर्वम् इदं श्रितं तां भवान् प्रब्रवीत्व् इति स चेत् सौम्य दुरधीयानो भविष्यत्य् आचार्योवाच ब्रह्मचारी ब्रह्माचारिणो सावित्रीं प्राहेति वक्ष्यति तत् त्वं ब्रूयाद् दुरधीयानं तं वै भवान् मौद्गल्यम् अवोचत् स त्वा यं प्रश्नम् अप्राक्षीन् न तं व्यवोचः पुरा संवत्सराद् आर्तिम् आरिष्यसीति ||
text_mt: Now Glāva Maitreya came to Ekādaśākṣa Maudgalya, who possessed this knowledge. / Knowing that [students] were living in studentship under him, he said: 'Indeed, my good fellows, what does this Maudgalya teach, that [people] live in studentship under him?' / A disciple of Maudgalya heard that. / He went to the teacher and reported: / 'This man who is the guest today spoke of you, sir, as having studied improperly.' / 'What, my good sir, does he know?' [asked Maudgalya]. / 'Sir, he claims [knowledge of] the three Vedas.' / 'My good sir, a disciple of his has been defeated and seeks victory; call him to me.' / He called him. / He addressed him: 'So-and-so!' / 'Sir!' [the student responded]. / 'What, my good sir, does your teacher study?' / 'Sir, he claims [knowledge of] the three Vedas.' / 'Now really, my good sir, all the Vedas have been grasped by us by heart; how can your teacher speak thus? / How, indeed, could the learned speak thus to the learned? / For whichever question I shall ask him, he will not be able to answer; / for he has not studied this.' / Maudgalya said to his own disciple: 'Go, my good sir, approach Glāva Maitreya: / "Sir, recite the Sāvitrī Gāyatrī of twenty-four wombs and twelve couples, / whose eye is Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, / upon which all this rests; let the master explain that." / If, my good sir, he has studied improperly, he will say: "The teacher spoke, the Vedic student recited the Sāvitrī to the Vedic student." Then you should say: "You, sir, spoke of that Maudgalya as having studied improperly.

He went to where the other was. / He questioned him. / He could not answer. / He said to him: 'You, sir, spoke of that Maudgalya as having studied improperly. / He asked you a question, and you did not explain it. / Before a year [passes] you will meet with misfortune.' / Maitreya said to his disciples: 'Sirs, disperse according to your purpose, to your homes, according to your will. / I indeed spoke of Maudgalya as having studied improperly; / he asked me a question, and I did not explain it. / I will approach him; / I will perform pacification.' / In the morning Maitreya, fuel in hand, approached Maudgalya: 'Here I am, sir, Maitreya.' / 'For what purpose?' / 'I indeed spoke of you, sir, as having studied improperly. / You asked me a question, and I did not explain it. / I will approach you [as a pupil]; / I will perform pacification.' / He said: 'Here you have approached, and everything has been done. They say that you travel with a wretched vehicle. / And this chariot of mine is a fine one; / I give it to you; / drive with it.' / He said: 'This indeed is friendliness and kindheartedness on your part, just as the master says; / nevertheless, I approach you [as a pupil].'

Having approached him, he asked: 'What, sir, do they say is the desirable [splendour] of Savitṛ? What do the wise say is the splendour of the god? Explain the thoughts, if you know them!'

'[and the thoughts] which Savitṛ impels as he goes?'

To him he said: 'The Vedas and the metres are the desirable [glory] of Savitṛ;

the poets declare the splendor of the god to be food; the thoughts are the sacrificial acts.

text_mt:
And that I explain to you: [the thoughts] which Savitṛ impels as he goes.'

Clasping his feet, he asked: 'Teach me, sir: Who is Savitṛ? What is the Sāvitrī?'

Mind is Savitṛ, speech is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is mind, there is speech; where speech is, there is mind. These two are origins, a single couple. Agni is Savitṛ, the earth is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is Agni, there is the earth; where the earth is, there is Agni. These two are origins, a single couple. Vāyu is Savitṛ, the intermediate space is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is Vāyu, there is the intermediate space; where the intermediate space is, there is Vāyu. These two are origins, a single couple. Āditya is Savitṛ, heaven is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is Āditya, there is heaven; where heaven is, there is Āditya. These two are origins, a single couple. The moon is Savitṛ, the constellations are the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is the moon, there are the constellations; where the constellations are, there is the moon. These two are origins, a single couple. Day is Savitṛ, night is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is day, there is night; where night is, there is day. These two are origins, a single couple. Heat is Savitṛ, cold is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is heat, there is cold; where cold is, there is heat. These two are origins, a single couple. Cloud is Savitṛ, rain is the Sāvitrī. Where indeed there is cloud, there is rain; where rain is, there is cloud.

These two are origins, a single couple.

Lightning is Savitṛ, thunder is the Sāvitrī.

Where indeed there is lightning, there is thunder; where thunder is, there is lightning.

These two are origins, a single couple.

Breath is Savitṛ, food is the Sāvitrī.

Where indeed there is breath, there is food; where food is, there is breath.

These two are origins, a single couple.

The Vedas are Savitṛ, the metres are the Sāvitrī.

Where indeed there are the Vedas, there are the metres; where the metres are, there are the Vedas.

These two are origins, a single couple.

The sacrifice is Savitṛ, the sacrificial fees are the Sāvitrī.

Where indeed there is sacrifice, there are the sacrificial fees; where the sacrificial fees are, there is sacrifice.

These two are origins, a single couple.

Knowing this indeed, when they said to Opākāri: 'Your Vedic student has died,' then he who was told this became like a piled fire-altar.

sanskrit_iast: brahma hedaṃ śriyaṃ pratiṣṭhām āyatanam aikṣata tat tapasva yadi tad vrate dhriyeta tat satye pratyatiṣṭhat sa savitā sāvitryā brāhmaṇaṃ sṛṣṭvā tat savitrīṃ paryadadhāt tat savitur vareṇyam iti sāvitryāḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ pṛthivy arcaṃ samadadhāt ṛcāgnim agninā śriyam śriyā striyam striyā mithunam mithunena prajām prajayā karma karmaṇā tapas tapasā satyam satyena brahma brahmaṇā brāhmaṇam brāhmaṇena vratam vratena vai brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśito bhavati aśūnyo bhavaty avichinno bhavaty avichinno 'sya tantur avichinnaṃ jīvanaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etaṃ sāvitryāḥ prathamaṃ pādaṃ vyācaṣṭe ||
meaning: ब्रह्म हेदं श्रियं प्रतिष्ठाम् आयतनम् ऐक्षत तत् तपस्व यदि तद् व्रते ध्रियेत तत् सत्ये प्रत्यतिष्ठत् स सविता सावित्र्या ब्राह्मणं सृष्ट्वा तत् सवित्रीं पर्यदधात् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति सावित्र्याः प्रथमः पादः पृथिव्य् अर्चं समदधात् ऋचाग्निम् अग्निना श्रियम् श्रिया स्त्रियम् स्त्रिया मिथुनम् मिथुनेन प्रजाम् प्रजया कर्म कर्मणा तपस् तपसा सत्यम् सत्येन ब्रह्म ब्रह्मणा ब्राह्मणम् ब्राह्मणेन व्रतम् व्रतेन वै ब्राह्मणः संशितो भवति अशून्यो भवत्य् अविछिन्नो भवत्य् अविछिन्नो ऽस्य तन्तुर् अविछिन्नं जीवनं भवति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् एवम् एतं सावित्र्याः प्रथमं पादं व्याचष्टे ||
