"Now if he does not choose one who knows thus as brahman priest, their sacrifice is emptied from the south, their sacrifice is emptied from the south."

Thus ends the second prapāṭhaka in the first part of the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa in the Atharvaveda.

Oṃ. The earth slopes to the south; the waters flow to the south.
Therefore, sacrifices are, as it were, higher than that earth where the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases abide.
Just as the waters flow over these worlds, even so the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases flow over all the gods.
Even so this sacred utterance carries all the Vedas: 'Oṃ' for the ṛc verses, 'Oṃ' for the yajus formulas, 'Oṃ' for the chants; 'Oṃ' is the proclamation of everything.
The wise used to perform this reply at the sacrifice:
'O divine brahman priests, come, come!'
These divine brahman priests are indeed the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases.
Praising them and choosing them, they think they are calling them.
No one other than a knower of the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, even if chosen, should come to the sacrifice.
Through the splendour of the sacrifice he attains splendour, through vigour, vigour, through fame, fame.
No one other than a knower of the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, even if chosen, should come to the sacrifice, lest he rob the sacrifice.
Just as a calf, having previously observed, would suckle the cow, so the brahman priest who knows the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, when chosen, should come to the sacrifice, lest he rob the sacrifice.
Just as if a cow or a horse or a mule were one-footed, two-footed, or three-footed, what could it carry, what could it reach?
Therefore, choose only the knower of the Ṛgveda as Hotṛ, the knower of the Yajurveda as Adhvaryu, the knower of the Sāmaveda as Udgātṛ, the knower of the Atharvans and Aṅgirases as brahman priest.
Thus indeed his sacrifice, four-footed, stands firm upon the four worlds, upon the four gods, upon the Vedas, upon the four priestly offices.
He stands firm with offspring and cattle who knows thus, and who knows thus the priestly duty of the priests, and who knows what is to be sacrificed in the sacrifice. Thus the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatir yajñam atanuta sa ṛcaiva hautram akarod yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnaudgātram atharvāṅgirobhir brahmatvam taṃ vā etaṃ mahāvādyaṃ kurute yad ṛcaiva hautram akarod yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnaudgātram atharvāṅgirobhir brahmatvam sa vā eṣa tribhir vedair yajñasyānyataraḥ pakṣaḥ saṃskriyate manasaiva brahmā yajñasyānyatraṃ pakṣaṃ saṃskaroti ayam u vai yaḥ pavate sa yajñas tasya manaś ca vāk ca vartanī manasā caiva hi vācā ca yajño vartate ada eva mana iyam eva vāk sa yad vadan nāsti vidyād ardhaṃ me 'sya yajñasyāntaragād iti tad yathaikapāt puruṣo yann ekacakro vā ratho vartamāno bhreṣaṃ nyety evam evāsya yajño bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajñasya bhreṣam anu yajamāno bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajamānasya bhreṣam anv ṛtvijo bhreṣaṃ niyanti ṛtvijāṃ bhreṣam anu dakṣiṇā bhreṣaṃ niyanti dakṣiṇānāṃ bhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir bhreṣaṃ nyeti putrapaśūnāṃ bhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokena bhreṣaṃ nyeti svargasya lokasya bhreṣam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo bhreṣaṃ nyeti yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: प्रजापतिर् यज्ञम् अतनुत स ऋचैव हौत्रम् अकरोद् यजुषाध्वर्यवं साम्नौद्गात्रम् अथर्वाङ्गिरोभिर् ब्रह्मत्वम् तं वा एतं महावाद्यं कुरुते यद् ऋचैव हौत्रम् अकरोद् यजुषाध्वर्यवं साम्नौद्गात्रम् अथर्वाङ्गिरोभिर् ब्रह्मत्वम् स वा एष त्रिभिर् वेदैर् यज्ञस्यान्यतरः पक्षः संस्क्रियते मनसैव ब्रह्मा यज्ञस्यान्यत्रं पक्षं संस्करोति अयम् उ वै यः पवते स यज्ञस् तस्य मनश् च वाक् च वर्तनी मनसा चैव हि वाचा च यज्ञो वर्तते अद एव मन इयम् एव वाक् स यद् वदन् नास्ति विद्याद् अर्धं मे ऽस्य यज्ञस्यान्तरगाद् इति तद् यथैकपात् पुरुषो यन्न् एकचक्रो वा रथो वर्तमानो भ्रेषं न्येत्य् एवम् एवास्य यज्ञो भ्रेषं न्येति यज्ञस्य भ्रेषम् अनु यजमानो भ्रेषं न्येति यजमानस्य भ्रेषम् अन्व् ऋत्विजो भ्रेषं नियन्ति ऋत्विजां भ्रेषम् अनु दक्षिणा भ्रेषं नियन्ति दक्षिणानां भ्रेषम् अनु यजमानः पुत्रपशुभिर् भ्रेषं न्येति पुत्रपशूनां भ्रेषम् अनु यजमानः स्वर्गेण लोकेन भ्रेषं न्येति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य भ्रेषम् अनु तस्यार्धस्य योगक्षेमो भ्रेषं न्येति यस्मिन्न् अर्धे यजन्त इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Prajāpati spread the sacrifice.
With the Ṛg[veda] he performed the office of the Hotṛ, with the Yajur[veda] that of the Adhvaryu, with the Sāma[veda] that of the Udgātṛ, and with the Atharvāṅgirases the office of the Brahman.
He makes it this great dispute, that with the Ṛg[veda] he performed the office of the Hotṛ, with the Yajur[veda] that of the Adhvaryu, with the Sāma[veda] that of the Udgātṛ, and with the Atharvāṅgirases the office of the Brahman.
Through the three Vedas one wing of the sacrifice is consecrated;
with the mind alone the brahman priest consecrates the other wing of the sacrifice.
This [wind] that purifies here is indeed the sacrifice;
mind and speech are its two wheel-tracks.
For by mind and speech the sacrifice proceeds.
Mind is that [distant] world; speech is this [near] world.
If, while speaking, he should realise, 'Half of my sacrifice has slipped away,'
then, just as a one-legged man walking, or a one-wheeled chariot moving along, stumbles, even so his sacrifice stumbles.
Following the stumbling of the sacrifice, the sacrificer stumbles.
Following the stumbling of the sacrificer, the priests stumble.
Following the stumbling of the priests, the sacrificial fees stumble.
Following the stumbling of the sacrificial fees, the sacrificer stumbles with respect to sons and cattle.
Following the stumbling with respect to sons and cattle, the sacrificer stumbles with respect to the heavenly world.
Following the stumbling with respect to the heavenly world, the welfare of that region stumbles in which they sacrifice. Thus [says] the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha smāha śvetaketur āruṇeyo brahmāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāṣamāṇam ardhaṃ me 'sya yajñasyāntaragād iti tasmād brahmā stute bahiḥpavamāne vācoyamyam upāṃśv antaryāmābhyām atha ye pavamānā odṛcas teṣu atha yāni stotrāṇi saśastrāṇy ā vaṣaṭkārāt teṣu sa yad ṛkto bhreṣaṃ nyṛcched oṃ bhūr janad iti gārhapatye juhuyāt yadi yajuṣṭa oṃ bhuvo janad iti dakṣiṇāgnau juduyāt yadi sāmata oṃ svar janad ity āhavanīye juhuyāt yady anājñātād brahmato voṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om ity āhavanīya eva juhuyāt tad vākovākyasyarcāṃ yajuṣāṃ sāmnām atharvāṅgirasām athāpi vedānāṃ rasana yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhīyate tad yathā lavaṇenety uktam tad yathobhayapāt puruṣo yann ubhayacakro vā ratho vartamāno 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti evam evāsya yajño 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajñasyābhreṣam anu yajamāno 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajamānasyābhreṣam anv ṛtvijo 'bhreṣaṃ niyanti ṛtvijām abhreṣam anu dakṣiṇā abhreṣaṃ niyanti dakṣiṇānām abhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir abhreṣaṃ nyeti putrapaśūnām abhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokenābhreṣaṃ nyeti svargasya lokasyābhreṣam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: तद् उ ह स्माह श्वेतकेतुर् आरुणेयो ब्रह्माणं दृष्ट्वा भाषमाणम् अर्धं मे ऽस्य यज्ञस्यान्तरगाद् इति तस्माद् ब्रह्मा स्तुते बहिःपवमाने वाचोयम्यम् उपांश्व् अन्तर्यामाभ्याम् अथ ये पवमाना ओदृचस् तेषु अथ यानि स्तोत्राणि सशस्त्राण्य् आ वषट्कारात् तेषु स यद् ऋक्तो भ्रेषं न्यृच्छेद् ओं भूर् जनद् इति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् यदि यजुष्ट ओं भुवो जनद् इति दक्षिणाग्नौ जुदुयात् यदि सामत ओं स्वर् जनद् इत्य् आहवनीये जुहुयात् यद्य् अनाज्ञाताद् ब्रह्मतो वों भूर् भुवः स्वर् जनद् ओम् इत्य् आहवनीय एव जुहुयात् तद् वाकोवाक्यस्यर्चां यजुषां साम्नाम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसाम् अथापि वेदानां रसन यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संधीयते तद् यथा लवणेनेत्य् उक्तम् तद् यथोभयपात् पुरुषो यन्न् उभयचक्रो वा रथो वर्तमानो ऽभ्रेषं न्येति एवम् एवास्य यज्ञो ऽभ्रेषं न्येति यज्ञस्याभ्रेषम् अनु यजमानो ऽभ्रेषं न्येति यजमानस्याभ्रेषम् अन्व् ऋत्विजो ऽभ्रेषं नियन्ति ऋत्विजाम् अभ्रेषम् अनु दक्षिणा अभ्रेषं नियन्ति दक्षिणानाम् अभ्रेषम् अनु यजमानः पुत्रपशुभिर् अभ्रेषं न्येति पुत्रपशूनाम् अभ्रेषम् अनु यजमानः स्वर्गेण लोकेनाभ्रेषं न्येति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्याभ्रेषम् अनु तस्यार्धस्य योगक्षेमो ऽभ्रेषं न्येति यस्मिन्न् अर्धे यजन्त इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
On this Śvetaketu Āruṇeya said, having seen the brahman priest speaking: 'Half of my sacrifice has slipped away.'
Therefore, when the Bahiṣpavamāna is sung, the brahman priest should maintain silence [together] with the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma [libations];
and also during those Pavamāna [chants] until their concluding verses;
and during those stotras accompanied by śastras up to the vaṣaṭ-call.
If he should stumble on account of a Ṛc, he should offer in the Gārhapatya [fire] saying: 'Oṃ bhūr janat.'
If on account of a Yajus, he should offer in the Dakṣiṇa fire saying: 'Oṃ bhuvo janat.'
If on account of a Sāman, he should offer in the Āhavanīya [fire] saying: 'Oṃ svar janat.'
If from an unknown [cause] or on account of the Brahman, he should offer in the Āhavanīya alone saying: 'Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om.'
That belongs to the disputation of the verses, the formulas, the chants, and the Atharvāṅgirases.
Furthermore, the breach in the sacrifice is healed by the sap of the Vedas,
just as [it is healed] with salt, as has been said.
Just as a two-legged man walking, or a two-wheeled chariot moving along, does not stumble, even so his sacrifice does not stumble.
Following the non-stumbling of the sacrifice, the sacrificer does not stumble.
Following the non-stumbling of the sacrificer, the priests do not stumble.
Following the non-stumbling of the priests, the sacrificial fees do not stumble.
Following the non-stumbling of the sacrificial fees, the sacrificer does not stumble with respect to sons and cattle.
Following the non-stumbling with respect to sons and cattle, the sacrificer does not stumble with respect to the heavenly world.
Following the non-stumbling with respect to the heavenly world, the welfare of that region does not stumble in which they sacrifice. Thus [says] the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: tad yad audumbaryāṃ ma āsiṣṭa hiṅṅ akārṣīn me prāstāvīn ma udagāsīn me subrahmaṇyām āhvāsīd ity udgātre dakṣiṇā nīyante grahān me 'grahīt prācārīn me 'śuśruvan me samanasas kārṣīd ayākṣīn me 'vaṣaṭkārṣīn ma ity adhvaryave hotṛṣadana āsiṣṭāyākṣīn me 'śāṃsīn me 'vaṣaṭkārṣīn ma iti hotre devayajanaṃ me cīkḷpad brahmāsādaṃ me 'sīsṛpad brahmajapān me 'japīt purastāddhomasaṃsthitahomān me 'hauṣīd ayākṣīn me 'śāṃsīn me 'vaṣaṭkārṣīn ma iti brahmaṇe bhūyiṣṭhena mā brahmaṇākārṣīd iti etad vai bhūyiṣṭhaṃ brahma yad bhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ ye 'ṅgirasaḥ sa raso ye 'tharvāṇo ye 'tharvāṇas tadbheṣajam yad bheṣajaṃ tad amṛtaṃ yad amṛtaṃ tad brahma sa vā eṣa pūrveṣām ṛtvijām ardhabhāgasyārdham itareṣām ardhaṃ brahmaṇa iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: तद् यद् औदुम्बर्यां म आसिष्ट हिङ्ङ् अकार्षीन् मे प्रास्तावीन् म उदगासीन् मे सुब्रह्मण्याम् आह्वासीद् इत्य् उद्गात्रे दक्षिणा नीयन्ते ग्रहान् मे ऽग्रहीत् प्राचारीन् मे ऽशुश्रुवन् मे समनसस् कार्षीद् अयाक्षीन् मे ऽवषट्कार्षीन् म इत्य् अध्वर्यवे होतृषदन आसिष्टायाक्षीन् मे ऽशांसीन् मे ऽवषट्कार्षीन् म इति होत्रे देवयजनं मे चीकॢपद् ब्रह्मासादं मे ऽसीसृपद् ब्रह्मजपान् मे ऽजपीत् पुरस्ताद्धोमसंस्थितहोमान् मे ऽहौषीद् अयाक्षीन् मे ऽशांसीन् मे ऽवषट्कार्षीन् म इति ब्रह्मणे भूयिष्ठेन मा ब्रह्मणाकार्षीद् इति एतद् वै भूयिष्ठं ब्रह्म यद् भृग्वङ्गिरसः ये ऽङ्गिरसः स रसो ये ऽथर्वाणो ये ऽथर्वाणस् तद्भेषजम् यद् भेषजं तद् अमृतं यद् अमृतं तद् ब्रह्म स वा एष पूर्वेषाम् ऋत्विजाम् अर्धभागस्यार्धम् इतरेषाम् अर्धं ब्रह्मण इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Sacrificial fees are brought to the Udgātṛ [with the thought]: 'Because he sat for me by the audumbarī post, sounded the hiṅ-call for me, chanted the prelude for me, sang the udgītha for me, and invoked the Subrahmaṇyā for me.'
To the Adhvaryu: 'He drew the cups for me, went forward for me, listened for me, made [the priests] of one mind, sacrificed for me, and uttered the vaṣaṭ-call for me.'
To the Hotṛ: 'He sat in the Hotṛ's seat, sacrificed for me, recited for me, and uttered the vaṣaṭ-call for me.'
To the brahman priest: 'He prepared the sacrificial ground for me, walked to the brahman's seat for me, murmured the brahman's silent prayers for me, offered the introductory and concluding oblations for me, sacrificed for me, recited for me, and uttered the vaṣaṭ-call for me;
he has acted for me with the most abundant Brahman.'
For this is the most abundant Brahman: the Bhṛgvaṅgirases.
Those that are the Aṅgirases, that is the essence; those that are the Atharvans, that is the remedy.
What is the remedy is the immortal; what is the immortal is Brahman.
He indeed receives half the share of the previous priests, while half belongs to the others, and half to the brahman priest. Thus [says] the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: devāś ca ha vā asurāś ca saṃgrāmaṃ samayatanta tatraitās tisro hotrā jihmaṃ pratipedire tāsām indra ukthāni sāmāni lulopa tāni hotre prāyacchat ājyaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva pra'ugaṃ potur vaiśvadevaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva niṣkevalyaṃ neṣṭuḥ marutvatīyaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva agnimārutam āgnīdhrasya tasmād etad abhyastataram iva śasyate yad āgnimārutam tasmād ete saṃśaṃsukā iva bhavanti yad dhotā potā neṣṭā āgnīdhro mumuhe vasīta tad brahmeyasāmivāsa tāsām ardhaṃ pratilulopa prathamārhaṇaṃ ca prathamapadaṃ caitad dakṣiṇāṃ caitat pariśiṣeded iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: देवाश् च ह वा असुराश् च संग्रामं समयतन्त तत्रैतास् तिस्रो होत्रा जिह्मं प्रतिपेदिरे तासाम् इन्द्र उक्थानि सामानि लुलोप तानि होत्रे प्रायच्छत् आज्यं ह वै होतुर् बभूव प्रऽउगं पोतुर् वैश्वदेवं ह वै होतुर् बभूव निष्केवल्यं नेष्टुः मरुत्वतीयं ह वै होतुर् बभूव अग्निमारुतम् आग्नीध्रस्य तस्माद् एतद् अभ्यस्ततरम् इव शस्यते यद् आग्निमारुतम् तस्माद् एते संशंसुका इव भवन्ति यद् धोता पोता नेष्टा आग्नीध्रो मुमुहे वसीत तद् ब्रह्मेयसामिवास तासाम् अर्धं प्रतिलुलोप प्रथमार्हणं च प्रथमपदं चैतद् दक्षिणां चैतत् परिशिषेदेद् इति ब्राह्मणम् ||

sanskrit_iast: uddālako ha vā āruṇir udīcyān vṛto dhāvayāṃ cakāra tasya ha niṣka upāhito babhūvopavādād bibhyato yo mā brāhmaṇo 'nūcāna upavadiṣyati tasmā etaṃ pradāsyamīti tad dhodīcyān brāhmaṇān bhayaṃ vivedoddālako ha vā ayam āyāti kaurupañcolo brahmā brahmaputraḥ sa ūrdhvaṃ vṛto na paryādadhīta kenemaṃ vīreṇa pratisaṃyatāmahā iti taṃ yata eva prapannaṃ dadhre tata evam anupratipedire te ha svaidāyanaṃ śaunakam ūcuḥ svaidāyana tvaṃ vai no brahmiṣṭho 'sīti tvayemaṃ vīreṇa pratisaṃyatāmahā iti taṃ yata eva prapannaṃ dadhre tata evam anupratipedire taṃ ha svaidāyanā ity āmantrayām āsa sa bho gautamasya putreti hāsmā asūyā pratiśrutaṃ pratiśuśrāva sa vai gautamasya putra ūrdhvaṃ vṛto dhāvet ||
meaning: उद्दालको ह वा आरुणिर् उदीच्यान् वृतो धावयां चकार तस्य ह निष्क उपाहितो बभूवोपवादाद् बिभ्यतो यो मा ब्राह्मणो ऽनूचान उपवदिष्यति तस्मा एतं प्रदास्यमीति तद् धोदीच्यान् ब्राह्मणान् भयं विवेदोद्दालको ह वा अयम् आयाति कौरुपञ्चोलो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मपुत्रः स ऊर्ध्वं वृतो न पर्यादधीत केनेमं वीरेण प्रतिसंयतामहा इति तं यत एव प्रपन्नं दध्रे तत एवम् अनुप्रतिपेदिरे ते ह स्वैदायनं शौनकम् ऊचुः स्वैदायन त्वं वै नो ब्रह्मिष्ठो ऽसीति त्वयेमं वीरेण प्रतिसंयतामहा इति तं यत एव प्रपन्नं दध्रे तत एवम् अनुप्रतिपेदिरे तं ह स्वैदायना इत्य् आमन्त्रयाम् आस स भो गौतमस्य पुत्रेति हास्मा असूया प्रतिश्रुतं प्रतिशुश्राव स वै गौतमस्य पुत्र ऊर्ध्वं वृतो धावेत् ||
text_mt:
Uddālaka Āruṇi, having been chosen [as a priest], went driving among the northerners.
He had a gold ornament tied on him, out of fear of reproof: 'To whichever learned brāhmaṇa shall reprove me, to him I will give this.'
Then fear seized the northern brāhmaṇas: 'Indeed, Uddālaka, this Kuru-Pañcāla brahman priest, son of a brahman priest, is coming.
Chosen high above [us], let him not overpower [us].
With what hero shall we contend against him?'
Just where they found him stationed, there they encountered him. They said to Svaidāyana Śaunaka: 'Svaidāyana, you indeed are the most learned in Brahman among us.
With you as hero we shall contend against him.'
Just where they found him stationed, there they encountered him.
He addressed him: 'Svaidāyana!'
He, with indignation, gave answer to his greeting: 'O son of Gautama!'
May that son of Gautama run, chosen high above!

sanskrit_iast: yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imāḥ prajāḥ śirastaḥ prathamaṃ lomaśā jāyante kasmād āsām aparam iva śmaśrūṇy upakakṣāṇy anyāni lomāni jāyante yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imāḥ prājāḥ śirastaḥ prathamaṃ palitā bhavanti kasmād antataḥ sarvā eva palitā bhavanti yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imāḥ prajā adantikā jāyante kasmād āsām aparam iva jāyante yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād āsāṃ saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāṇāṃ prabhidyante kasmād āsāṃ punar eva jāyante kasmād antataḥ sarva eva prabhidyante yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād adhare dantāḥ pūrve jāyante para uttare yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād adhare dantāḥ aṇīyāṃso hrasīyāṃsaḥ prathīyāṃso varṣīyāṃsa uttare yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imau daṃṣṭrau dīrghatarau kasmāt same iva jaṃbhe yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād ime śrotre antarataḥ same iva dīrṇe yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmāt pumāṃsaḥ śmaśruvanto 'śmaśruvaḥ striyaḥ yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād āsāṃ saṃtatam iva śarīraṃ bhavati kasmād āsām asthīni dṛḍhatarāṇīva bhavanti yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād āsāṃ prathame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ na saṃbhavati kasmād āsāṃ madhyame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ saṃbhavati kasmād āsām uttame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ na saṃbhavati yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād idaṃ śiśnam uccaśa eti nīcī padyate kasmāt sakṛd apānam ||
meaning: यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् इमाः प्रजाः शिरस्तः प्रथमं लोमशा जायन्ते कस्माद् आसाम् अपरम् इव श्मश्रूण्य् उपकक्षाण्य् अन्यानि लोमानि जायन्ते यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् इमाः प्राजाः शिरस्तः प्रथमं पलिता भवन्ति कस्माद् अन्ततः सर्वा एव पलिता भवन्ति यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् इमाः प्रजा अदन्तिका जायन्ते कस्माद् आसाम् अपरम् इव जायन्ते यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् आसां सप्तवर्षाष्टवर्षाणां प्रभिद्यन्ते कस्माद् आसां पुनर् एव जायन्ते कस्माद् अन्ततः सर्व एव प्रभिद्यन्ते यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् अधरे दन्ताः पूर्वे जायन्ते पर उत्तरे यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् अधरे दन्ताः अणीयांसो ह्रसीयांसः प्रथीयांसो वर्षीयांस उत्तरे यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् इमौ दंष्ट्रौ दीर्घतरौ कस्मात् समे इव जंभे यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् इमे श्रोत्रे अन्तरतः समे इव दीर्णे यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्मात् पुमांसः श्मश्रुवन्तो ऽश्मश्रुवः स्त्रियः यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् आसां संततम् इव शरीरं भवति कस्माद् आसाम् अस्थीनि दृढतराणीव भवन्ति यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् आसां प्रथमे वयसि रेतः सिक्तं न संभवति कस्माद् आसां मध्यमे वयसि रेतः सिक्तं संभवति कस्माद् आसाम् उत्तमे वयसि रेतः सिक्तं न संभवति यस् तद् दर्शपूर्णमासयो रूपं विद्यात् कस्माद् इदं शिश्नम् उच्चश एति नीची पद्यते कस्मात् सकृद् अपानम् ||
text_mt:
"Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why are these creatures born hairy first on the head? Why do beards, underarm hair, and other hairs grow later on them?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why do these creatures become grey first on the head? Why in the end do they become completely grey?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why are these creatures born toothless? Why do [teeth] grow later on them?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why do they break off when they are seven or eight years old? Why do they grow again on them? Why in the end do they all break off?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why do the lower teeth grow first, and the upper ones later?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why are the lower teeth finer and shorter, and the upper ones broader and larger?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why are these two canine teeth longer? Why are the jaws matched as it were?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why are these two ears slit matched as it were on the inside?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why do men have beards, and women are beardless?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why is their body continuous, as it were? Why are their bones firmer, as it were?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why does semen shed not generate in their first stage of life? Why does semen shed generate in their middle stage of life? Why does semen shed not generate in their last stage of life?
Whoever knows that form of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifice: Why does this penis rise upward and fall downward?
Why is there an exhalation once?"

sanskrit_iast: atha yaḥ purastād aṣṭāv ājyabhāgān vidyān madhyataḥ pañca havirbhāgāḥ ṣaṭ prājāpatyā upariṣṭād aṣṭāv ājyabhāgān vidyāt atha yo gāyatrīṃ hariṇīṃ jyotiṣpakṣāṃ sarvair yajñair yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam abhivahantīṃ vidyāt atha yaḥ apaṅktiṃ pañcapadāṃ saptadaśākṣarāṃ sarvair yajñair yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam abhivahantīṃ vidyāt tasmai ha niṣkaṃ prayacchann uvācānūcāno ha vai svaidāyanāsi suvarṇaṃ vai suvarṇavide dadāmīti tad upayamya niścakrāma tatrāpavavrāja yatretaro babhūva taṃ ha papraccha kim eṣa gautamasya putra iti eṣa brahmā brahmāputra iti hovāca yad enaṃ kaś cid upavadetota mīmāṃseta ha vā mūrdhā vā asya vipatet prāṇā vainaṃ jahyur iti te mitha eva cikrandeyur viprāpavavraja yatretaro babhūva te prātaḥ samitpāṇaya upodeyur upāyāmo bhavantam iti kim artham iti yān eva no bhavāṃs tān hyaḥ praśnān apṛcchat tān eva no bhavān vyācakṣīteti tatheti tebhya etān praśnān vyācacaṣṭe ||
meaning: अथ यः पुरस्ताद् अष्टाव् आज्यभागान् विद्यान् मध्यतः पञ्च हविर्भागाः षट् प्राजापत्या उपरिष्टाद् अष्टाव् आज्यभागान् विद्यात् अथ यो गायत्रीं हरिणीं ज्योतिष्पक्षां सर्वैर् यज्ञैर् यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकम् अभिवहन्तीं विद्यात् अथ यः अपङ्क्तिं पञ्चपदां सप्तदशाक्षरां सर्वैर् यज्ञैर् यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकम् अभिवहन्तीं विद्यात् तस्मै ह निष्कं प्रयच्छन्न् उवाचानूचानो ह वै स्वैदायनासि सुवर्णं वै सुवर्णविदे ददामीति तद् उपयम्य निश्चक्राम तत्रापवव्राज यत्रेतरो बभूव तं ह पप्रच्छ किम् एष गौतमस्य पुत्र इति एष ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मापुत्र इति होवाच यद् एनं कश् चिद् उपवदेतोत मीमांसेत ह वा मूर्धा वा अस्य विपतेत् प्राणा वैनं जह्युर् इति ते मिथ एव चिक्रन्देयुर् विप्रापवव्रज यत्रेतरो बभूव ते प्रातः समित्पाणय उपोदेयुर् उपायामो भवन्तम् इति किम् अर्थम् इति यान् एव नो भवांस् तान् ह्यः प्रश्नान् अपृच्छत् तान् एव नो भवान् व्याचक्षीतेति तथेति तेभ्य एतान् प्रश्नान् व्याचचष्टे ||
text_mt:
"Now, whoever knows the eight portions of clarified butter in front, five oblation-portions in the middle, six pertaining to Prajāpati, and eight portions of clarified butter above;
now, whoever knows the Gāyatrī, tawny, with wings of light, carrying the sacrificer to the heavenly world through all the sacrifices;
now, whoever knows the non-paṅkti of five feet and seventeen syllables, carrying the sacrificer to the heavenly world through all the sacrifices—"
Giving him the golden neck-ornament, he said: "Learned indeed are you, Svaidāyana! Gold indeed I give to the knower of gold."
Taking that, he departed.
He went to where the other was.
He asked him: "What [sort of man] is this son of Gautama?"
"This one is a Brahman, a son of Brahman," he said. "If anyone should rebuke him or dispute [with him], his head would split apart, or the life-breaths would leave him."
They lamented among themselves. The priest departed to where the other was.
In the morning, with firewood in hand, they approached [saying]: "We approach you as pupils."
"For what purpose?"
"The very questions that you asked us yesterday, let your honor explain those very ones to us."
"So be it."
He explained these questions to them:

sanskrit_iast: yat purastād vedeḥ prathamaṃ barhi stṛṇāti tasmād imāḥ prajāḥ śirastaḥ prathamaṃ lomaśā jāyante yad aparam iva prastaram anuprastṛṇāti tasmād āsām aparam iva śmaśrūṇy upakakṣāṇy anyāni lomāni jāyante yat prāg barhiṣaḥ prastaram anupraharati tasmād imāḥ prajāḥ śirastaḥ prathamaṃ palitā bhavanti yad antataḥ sarvam evānupraharati tasmād antataḥ sarva eva palitā bhavanti yat prayājā apuro'nuvākyāvanto bhavanti tasmād imāḥ prajā adantikā jāyante yad dhavīṃṣi puro'nuvākyāvanti bhavanti tasmād āsām aparam iva jāyante yad anuyājā apuro'nuvākyāvanto bhavanti tasmād āsāṃ saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāṇāṃ prabhidyante yat patnīsaṃyājāḥ puro'nuvākyāvanto bhavanti tasmād āsāṃ punar eva jāyante yat samiṣṭayajur apuro'nuvākyāvad bhavati tasmād antataḥ sarva eva prabhidyante yad gāyatryānūcya triṣṭubhā yajati tasmād adhare dantāḥ pūrve jāyante para uttare yad ṛcānūcya yajuṣā yajati tasmād adhare dantā aṇīyāṃso hrasīyāṃsaḥ prathīyāṃso varṣīyāṃsa uttare yad āghārau dīrghatarau prāñcāv āghārayati tasmād imau daṃṣṭrau dīrghatarau yat saṃyājye sacchandasī tasmāt same iva jambhe yac caturthe prayāje samānayati tasmād ime śrotre antarataḥ same iva dīrṇe yaj japaṃ japitvābhihiṃkṛṇoti tasmāt pumāṃsaḥ śmaśruvanto 'śmaśruva striyaḥ yat sāmidhenīḥ saṃtanvann anvāha tasmād āsāṃ saṃtatam iva śarīraṃ bhavati yat sāmidhenyaḥ kāṣṭhahaviṣo bhavanti tasmād āsām asthīni dṛḍhatarāṇīva bhavanti yat prayājā ājyahaviṣo bhavanti tasmād āsāṃ prathame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ na saṃbhavati yan madhye haviṣāṃ dadhnā ca puroḍāśena ca pracaranti tasmād āsāṃ madhyame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ saṃbhavati yad anuyājā ājyahaviṣo bhavanti tasmād āsām uttame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ na saṃbhavati yad uttame 'nuyāje sakṛd apāniti tasmād idaṃ śiśnam uccaśa eti nīcī padyate yan nāpānet sakṛcchūnaṃ syāt yan muhur apānet sakṛtpannaṃ syāt tasmāt sakṛd apāniti net sakṛcchūnaṃ syāt sakṛtpannaṃ veti ||
meaning: यत् पुरस्ताद् वेदेः प्रथमं बर्हि स्तृणाति तस्माद् इमाः प्रजाः शिरस्तः प्रथमं लोमशा जायन्ते यद् अपरम् इव प्रस्तरम् अनुप्रस्तृणाति तस्माद् आसाम् अपरम् इव श्मश्रूण्य् उपकक्षाण्य् अन्यानि लोमानि जायन्ते यत् प्राग् बर्हिषः प्रस्तरम् अनुप्रहरति तस्माद् इमाः प्रजाः शिरस्तः प्रथमं पलिता भवन्ति यद् अन्ततः सर्वम् एवानुप्रहरति तस्माद् अन्ततः सर्व एव पलिता भवन्ति यत् प्रयाजा अपुरोऽनुवाक्यावन्तो भवन्ति तस्माद् इमाः प्रजा अदन्तिका जायन्ते यद् धवींषि पुरोऽनुवाक्यावन्ति भवन्ति तस्माद् आसाम् अपरम् इव जायन्ते यद् अनुयाजा अपुरोऽनुवाक्यावन्तो भवन्ति तस्माद् आसां सप्तवर्षाष्टवर्षाणां प्रभिद्यन्ते यत् पत्नीसंयाजाः पुरोऽनुवाक्यावन्तो भवन्ति तस्माद् आसां पुनर् एव जायन्ते यत् समिष्टयजुर् अपुरोऽनुवाक्यावद् भवति तस्माद् अन्ततः सर्व एव प्रभिद्यन्ते यद् गायत्र्यानूच्य त्रिष्टुभा यजति तस्माद् अधरे दन्ताः पूर्वे जायन्ते पर उत्तरे यद् ऋचानूच्य यजुषा यजति तस्माद् अधरे दन्ता अणीयांसो ह्रसीयांसः प्रथीयांसो वर्षीयांस उत्तरे यद् आघारौ दीर्घतरौ प्राञ्चाव् आघारयति तस्माद् इमौ दंष्ट्रौ दीर्घतरौ यत् संयाज्ये सच्छन्दसी तस्मात् समे इव जम्भे यच् चतुर्थे प्रयाजे समानयति तस्माद् इमे श्रोत्रे अन्तरतः समे इव दीर्णे यज् जपं जपित्वाभिहिंकृणोति तस्मात् पुमांसः श्मश्रुवन्तो ऽश्मश्रुव स्त्रियः यत् सामिधेनीः संतन्वन्न् अन्वाह तस्माद् आसां संततम् इव शरीरं भवति यत् सामिधेन्यः काष्ठहविषो भवन्ति तस्माद् आसाम् अस्थीनि दृढतराणीव भवन्ति यत् प्रयाजा आज्यहविषो भवन्ति तस्माद् आसां प्रथमे वयसि रेतः सिक्तं न संभवति यन् मध्ये हविषां दध्ना च पुरोडाशेन च प्रचरन्ति तस्माद् आसां मध्यमे वयसि रेतः सिक्तं संभवति यद् अनुयाजा आज्यहविषो भवन्ति तस्माद् आसाम् उत्तमे वयसि रेतः सिक्तं न संभवति यद् उत्तमे ऽनुयाजे सकृद् अपानिति तस्माद् इदं शिश्नम् उच्चश एति नीची पद्यते यन् नापानेत् सकृच्छूनं स्यात् यन् मुहुर् अपानेत् सकृत्पन्नं स्यात् तस्मात् सकृद् अपानिति नेत् सकृच्छूनं स्यात् सकृत्पन्नं वेति ||
text_mt: Because he first strews the sacred grass in front of the altar, therefore these creatures are first born hairy from the head. / Because he strews the prastara bunch afterwards, as it were, therefore their beard, armpits, and other hair are born later, as it were. / Because he casts forward the prastara bunch before the sacred grass, therefore these creatures first become grey from the head. / Because he casts forward all of it at the end, therefore all become grey at the end. / Because the fore-offerings have no introductory verses, therefore these creatures are born toothless. / Because the oblations have introductory verses, therefore [their teeth] are born later, as it were. / Because the after-offerings have no introductory verses, therefore [the teeth] of those [who are] seven or eight years old break out. / Because the offerings to the wives [of the gods] have introductory verses, therefore [their teeth] grow again. / Because the samiṣṭayajus has no introductory verse, therefore in the end all [teeth] fall out. / Because he recites with a gāyatrī and sacrifices with a triṣṭubh, therefore the lower teeth are born first, and later the upper. / Because he recites with an ṛc verse and sacrifices with a yajus formula, therefore the lower teeth are smaller and shorter, and the upper ones are broader and larger. / Because he pours the two libations longer and eastward, therefore these two canine teeth are longer. / Because the two saṃyājyā verses are of the same metre, therefore the two jaws are equal, as it were. / Because at the fourth fore-offering he pours together, therefore these two ears inside are equal and cleft, as it were. / Because having muttered the silent prayer he pronounces hiṃ, therefore men have beards and women are beardless. / Because he recites the kindling verses continuously, therefore their body is continuous, as it were. / Because the kindling verses have firewood as oblation, therefore their bones are rather firm, as it were. / Because the fore-offerings have clarified butter as oblation, therefore in their first age semen that is poured does not conceive. / Because in the middle of the oblations they proceed with curd and with rice-cake, therefore in their middle age semen that is poured conceives. / Because the after-offerings have clarified butter as oblation, therefore in their last age semen that is poured does not conceive. / Because at the last after-offering he exhales once, therefore this penis rises up and falls down. / If he were not to exhale, it would be swollen once and for all. / If he were to exhale repeatedly, it would fall once and for all.

meaning: अथ ये पुरस्ताद् अष्टाव् आज्यभागाः पञ्च प्रयाजा द्वाव् आघारौ द्वाव् आज्यभागाव् आग्नेय आज्यभागानां प्रथमः सौम्यो द्वितीयो हविर्भागानाम् हविर् ह्य् एव सौम्यम् आग्नेयः पुरोडाशः अग्नीषोमीयः पुरोडाशो ऽग्निः स्विष्टकृद् इत्य् एते मध्यतः पञ्च हविर्भागाः अथ ये षट् प्राजापत्या इडा च प्राशित्रं च यच् चाग्नीध्रायावद्यति ब्रह्मभागो यजमानभागो ऽन्वाहार्य एव षष्ठः अथ य उपरिष्टाद् अष्टाव् आज्यभागास् त्रयो ऽनुयाजाश् चत्वारः पत्नीसंयाजाः समिष्टयजुर् अष्टमम् अथ या गायत्री हरिणी ज्योतिष्पक्षा सर्वैर् यज्ञैर् यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकम् अभिवहति वेदिर् एव सा तस्य ये पुरस्ताद् अष्टाव् आज्याभागाः स दक्षिणः पक्षः अथ य उपरिष्टाद् अष्टाव् आज्यभागाः स उत्तरः पक्षः हवींष्य् आत्मा गार्हपत्यो जघनम् आहवनीयः शिरः सौवर्णराजतौ पक्षौ तद् यद् आदित्यं पुरस्तात् पर्यन्तं न पश्यन्ति तस्माद् अज्योतिष्क उत्करो भवति अथ या पङ्क्तिः पञ्चपदा सप्तदशाक्षरा सर्वैर् यज्ञैर् यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकम् अभिवहति याज्यैव सा तस्या ओं श्रावयेति चतुरक्षरम् अस्तु श्रौषद् इति चतुरक्षरम् यजेति द्व्यक्षरम् ये यजामह इति पञ्चाक्षरम् द्व्यक्षरो वै वषट्कारः सैषा पङ्क्तिः पञ्चपदा सप्तदशाक्षरा सर्वैर् यज्ञैर् यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकम् अभिवहति तद् यत्रास्यैश्वर्यं स्याद् यत्र वैनम् अभिवहेयुर् एवंविदम् एव तत्र ब्रह्माणं वृणीयान् नानेवंविदम् इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Therefore he exhales once, lest it be swollen at once or fallen at once.

Now, the eight ghee-portions in front are the five preliminary offerings, the two libations, and the two ghee-portions. The one sacred to Agni is the first of the ghee-portions; the one sacred to Soma is the second of the oblation-portions, for the Soma offering is indeed an oblation. The cake for Agni, the cake for Agni-Soma, and Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—these are the five oblation-portions in the middle. Now, the six belonging to Prajāpati are the iḍā, the prāśitra, that which is cut off for the Agnīdhra, the brahman priest's portion, the sacrificer's portion, and the anvāhārya is the sixth. Now, the eight ghee-portions at the end are the three after-offerings, the four wife-offerings, and the samiṣṭayajus as the eighth. Now, the yellow Gāyatrī with wings of light which carries the sacrificer with all sacrifices to the heavenly world is the altar itself. Its eight ghee-portions in front are the right wing; its eight ghee-portions at the end are the left wing; the oblations are the body; the Gārhapatya is the rump; the Āhavanīya is the head; the two wings are of gold and silver. Since they do not see the sun surrounding [it] in front, therefore the rubbish-heap is without light. Now, the Paṅkti of five feet and seventeen syllables which carries the sacrificer with all sacrifices to the heavenly world is the offering-verse itself. Its 'om śrāvaya' has four syllables; 'astu śrauṣaṭ' has four syllables; 'yaja' has two syllables; 'ye yajāmahe' has five syllables; the vaṣaṭ-call has two syllables. That is the Paṅkti: having five feet and seventeen syllables, it carries the sacrificer with all sacrifices to the heavenly world. Therefore, wherever one might hold lordship, or wherever they would conduct him, there one should choose only a brahman priest who knows thus, not one who does not know thus. Such is the Brāhmaṇa.

Then Prācīnayogya came [and said]: “Gautama, I ask you about the agnihotra.” / “Ask, Prācīnayogya.” / “To what deity belongs your cow when being called? / To what deity when summoned? / To what deity when let loose? / To what deity while the calf is being brought up? / To what deity when the calf has been brought up? / To what deity while being milked? / To what deity when milked? / To what deity when being stepped forth with? / To what deity when being carried? / To what deity when being set over the fire? / To what deity when set over the fire? / To what deity when being illuminated from above? / To what deity when illuminated from above? / To what deity when boiling over? / To what deity when curdled? / To what deity when counteracted with water? / To what deity when being taken off? / To what deity when taken off? / To what deity when being ladled out? / To what deity when ladled out? / To what deity when being stepped forth with?

To what deity when being carried?

To what deity when being set down?

To what deity when set down?

To what deity did you offer the first oblation?

To what deity did you look at the Gārhapatya?

To what deity belongs the subsequent oblation?

To what deity, having offered, did you raise the ladle thrice northward?

To what deity, placing the ladle on the sacrificial grass and wiping it, did you wipe your hands to the north?

To what deity did you pour down water with the unwashed ladle?

To what deity with the washed [ladle]?

text_mt:
To what deity did you wipe the handle of the ladle downward at night?

To what deity did you wipe it upward in the morning?”

“If you know this, Gautama, your offering is offered; but if you do not know, your offering is unoffered.” Thus the brāhmaṇa.

He said: “Mine belongs to Rudra in the cow when being called; / to Manu when summoned; / to Vāyu when let loose; / to Virāj while the calf is being brought up; / to Jagatī when brought up; / to the Aśvins while being milked; / to Soma when milked; / to Bṛhaspati when being stepped forth with; / to Heaven and Earth when being carried; / to Agni when being set over the fire; / to Vaiśvānara when set over the fire; / to Viṣṇu when being illuminated from above; / to the Maruts when illuminated from above; / to Pūṣan when boiling over; / to Varuṇa when curdled; / to Sarasvatī when counteracted with water; / to Tvaṣṭṛ when being taken off; / to Dhātṛ when taken off; / to the All-Gods when being ladled out; / to Savitṛ when ladled out; / to Bṛhaspati when being stepped forth with; / to Heaven and Earth when being carried; / to Indra when being set down;

When I offered the first oblation, I placed myself in the heavenly world.

When I looked at the Gārhapatya, [it was] for the continuation of this world.

The subsequent oblation belongs to Prajāpati.

Therefore it is fuller, in mind alone.

When, having offered, I raised the ladle thrice northward, thereby I pleased the Rudras.

When, placing the ladle on the sacrificial grass and wiping it, I wiped my hands to the north, thereby I pleased the herbs and trees.

When, wiping a second time and putting the sacred cord over the right shoulder, I made svadhā to the ancestors to the south, thereby I pleased the ancestors.

When I ate the first [portion], thereby I pleased the vital breaths.

When the second, thereby [I pleased] the embryos.

Therefore embryos live without eating.

When I ate everything at the end, thereby I pleased all the gods.

When I poured down water with the unwashed ladle, thereby I pleased the serpents and other folk.

When with the washed [ladle], thereby [I pleased] the serpents and holy folk.

When I poured down water with the ladle behind the Āhavanīya, thereby I pleased the Gandharvas and Apsarases.

When I heated the dipping spoon and the offering ladle, thereby I pleased the Seven Seers.

When I wiped the handle of the ladle downward at night, those who lie down at night, [being] on the south, them I led upward.

When I wiped it upward in the morning, those who set out in the morning, [being] on the south, them I led upward.” Thus the brāhmaṇa.

“Just so it is, sir, as you say. / Yet I ask you.” / “Ask, Prācīnayogya.” / “If in the evening one's fires were set up, all were burning, the sacrificial vessels were washed and set down, and then the Dakṣiṇāgni were to go out, what fear would come from that?” / “Swiftly his wife passes away, if one offers without knowing. / But by knowledge I make the offering over it.” / “What is your knowledge, what is the expiation?” / “Having brought the Dakṣiṇāgni forward from the Gārhapatya, having extracted the embers to the east, he should offer, saying: ‘To out-breath and in-breath, svāhā!’ / Then in the morning, having set up the fires in their proper place, he should offer as before. / That is my knowledge, that is the expiation.” / “And if the Āhavanīya were to go out, what fear would come from that?” / “Swiftly his son passes away, if one offers without knowing. / But by knowledge I make the offering over it.” / “What is your knowledge, what is the expiation?” / “Having brought the Āhavanīya forward from the Gārhapatya, having extracted the embers to the west, he should offer, saying: ‘To equalised breath and diffused breath, svāhā!’ / Then in the morning, having set up the fires in their proper place, he should offer as before. / That is my knowledge, that is the expiation.” / “And if the Gārhapatya were to go out, what fear would come from that?” / “Swiftly the householder passes away, if one offers without knowing. / But by knowledge I make the offering over it.” / “What is your knowledge, what is the expiation?” / “Having carried the Āhavanīya along with its ashes south around the Dakṣiṇāgni and established it in the Gārhapatya's hearth, and having brought the Āhavanīya forward from there, having extracted the embers to the north, he should offer, saying: ‘To the up-breath and form, svāhā!’ / Then in the morning, having set up the fires in their proper place, he should offer as before.

That is my knowledge, that is the expiation.”

“And if all the fires were to go out, what fear would come from that?”

“Swiftly the householder suffers complete ruin, if one offers without knowing.

"I, however, offer with knowledge."

"What is your knowledge? What is the expiation?"

"Having smeared the fire-hearths with a lump of dung from an ox, and having set down what is to be offered, and having churned the fire, one should offer saying: 'To out-breath and in-breath, svāhā! To equalizing breath and diffused breath, svāhā! To ascending breath and bodily form, svāhā!'"

"Then in the morning, having built up the fires in their proper places, one should offer as before."

"That is my knowledge; that is the expiation."

"Now, if they should not be able to generate fire, and no wind should blow from anywhere, what danger would come from that?"

"Futile is his sacrificed and offered [oblation], who offers without knowledge."

"I, however, offer with knowledge."

"What is your knowledge? What is the expiation?"

"Having smeared the fire-hearths with a lump of dung from an ox alone, and having set down what is to be offered, one should offer into oneself with the hymn: 'May the wind blow healing...'"

"Then in the morning, having churned the fire, and having built up the fires in their proper places, one should offer as before."

"That is my knowledge; that is the expiation," thus the Brāhmaṇa.

"Just so is it, venerable sir, as you say. / I indeed approach you [as a pupil]." / "If you had not spoken thus, your head would have flown apart. / Come, then, I will tell you that so that it will not fly apart. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, speech is satisfied thereby. / Speech being satisfied, fire is satisfied. / Fire being satisfied, the earth is satisfied. / The earth being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the earth are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, the breath is satisfied thereby. / The breath being satisfied, the wind is satisfied. / The wind being satisfied, the intermediate space is satisfied. / The intermediate space being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the intermediate space are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, the eye is satisfied thereby. / The eye being satisfied, the sun is satisfied. / The sun being satisfied, heaven is satisfied. / Heaven being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to heaven are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, the mind is satisfied thereby. / The mind being satisfied, the moon is satisfied. / The moon being satisfied, the waters are satisfied. / The waters being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the waters are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, hearing is satisfied thereby. / Hearing being satisfied, the quarters and intermediate regions are satisfied. / The quarters and intermediate regions being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the quarters and intermediate regions are satisfied."

For him who knows thus, eating and drinking, this right hand is the offering spoon juhū;

sanskrit_iast: priyamedhā ha vai bharadvājā yajñavido manyamānās te ha sma na kañ cana vedavidam upayanti te sarvam avidus te sahaivāvidus te 'gnihotra eva na samavadanta teṣām ekaḥ sakṛd agnihotram ajuhod dvir ekas trir ekas teṣāṃ yaḥ sakṛd agnihotram ajuhot tam itarāv apṛcchatāṃ kasmai tvaṃ juhoṣīti ekadhā vā idaṃ sarvaṃ prajāpatiḥ prajāpataya evāhaṃ sāyaṃ juhomīti prajāpataye prātar iti teṣāṃ yo dvir ajuhot tam itarāv apṛcchatāṃ kābhyāṃ tvaṃ juhoṣīti agnaye prajāpataya iti sāyaṃ sūryāya prajāpataya iti prātas teṣāṃ yas trir ajuhot tam itarāv apṛcchatāṃ kebhyas tvaṃ juhoṣīty agnaye prajāpataye 'numataya iti sāyaṃ sūryāya prajāpataye 'gnaye sviṣṭakṛta iti prātas teṣāṃ yo dvir ajuhot sa ārdhnot sa bhūyiṣṭho 'bhavat prajayā cetarau śriyā cetarāv atyākrāmat tasya ha prajām itarayoḥ praje sajātatvam upaitām tasmād dvir hotavyaṃ yajuṣā caiva manasā ca yām eva sa ṛddhim ārdhnot tām ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān agnihotraṃ juhotīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: प्रियमेधा ह वै भरद्वाजा यज्ञविदो मन्यमानास् ते ह स्म न कञ् चन वेदविदम् उपयन्ति ते सर्वम् अविदुस् ते सहैवाविदुस् ते ऽग्निहोत्र एव न समवदन्त तेषाम् एकः सकृद् अग्निहोत्रम् अजुहोद् द्विर् एकस् त्रिर् एकस् तेषां यः सकृद् अग्निहोत्रम् अजुहोत् तम् इतराव् अपृच्छतां कस्मै त्वं जुहोषीति एकधा वा इदं सर्वं प्रजापतिः प्रजापतय एवाहं सायं जुहोमीति प्रजापतये प्रातर् इति तेषां यो द्विर् अजुहोत् तम् इतराव् अपृच्छतां काभ्यां त्वं जुहोषीति अग्नये प्रजापतय इति सायं सूर्याय प्रजापतय इति प्रातस् तेषां यस् त्रिर् अजुहोत् तम् इतराव् अपृच्छतां केभ्यस् त्वं जुहोषीत्य् अग्नये प्रजापतये ऽनुमतय इति सायं सूर्याय प्रजापतये ऽग्नये स्विष्टकृत इति प्रातस् तेषां यो द्विर् अजुहोत् स आर्ध्नोत् स भूयिष्ठो ऽभवत् प्रजया चेतरौ श्रिया चेतराव् अत्याक्रामत् तस्य ह प्रजाम् इतरयोः प्रजे सजातत्वम् उपैताम् तस्माद् द्विर् होतव्यं यजुषा चैव मनसा च याम् एव स ऋद्धिम् आर्ध्नोत् ताम् ऋध्नोति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Ever sacrificed, ever offered, ever eaten and drunk is the Agnihotra of him who knows thus and who, knowing thus, offers the Agnihotra; thus the Brāhmaṇa.

The Priyamedha Bharadvājas, indeed, thinking themselves to be knowers of sacrifice,
would not approach any knower of the Veda.
They knew everything;
they knew [it] together.
They disagreed only regarding the Agnihotra.
One of them offered the Agnihotra once, one twice, one thrice.
To the one among them who offered the Agnihotra once, the other two said: 'To whom do you offer?'
'Prajāpati is indeed this whole [universe] in one way.
I offer to Prajāpati alone in the evening; to Prajāpati in the morning.'
To the one among them who offered twice, the other two said: 'To whom [two] do you offer?'
'To Agni [and] Prajāpati in the evening; to Sūrya [and] Prajāpati in the morning.'
To the one among them who offered thrice, the other two said: 'To whom [pl.] do you offer?' 'To Agni, Prajāpati, and Anumati in the evening; to Sūrya, Prajāpati, and Agni Sviṣṭakṛt in the morning.'
The one among them who offered twice prospered;
he became the greatest;
he surpassed the other two in offspring and fortune.
The offspring of the other two entered into the status of kinship [as dependents] to his offspring.
Therefore, one should offer twice, with a yajus-formula and silently in mind.
He prospers with the very prosperity with which that one prospered, who knows thus and who, knowing thus, offers the Agnihotra. Such is the Brāhmaṇa. || 15

sanskrit_iast: svāhā vai kutaḥ saṃbhūtā kena prakṛtā kiṃ vāsyā gotram katy akṣarā kati padā kati varṇā kiṃ pūrvāvasānā kva cit sthitā kim adhiṣṭhānā brūhi svāhāyā yad daivataṃ rūpaṃ ca svāhā vai satyasaṃbhūtā brahmaṇā prakṛtā lāmagāyanasagotrā dve akṣare ekaṃ padam trayaś ca varṇāḥ śuklaḥ padmaḥ suvarṇa iti sarvacchandasāṃ vedeṣu samāsabhūtaikocchvāsā varṇānte catvāro vedāḥ śarīre ṣaḍaṅgāny oṣadhivanaspatayo lomāni cakṣuṣī sūryācandramasau sā svāhā sā svadhā yajñeṣu vaṣaṭkārabhūtā prayujyate tasyā agnir daivatam brāhmaṇo rūpam iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: स्वाहा वै कुतः संभूता केन प्रकृता किं वास्या गोत्रम् कत्य् अक्षरा कति पदा कति वर्णा किं पूर्वावसाना क्व चित् स्थिता किम् अधिष्ठाना ब्रूहि स्वाहाया यद् दैवतं रूपं च स्वाहा वै सत्यसंभूता ब्रह्मणा प्रकृता लामगायनसगोत्रा द्वे अक्षरे एकं पदम् त्रयश् च वर्णाः शुक्लः पद्मः सुवर्ण इति सर्वच्छन्दसां वेदेषु समासभूतैकोच्छ्वासा वर्णान्ते चत्वारो वेदाः शरीरे षडङ्गान्य् ओषधिवनस्पतयो लोमानि चक्षुषी सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ सा स्वाहा सा स्वधा यज्ञेषु वषट्कारभूता प्रयुज्यते तस्या अग्निर् दैवतम् ब्राह्मणो रूपम् इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
From what, indeed, did Svāhā arise?
By whom was she produced?
What is her lineage?
How many syllables [has she]?
How many words?
How many colours?
What are her initial and final [elements]?
Where does she abide?
What is her support?
Declare what is the deity and the form of Svāhā!
Svāhā arose from Truth;
she was produced by Brahman;
she belongs to the Lāmagāyana lineage;
[she has] two syllables,
one word,
and three colours: white, lotus-red, and golden.
She is the condensation of all metres in the Vedas, [uttered in] a single breath; at the end of the sound, the four Vedas are in [her] body;
the six auxiliary disciplines [are her limbs]; the herbs and forest trees are her body-hairs;
her two eyes are the sun and the moon.
She, as Svāhā, as Svadhā, is employed in the sacrifices, having become the vaṣaṭ-call.
Agni is her deity;
a brāhmaṇa is her form. Such is the Brāhmaṇa. || 16

sanskrit_iast: athāpi kāravo ha nāma ṛṣayo 'lpasvā āsan ta imam ekagum agniṣṭomaṃ dadṛśus tam āharan tenāyajanta te svar yayuḥ sa ya icchet svar iyām iti sa etenaikagunāgniṣṭomena yajeteti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथापि कारवो ह नाम ऋषयो ऽल्पस्वा आसन् त इमम् एकगुम् अग्निष्टोमं ददृशुस् तम् आहरन् तेनायजन्त ते स्वर् ययुः स य इच्छेत् स्वर् इयाम् इति स एतेनैकगुनाग्निष्टोमेन यजेतेति ब्राह्मणम् ||

sanskrit_iast: athātaḥ savanīyasya paśor vibhāgaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ uddhṛtyāvadānāni hanū sajihve prastotuḥ kaṇṭhaḥ sakākudraḥ pratihartuḥ śyenaṃ vakṣa udgātuḥ dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ sāṃsam adhvaryoḥ savyam upagātṝṇām savyo 'ṃsaḥ pratiprasthātuḥ dakṣiṇā śroṇirathyāstrī brahmaṇaḥ avarasakthaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ ūruḥ potuḥ savyā śroṇir hotuḥ avarasakthaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya arur acchāvākasya dakṣiṇā dor neṣṭuḥ savyā sadasyasya sadaṃ cānūkaṃ ca gṛhapateḥ jāghanī patnyās tāṃ sā brāhmaṇena pratigrāhayati vaniṣṭhur hṛdayaṃ vṛkkau cāṅgulyāni dakṣiṇo bāhur āgnīdhrasya savya ātreyasya dakṣiṇau pādau gṛhapater vratapradasya savyau pādau gṛhapatnyāḥ vratapradāyāḥ sahaivainayor oṣṭhas taṃ gṛhapatir evānuśinaṣṭi maṇikāś ca skandhyās tisraś ca kīkasā grāvastutas tisraś caiva kīkasā ardhaṃ cāpānasyonnetuḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ camasādhvaryūṇāṃ klomā śamayituḥ śiraḥ subrahmaṇyasya yaḥ śvaḥsutyām āhvayate tasya carma tathā khalu ṣaṭtriṃśat sampadyante ṣaṭtriṃśadavadānā gauḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣarā bṛhatī bārhato vai svargo lokaḥ bṛhatyā vai devāḥ svarge loke yajante bṛhatyā svarge loke pratitiṣṭhanti pratitiṣṭhanti prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ vibhajante atha yad ato 'nyathāśīliko vā pāpakṛto vā hutādo vānyajanā vā vimathnīrann evam evaiṣāṃ paśur vimathato bhavaty asvargyaḥ devabhājo ha vā imaṃ śrutaṛṣiḥ paśor vibhāgaṃ vidāṃ cakāra tam u girijāya bābhravyāyānyo manuṣyebhyaḥ provāca tato 'yam arvāṅ manuṣyeṣv āsīd iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथातः सवनीयस्य पशोर् विभागं व्याख्यास्यामः उद्धृत्यावदानानि हनू सजिह्वे प्रस्तोतुः कण्ठः सकाकुद्रः प्रतिहर्तुः श्येनं वक्ष उद्गातुः दक्षिणं पार्श्वं सांसम् अध्वर्योः सव्यम् उपगातॄणाम् सव्यो ऽंसः प्रतिप्रस्थातुः दक्षिणा श्रोणिरथ्यास्त्री ब्रह्मणः अवरसक्थं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः ऊरुः पोतुः सव्या श्रोणिर् होतुः अवरसक्थं मैत्रावरुणस्य अरुर् अच्छावाकस्य दक्षिणा दोर् नेष्टुः सव्या सदस्यस्य सदं चानूकं च गृहपतेः जाघनी पत्न्यास् तां सा ब्राह्मणेन प्रतिग्राहयति वनिष्ठुर् हृदयं वृक्कौ चाङ्गुल्यानि दक्षिणो बाहुर् आग्नीध्रस्य सव्य आत्रेयस्य दक्षिणौ पादौ गृहपतेर् व्रतप्रदस्य सव्यौ पादौ गृहपत्न्याः व्रतप्रदायाः सहैवैनयोर् ओष्ठस् तं गृहपतिर् एवानुशिनष्टि मणिकाश् च स्कन्ध्यास् तिस्रश् च कीकसा ग्रावस्तुतस् तिस्रश् चैव कीकसा अर्धं चापानस्योन्नेतुः अत ऊर्ध्वं चमसाध्वर्यूणां क्लोमा शमयितुः शिरः सुब्रह्मण्यस्य यः श्वःसुत्याम् आह्वयते तस्य चर्म तथा खलु षट्त्रिंशत् सम्पद्यन्ते षट्त्रिंशदवदाना गौः षट्त्रिंशदक्षरा बृहती बार्हतो वै स्वर्गो लोकः बृहत्या वै देवाः स्वर्गे लोके यजन्ते बृहत्या स्वर्गे लोके प्रतितिष्ठन्ति प्रतितिष्ठन्ति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं विभजन्ते अथ यद् अतो ऽन्यथाशीलिको वा पापकृतो वा हुतादो वान्यजना वा विमथ्नीरन्न् एवम् एवैषां पशुर् विमथतो भवत्य् अस्वर्ग्यः देवभाजो ह वा इमं श्रुतऋषिः पशोर् विभागं विदां चकार तम् उ गिरिजाय बाभ्रव्यायान्यो मनुष्येभ्यः प्रोवाच ततो ऽयम् अर्वाङ् मनुष्येष्व् आसीद् इति ब्राह्मणम् ||

sanskrit_iast: athāto dīkṣā kasya svid dhetor dīkṣita ityācakṣate śreṣṭhāṃ dhiyaṃ kṣiyatīti taṃ vā etaṃ dhīkṣitaṃ santaṃ dīkṣita ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ kasya svid dhetor dīkṣito 'pratyutthāyiko bhavaty anabhivādukaḥ pratyuttheyo 'bhivādyaḥ ye pratyuttheyā abhivādyās ta enam āviṣṭā bhavanty atharvāṅgirasas tasya kim ātharvaṇam iti yad ātmany eva juhvati na parasmin evaṃ hātharvaṇānām odanasavānām ātmany eva juhvati na parasmin athāsya kim āṅgirasam iti yad ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca nāmāni na gṛhṇāty evaṃ ha tasminnāsād ātmanaś caiva pareṣāṃ ca nāmāni na gṛhyante vicakṣaṇavatīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣante canasitavatīm vicakṣayanti brāhmaṇaṃ canasayanti prājāpatyam saiṣā vratadhug atharvāṅgirasas tāṃ hy anvāyattāḥ kasya svid dhetor dīkṣito 'nāśyanno bhavati nāsya nāma gṛhṇanti annastho nāmastho bhavatīty āhus tasya ye 'nnam adanti te 'sya pāpmānam adanti athāsya ye nāma gṛhṇanti te 'sya nāmnaḥ pāpmānam apāghnate athāpi vedānāṃ garbhabhūto bhavatīty āhus tasyājātasyāvijñātasyākrītasomasyābhojanīyaṃ bhavatīty āhuḥ sa dīkṣāṇāṃ prātar jāyate somaṃ krīṇanti tasya jātasya vijñātasya krītasomasya bhojanīyaṃ bhavatīty āhuḥ kasya svid dhetoḥ saṃsavā parijihīrṣitā bhavanti yataro vīryavattaro bhavati sa parasya yajñaṃ parimuṣṇāti kasya svid dhetor daive na dhyāyet saṃsthite nādhīyīteti saṃsavasyaiva hetor iti vidyotamāne stanayaty atho varṣati vāyavyam abhiṣuṇvanti vai devāḥ somaṃ ca bhakṣayanti tad abhiṣuṇvanti brāhmaṇāḥ śuśruvāṃso 'nūcānās teṣāṃ sarvarasabhakṣāḥ pitṛpitāmahā bhavanti sa daive na dhyāyet saṃsthite nādhīyīteti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथातो दीक्षा कस्य स्विद् धेतोर् दीक्षित इत्याचक्षते श्रेष्ठां धियं क्षियतीति तं वा एतं धीक्षितं सन्तं दीक्षित इत्य् आचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवा भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षद्विषः कस्य स्विद् धेतोर् दीक्षितो ऽप्रत्युत्थायिको भवत्य् अनभिवादुकः प्रत्युत्थेयो ऽभिवाद्यः ये प्रत्युत्थेया अभिवाद्यास् त एनम् आविष्टा भवन्त्य् अथर्वाङ्गिरसस् तस्य किम् आथर्वणम् इति यद् आत्मन्य् एव जुह्वति न परस्मिन् एवं हाथर्वणानाम् ओदनसवानाम् आत्मन्य् एव जुह्वति न परस्मिन् अथास्य किम् आङ्गिरसम् इति यद् आत्मनश् च परेषां च नामानि न गृह्णात्य् एवं ह तस्मिन्नासाद् आत्मनश् चैव परेषां च नामानि न गृह्यन्ते विचक्षणवतीं वाचं भाषन्ते चनसितवतीम् विचक्षयन्ति ब्राह्मणं चनसयन्ति प्राजापत्यम् सैषा व्रतधुग् अथर्वाङ्गिरसस् तां ह्य् अन्वायत्ताः कस्य स्विद् धेतोर् दीक्षितो ऽनाश्यन्नो भवति नास्य नाम गृह्णन्ति अन्नस्थो नामस्थो भवतीत्य् आहुस् तस्य ये ऽन्नम् अदन्ति ते ऽस्य पाप्मानम् अदन्ति अथास्य ये नाम गृह्णन्ति ते ऽस्य नाम्नः पाप्मानम् अपाघ्नते अथापि वेदानां गर्भभूतो भवतीत्य् आहुस् तस्याजातस्याविज्ञातस्याक्रीतसोमस्याभोजनीयं भवतीत्य् आहुः स दीक्षाणां प्रातर् जायते सोमं क्रीणन्ति तस्य जातस्य विज्ञातस्य क्रीतसोमस्य भोजनीयं भवतीत्य् आहुः कस्य स्विद् धेतोः संसवा परिजिहीर्षिता भवन्ति यतरो वीर्यवत्तरो भवति स परस्य यज्ञं परिमुष्णाति कस्य स्विद् धेतोर् दैवे न ध्यायेत् संस्थिते नाधीयीतेति संसवस्यैव हेतोर् इति विद्योतमाने स्तनयत्य् अथो वर्षति वायव्यम् अभिषुण्वन्ति वै देवाः सोमं च भक्षयन्ति तद् अभिषुण्वन्ति ब्राह्मणाः शुश्रुवांसो ऽनूचानास् तेषां सर्वरसभक्षाः पितृपितामहा भवन्ति स दैवे न ध्यायेत् संस्थिते नाधीयीतेति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Another, non-human being proclaimed it to Girija Bābhravya.

Thence it came down among men; thus the Brāhmaṇa.

Now then, the consecration.
For what reason do they call [him] 'the consecrated' (dīkṣita)?
Because he abides in the highest thought (dhīṃ kṣiyati).
Him, being thus 'dhīkṣita', they call 'dīkṣita' cryptically;
for the gods are fond of the cryptic, as it were, and hate the direct.
For what reason does the consecrated one not rise up [to greet anyone], nor greet [anyone], but is to be risen for and to be greeted?
Those who are to be risen for and greeted—the Atharvans and Aṅgirases—have entered into him.
What in him belongs to Atharvan?
In that they make the oblation into his own self, not into another.
Even so, in the boiled-rice pressings of the Atharvans, they make the oblation into their own self, not into another.
Then what in him belongs to Aṅgiras?
In that he does not pronounce his own name nor the names of others; thus indeed, in that assembly, his own name and the names of others are not pronounced.
They speak clear speech, pleasing [speech].
They make the brāhmaṇa clear; they please him who belongs to Prajāpati.
This is the observance-yielding [speech] of the Atharvans and Aṅgirases;
for they are dependent upon it.
For what reason does the consecrated one become one whose food is not to be eaten, and they do not pronounce his name?
They say: 'He resides in food, he resides in a name.' Those who eat his food eat his evil.
Then those who pronounce his name ward off evil from his name.
Moreover, they say: 'He becomes an embryo of the Vedas.'
They say: 'Before he is born, before he is known, before his Soma is purchased, [his food] is not to be eaten.'
He is born in the morning of the consecrations; they purchase the Soma; they say: 'When he is born, when he is known, when his Soma is purchased, [his food] is fit to be eaten.'
For what reason is conflicting soma-pressing (saṃsava) avoided?

Whichever of the two is more vigorous robs the sacrifice of the other.

'For what reason should one not meditate when [thunder/lightning] is divine, nor study when [the sacrifice] is concluded?'

'Only for the reason of conflicting soma-pressing,' [they say].

When it lightens, when it thunders, and also when it rains, it pertains to Vāyu; the gods indeed press Soma and consume [it].

sanskrit_iast: samāvṛttā ācāryā niṣedus tān ha yajño dīkṣiṣyamāṇān brāhmaṇarūpaṃ kṛtvopodeyāya itthaṃ ced vo 'pasamavatsur hanta vo 'haṃ madhye dīkṣā iti ta ūcur naiva tvā vidma na jānīmaḥ ko hīdavijñāyamānena saha dīkṣiṣyatīti yan nv idaṃ dīkṣiṣyadhve bhūyo na dīkṣiṣyadhve atha vā u evaṃ dīkṣayiṣyatha saṃ vai tarhi mohiṣyatha mohiṣyati vo yajñaḥ sarve te dīkṣayiṣyatheti atha vā u ekaṃ dīkṣayiṣyatha te vā ahīnartvijo gṛhapatayo bhaviṣyatha te tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyanta āsāṃ cakrire sa hovāca kiṃ nu tūṣṇīm ādhve bhūyo vaḥ pṛcchāmaḥ pṛcchateti yan nv idaṃ dīkṣiṣyadhva upame etasmin saṃvatsare mithunaṃ cariṣyatha nopaiṣyatheti dhig iti hocuḥ kathaṃ na dīkṣitā upaiṣyāmo nopaiṣyāmahā iti te vai brāhmaṇānām abhimantāro bhaviṣyatha reto ha vo ya etasmin saṃvatsare brāhmaṇās tad abhaviṣyaṃs te bodhimatā bhaviṣyatheti atha vā upeṣyāmo nopeṣyāmahā iti te vai dīkṣitā avakīrṇino bhaviṣyatha na ha vai devayānaḥ panthā prādur bhaviṣyatīti tiro vai devayānaḥ panthā bhaviṣyatīti te vayaṃ bhagavantam evopadhāvāma yathā svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ samaśnavāmahā iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: समावृत्ता आचार्या निषेदुस् तान् ह यज्ञो दीक्षिष्यमाणान् ब्राह्मणरूपं कृत्वोपोदेयाय इत्थं चेद् वो ऽपसमवत्सुर् हन्त वो ऽहं मध्ये दीक्षा इति त ऊचुर् नैव त्वा विद्म न जानीमः को हीदविज्ञायमानेन सह दीक्षिष्यतीति यन् न्व् इदं दीक्षिष्यध्वे भूयो न दीक्षिष्यध्वे अथ वा उ एवं दीक्षयिष्यथ सं वै तर्हि मोहिष्यथ मोहिष्यति वो यज्ञः सर्वे ते दीक्षयिष्यथेति अथ वा उ एकं दीक्षयिष्यथ ते वा अहीनर्त्विजो गृहपतयो भविष्यथ ते तूष्णीं ध्यायन्त आसां चक्रिरे स होवाच किं नु तूष्णीम् आध्वे भूयो वः पृच्छामः पृच्छतेति यन् न्व् इदं दीक्षिष्यध्व उपमे एतस्मिन् संवत्सरे मिथुनं चरिष्यथ नोपैष्यथेति धिग् इति होचुः कथं न दीक्षिता उपैष्यामो नोपैष्यामहा इति ते वै ब्राह्मणानाम् अभिमन्तारो भविष्यथ रेतो ह वो य एतस्मिन् संवत्सरे ब्राह्मणास् तद् अभविष्यंस् ते बोधिमता भविष्यथेति अथ वा उपेष्यामो नोपेष्यामहा इति ते वै दीक्षिता अवकीर्णिनो भविष्यथ न ह वै देवयानः पन्था प्रादुर् भविष्यतीति तिरो वै देवयानः पन्था भविष्यतीति ते वयं भगवन्तम् एवोपधावाम यथा स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं समश्नवामहा इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Then the brāhmaṇas who have heard [the Veda] and are learned in it press [it].

Their fathers and grandfathers become consumers of all essences.

'He should not meditate when [thunder/lightning] is divine, nor study when [the sacrifice] is concluded'—so says the Brāhmaṇa.

The teachers, having completed their studentship, sat down.
As they were about to be consecrated, Sacrifice, having assumed the form of a brahmin, approached them:
'If you have settled down together thus, well, let me be consecrated among you.'
They said: 'We do not know you at all, nor do we recognise you.
Who indeed will be consecrated together with one who is not known?'
[He said:] 'If you now undergo consecration, you will not be consecrated again.
Or if you consecrate [one another] in this manner, then you will indeed become bewildered;
your sacrifice will become bewildered if all of you consecrate [one another].
Or if you consecrate only one, then you will become priests of an ahīna sacrifice, [not] householders.'
They sat silently pondering.
He said: 'Why now do you sit in silence?
Let us ask you further.'
'Ask,' [they said].
'If you now undergo consecration, will you engage in copulation in this near year, or will you not approach [your wives]?'
'Fie!' they said.
'How shall we, being consecrated, approach, or not approach?'
'Indeed, you will be despisers of brahmins.
The semen of yours that would have become brahmins in this year, you will become mindful of that.'
'Then we will approach, or we will not approach.'
'Indeed, you, being consecrated, will become violators of chastity (avakīrṇin).
The path leading to the gods will certainly not appear;
the path leading to the gods will be concealed.'
'Let us then take refuge in the venerable one himself, so that we may safely attain the end of the year'—so runs the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: sa hovāca dvādaśa ha vai vasūni dīkṣitād utkrāmanti na ha vai dīkṣito 'gnihotraṃ juhuyāt na paurṇamāsena yajñena yajeta nāmāvāsyena asmin vasīta na pitṛyajñena yajeta na tatra gacched yatra manasā jigamiṣet neṣṭyā yajeta na vācā yathākathā cid abhibhāṣeta na mithunaṃ caret nānnāsya yathākāmam upayuñjīta na paśubandhena yajñena yajeta na tatra gacched yatra cakṣuṣā parāpaśyet kṛṣṇājinaṃ vasīta kurīraṃ dhārayet muṣṭī kuryāt aṅguṣṭhaprabhṛtayas tisra ucchrayet mṛgaśṛṅgaṃ gṛhṇīyāt tena kaṣeta atha yasya dīkṣitasya vāg vāyatā syān muṣṭī vā visṛṣṭau sa etāni japet ||
meaning: स होवाच द्वादश ह वै वसूनि दीक्षिताद् उत्क्रामन्ति न ह वै दीक्षितो ऽग्निहोत्रं जुहुयात् न पौर्णमासेन यज्ञेन यजेत नामावास्येन अस्मिन् वसीत न पितृयज्ञेन यजेत न तत्र गच्छेद् यत्र मनसा जिगमिषेत् नेष्ट्या यजेत न वाचा यथाकथा चिद् अभिभाषेत न मिथुनं चरेत् नान्नास्य यथाकामम् उपयुञ्जीत न पशुबन्धेन यज्ञेन यजेत न तत्र गच्छेद् यत्र चक्षुषा परापश्येत् कृष्णाजिनं वसीत कुरीरं धारयेत् मुष्टी कुर्यात् अङ्गुष्ठप्रभृतयस् तिस्र उच्छ्रयेत् मृगशृङ्गं गृह्णीयात् तेन कषेत अथ यस्य दीक्षितस्य वाग् वायता स्यान् मुष्टी वा विसृष्टौ स एतानि जपेत् ||
text_mt:
He said: 'Twelve treasures (vasu) indeed depart from the consecrated one.
The consecrated one should not offer the Agnihotra.
He should not sacrifice with the Full-Moon sacrifice,
nor with the New-Moon sacrifice.
He should dwell in this [sacrificial area].
He should not sacrifice with the Ancestral sacrifice (pitṛyajña).
He should not go where he wishes to go in his mind.
He should not sacrifice with an iṣṭi sacrifice.
He should not converse with his speech just any which way.
He should not engage in copulation.
He should not consume ordinary food according to his desire.
He should not sacrifice with the animal sacrifice (paśubandha).
He should not go where he might look away with his eye.
He should wear a black antelope skin.
He should wear a head-ornament (kurīra).
He should clench his fists.
He should raise the three [fingers] beginning with the thumb.
He should take a black-buck horn;
with that he should scratch himself.
Now, if the consecrated one’s speech should be broken, or his two fists released, he should murmur these [following formulas]':

sanskrit_iast: agnihotraṃ ca mā paurṇamāsaś ca yajñaḥ purastāt pratyañcam ubhau kāmaprau bhūtvā kṣityā sahāviśatām vasatiś ca māmāvāsyaś ca yajñaḥ paścāt prāñcam ubhāv iti samānam manaś ca mā pitṛyajñaś ca yajño dakṣiṇata udañcam ubhāv iti samānam vāk ca meṣṭiś cottarato dakṣiṇāñcam ubhāv iti samānam retaś ca mānnaṃ ceta ūrdhvam ubhāv iti samānam cakṣuś ca mā paśubandhaś ca yajño 'muto 'rvāñcam ubhau kāmaprau bhūtvākṣityā sahāviśatām iti khalu ha vai dīkṣito ya ātmani vasūni dhatte na caivāsya kā canārtir bhavati na ca yajñaviṣkandham upayāty apahanti punarmṛtyum apātyeti punarājātim kāmacāro 'sya sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān dīkṣām upaitīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अग्निहोत्रं च मा पौर्णमासश् च यज्ञः पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चम् उभौ कामप्रौ भूत्वा क्षित्या सहाविशताम् वसतिश् च मामावास्यश् च यज्ञः पश्चात् प्राञ्चम् उभाव् इति समानम् मनश् च मा पितृयज्ञश् च यज्ञो दक्षिणत उदञ्चम् उभाव् इति समानम् वाक् च मेष्टिश् चोत्तरतो दक्षिणाञ्चम् उभाव् इति समानम् रेतश् च मान्नं चेत ऊर्ध्वम् उभाव् इति समानम् चक्षुश् च मा पशुबन्धश् च यज्ञो ऽमुतो ऽर्वाञ्चम् उभौ कामप्रौ भूत्वाक्षित्या सहाविशताम् इति खलु ह वै दीक्षितो य आत्मनि वसूनि धत्ते न चैवास्य का चनार्तिर् भवति न च यज्ञविष्कन्धम् उपयात्य् अपहन्ति पुनर्मृत्युम् अपात्येति पुनराजातिम् कामचारो ऽस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् दीक्षाम् उपैतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
'May both the Agnihotra and the Full-Moon sacrifice, becoming fulfillers of desire, enter me from the east towards the west, together with stability (kṣiti).
Both the dwelling (vasati) and the New-Moon sacrifice from the west towards the east—both [as before].
Both the mind and the Ancestral sacrifice from the south towards the north—both [as before].
Both speech and the iṣṭi sacrifice from the north towards the south—both [as before].
Both semen and food from here upwards—both [as before].
Both the eye and the animal sacrifice, becoming fulfillers of desire, enter me from yonder downwards, together with imperishability (akṣiti).'
Indeed, the consecrated one who thus places the treasures within himself, no distress whatever befalls him, nor does he fall into failure of the sacrifice; he wards off repeated death;
he passes beyond rebirth.
His free movement shines forth in all worlds—who knows thus, and who, knowing thus, undergoes consecration—so runs the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasya dīkṣitasyartumatī jāyā syāt pratisnāvā pratisnāvā sarūpavatsāyā goḥ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsyoddhṛtyābhihiṃkṛtya garbhavedanapuṃsavanaiḥ saṃpātavantaṃ kṛtvā taṃ paraiva prāśnīyāt reto vā annam vṛṣā hiṃkāraḥ evaṃ hīśvarā yā dīkṣitāya dīkṣitā jāyā putraṃ labheteti etenaiva prakrameṇa yajeteti brāhmaṇam || ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇapūrvabhāge tṛtīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
meaning: अथ यस्य दीक्षितस्यर्तुमती जाया स्यात् प्रतिस्नावा प्रतिस्नावा सरूपवत्साया गोः पयसि स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वाभिघार्योद्वास्योद्धृत्याभिहिंकृत्य गर्भवेदनपुंसवनैः संपातवन्तं कृत्वा तं परैव प्राश्नीयात् रेतो वा अन्नम् वृषा हिंकारः एवं हीश्वरा या दीक्षिताय दीक्षिता जाया पुत्रं लभेतेति एतेनैव प्रक्रमेण यजेतेति ब्राह्मणम् || इत्य् अथर्ववेदे गोपथब्राह्मणपूर्वभागे तृतीयः प्रपाठकः ||
text_mt:
Now, if the consecrated one's wife should have her menstrual period: after boiling a mess of cooked grain (sthālīpāka) in the milk of a cow that has a similarly coloured calf and yields milk to another calf, after basting it with ghee, taking it off the fire, dishing it out, uttering hiṃ over it, and endowing it with the residues of the oblations for perception of pregnancy (garbhavedana) and procuring a male child (puṃsavana), she alone should consume it completely.
Food is indeed semen;
the sound hiṃ is the male.
For thus the consecrated wife is able to obtain a son for the consecrated [husband].
Following just this procedure, he should sacrifice—so runs the Brāhmaṇa.

Thus ends the third prapāṭhaka in the first part of the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa of the Atharvaveda.

sanskrit_iast: om ayaṃ vai yajño yo 'yaṃ pavate tam eta īpsanti ye saṃvatsarāya dīkṣante teṣāṃ gṛhapatiḥ prathamo dīkṣate ayaṃ vai loko gṛhapatiḥ asmin vā idaṃ sarvaṃ loke pratiṣṭhitam gṛhapatā u eva sarve sattriṇaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ pratiṣṭhāyā evainaṃ tat pratiṣṭhityai dīkṣante ||
meaning: ओम् अयं वै यज्ञो यो ऽयं पवते तम् एत ईप्सन्ति ये संवत्सराय दीक्षन्ते तेषां गृहपतिः प्रथमो दीक्षते अयं वै लोको गृहपतिः अस्मिन् वा इदं सर्वं लोके प्रतिष्ठितम् गृहपता उ एव सर्वे सत्त्रिणः प्रतिष्ठिताः प्रतिष्ठाया एवैनं तत् प्रतिष्ठित्यै दीक्षन्ते ||
text_mt:
Oṃ. This one who purifies himself is indeed the sacrifice.
Those who consecrate themselves for the year desire to obtain him.
Among them, the master of the house consecrates himself first.
This world is indeed the master of the house.
In this world, indeed, everything here is firmly established.
And on the master of the house, all the session-performers are firmly established.
They consecrate him then for a firm standing, for firm establishment.

sanskrit_iast: atha brahmāṇaṃ dīkṣayati candramā vai brahmādhidaivaṃ mano 'dhyātmam manasaiva tad oṣadhīḥ saṃdadhāti tad yā oṣadhīr veda sa eva brahmauṣadhīs tad anena lokena saṃdadhāti tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokam oṣadhibhir vyāpādayet ucchoṣukā ha syus tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta ||
meaning: अथ ब्रह्माणं दीक्षयति चन्द्रमा वै ब्रह्माधिदैवं मनो ऽध्यात्मम् मनसैव तद् ओषधीः संदधाति तद् या ओषधीर् वेद स एव ब्रह्मौषधीस् तद् अनेन लोकेन संदधाति तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत स यद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो दीक्षेतेमं तं लोकम् ओषधिभिर् व्यापादयेत् उच्छोषुका ह स्युस् तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत ||
text_mt:
Then he initiates the brahman priest. The moon indeed is the brahman priest with respect to the deities; the mind with respect to the self.
Through the mind he thus joins the plants.
He who knows the plants, he indeed is the brahman priest; he joins the plants
with this world.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two.
If another should be initiated between these two, he would deprive this world of plants;
they would indeed wither up.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two. || 2

sanskrit_iast: athodgātāraṃ dīkṣayati ādityo vā udgātādhidaivaṃ cakṣur adhyātmam parjanya ādityaḥ parjanyād adhi vṛṣṭir jāyate vṛṣṭir eva tad oṣadhīḥ saṃdadhāti tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokaṃ varṣeṇa vyāpādayet avarṣukā ha syus tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta ||
meaning: अथोद्गातारं दीक्षयति आदित्यो वा उद्गाताधिदैवं चक्षुर् अध्यात्मम् पर्जन्य आदित्यः पर्जन्याद् अधि वृष्टिर् जायते वृष्टिर् एव तद् ओषधीः संदधाति तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत स यद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो दीक्षेतेमं तं लोकं वर्षेण व्यापादयेत् अवर्षुका ह स्युस् तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत ||
text_mt:
Then he initiates the Udgātṛ.
The sun indeed is the Udgātṛ with respect to the deities; the eye with respect to the self.
Parjanya is the sun.
From Parjanya rain is born.
Rain indeed thus joins the plants.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two.
If another should be initiated between these two, he would deprive this world of rain;
it would not rain.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two. || 3

sanskrit_iast: atha hotāraṃ dīkṣayati agnir vai hotādhidaivaṃ vāg adhyātmam annaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ vācaṃ caiva tad agniṃ cānnena saṃdādhāti tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokam annena vyāpādayet aśanāyukā ha syus tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta ||
meaning: अथ होतारं दीक्षयति अग्निर् वै होताधिदैवं वाग् अध्यात्मम् अन्नं वृष्टिः वाचं चैव तद् अग्निं चान्नेन संदाधाति तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत स यद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो दीक्षेतेमं तं लोकम् अन्नेन व्यापादयेत् अशनायुका ह स्युस् तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत ||
text_mt:
Then he initiates the Hotṛ.
Agni indeed is the Hotṛ with respect to the deities; speech with respect to the self.
Rain is food.
Through food he thus joins speech and Agni.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two.
If another should be initiated between these two, he would deprive this world of food;
they would indeed hunger.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two. || 4

sanskrit_iast: athādhvaryuṃ pratiprasthātā dīkṣayati vāyur vā adhvaryur adhidaivaṃ prāṇo 'dhyātmam annaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ vāyuṃ caiva tat prāṇaṃ cānnena saṃdadhāti tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokaṃ prāṇena vyāpādayet pramāyukā ha syus tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta ||
meaning: अथाध्वर्युं प्रतिप्रस्थाता दीक्षयति वायुर् वा अध्वर्युर् अधिदैवं प्राणो ऽध्यात्मम् अन्नं वृष्टिः वायुं चैव तत् प्राणं चान्नेन संदधाति तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत स यद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो दीक्षेतेमं तं लोकं प्राणेन व्यापादयेत् प्रमायुका ह स्युस् तस्माद् एताव् अन्तरेणान्यो न दीक्षेत ||
text_mt:
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ initiates the Adhvaryu.
Vāyu indeed is the Adhvaryu with respect to the deities; the breath with respect to the self.
Rain is food.
Through food he thus joins Vāyu and the breath.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two.
If another should be initiated between these two, he would deprive this world of breath;
they would indeed die.
Therefore another should not be initiated between these two. || 5

sanskrit_iast: atha brahmaṇe brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaṃ dīkṣayati athodgātre prastotāraṃ dīkṣayati atha hotre maitrāvaruṇaṃ dīkṣayati athādhvaryave pratiprasthātāraṃ neṣṭā dīkṣayati sa hainam anu eteṣāṃ vai navānāṃ kḷptim anv itare kalpante nava vai prāṇāḥ prāṇair yajñas tāyate atha brahmaṇe potāraṃ dīkṣayati athodgātre pratihartāraṃ dīkṣayati atha hotre 'cchāvākaṃ dīkṣayati athādhvaryave neṣṭāram unnetā dīkṣayati sa hainam anu atha brahmaṇa āgnīdhraṃ dīkṣyati athodgātre subrahmaṇyaṃ dīkṣayati atha hotre grāvastutaṃ dīkṣayati atha tamanyaḥ snātako vā brahmacārī vā dīkṣayati na pūtaḥ pāvayed ity āhuḥ saiṣānupūrvaṃ dīkṣā tad ya evaṃ dīkṣante dīkṣiṣyamāṇā eva te sattriṇāṃ prāyaścittaṃ na vindante sattriṇāṃ prāyaścittam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemaḥ kalpate yasminn ardhe dīkṣanta iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथ ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनं दीक्षयति अथोद्गात्रे प्रस्तोतारं दीक्षयति अथ होत्रे मैत्रावरुणं दीक्षयति अथाध्वर्यवे प्रतिप्रस्थातारं नेष्टा दीक्षयति स हैनम् अनु एतेषां वै नवानां कॢप्तिम् अन्व् इतरे कल्पन्ते नव वै प्राणाः प्राणैर् यज्ञस् तायते अथ ब्रह्मणे पोतारं दीक्षयति अथोद्गात्रे प्रतिहर्तारं दीक्षयति अथ होत्रे ऽच्छावाकं दीक्षयति अथाध्वर्यवे नेष्टारम् उन्नेता दीक्षयति स हैनम् अनु अथ ब्रह्मण आग्नीध्रं दीक्ष्यति अथोद्गात्रे सुब्रह्मण्यं दीक्षयति अथ होत्रे ग्रावस्तुतं दीक्षयति अथ तमन्यः स्नातको वा ब्रह्मचारी वा दीक्षयति न पूतः पावयेद् इत्य् आहुः सैषानुपूर्वं दीक्षा तद् य एवं दीक्षन्ते दीक्षिष्यमाणा एव ते सत्त्रिणां प्रायश्चित्तं न विन्दन्ते सत्त्रिणां प्रायश्चित्तम् अनु तस्यार्धस्य योगक्षेमः कल्पते यस्मिन्न् अर्धे दीक्षन्त इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Then he initiates the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin for the brahman priest.
Then he initiates the Prastotṛ for the Udgātṛ.
Then he initiates the Maitrāvaruṇa for the Hotṛ.
Then the Neṣṭṛ initiates the Pratiprasthātṛ for the Adhvaryu,
[and] he [the Pratiprasthātṛ] initiates him [the Neṣṭṛ] in turn.
According to the arrangement of these nine, the others are arranged.
Nine indeed are the vital breaths;
the sacrifice is extended through the vital breaths.
Then he initiates the Potṛ for the brahman priest.
Then he initiates the Pratihartṛ for the Udgātṛ.
Then he initiates the Acchāvāka for the Hotṛ.
Then the Unnetṛ initiates the Neṣṭṛ for the Adhvaryu,
[and] he initiates him in turn.
Then he initiates the Āgnīdhra for the brahman priest.
Then he initiates the Subrahmaṇya for the Udgātṛ.
Then he initiates the Grāvastut for the Hotṛ.
Then another, either a Snātaka or a Brahmacārin, initiates him [the Unnetṛ].
They say: 'One who has been purified should not purify.'
This is the succession of initiation.
Those who are initiated thus, when about to be initiated, do not encounter the need for an expiation of the session-sacrificers.
Following the expiation of the session-sacrificers, the acquisition and preservation of property are established for that region in which they are initiated, so says the Brāhmaṇa. || 6

sanskrit_iast: śraddhayā vai devā dīkṣaṇīyāṃ niramimatāditeḥ prāyaṇīyām somāt krayam viṣṇor ātithyam ādityāt pravargyam svadhāyā upasadaḥ agnīṣomābhyām aupavasathyam ahaḥ prātaryāvadbhyo devebhyaḥ prātaranuvākam vasubhyaḥ prātaḥsavanam rudrebhyo mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam ādityebhyas tṛtīyasavanam varuṇād avabhṛtham aditer udayanīyām mitrāvaruṇābhyām anūbandhyām tvaṣṭus tvāṣṭram devībhyo devikābhyo devatāhavīṃṣi kāmād daśātirātram svargāl lokād udavasānīyām tad vā etad agniṣṭomasya janma sa ya evam etad agniṣṭomasya janma vedāgniṣṭomena sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apy etīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: श्रद्धया वै देवा दीक्षणीयां निरमिमतादितेः प्रायणीयाम् सोमात् क्रयम् विष्णोर् आतिथ्यम् आदित्यात् प्रवर्ग्यम् स्वधाया उपसदः अग्नीषोमाभ्याम् औपवसथ्यम् अहः प्रातर्यावद्भ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रातरनुवाकम् वसुभ्यः प्रातःसवनम् रुद्रेभ्यो माध्यंदिनं सवनम् आदित्येभ्यस् तृतीयसवनम् वरुणाद् अवभृथम् अदितेर् उदयनीयाम् मित्रावरुणाभ्याम् अनूबन्ध्याम् त्वष्टुस् त्वाष्ट्रम् देवीभ्यो देविकाभ्यो देवताहवींषि कामाद् दशातिरात्रम् स्वर्गाल् लोकाद् उदवसानीयाम् तद् वा एतद् अग्निष्टोमस्य जन्म स य एवम् एतद् अग्निष्टोमस्य जन्म वेदाग्निष्टोमेन सात्मा सलोको भूत्वा देवान् अप्य् एतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||

sanskrit_iast: atha yad dīkṣaṇīyayā yajante śraddhām eva tad devīṃ devatāṃ yajante śraddhā devī devatā bhavanti śraddhāyā devyāḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat prāyaṇīyayā yajante 'ditim eva tad devīṃ devatāṃ yajante aditir devī devatā bhavanti adityā devyāḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat krayam upayanti somam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante somo devo devatā bhavanti somasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad ātithyayā yajante viṣṇum eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante viṣṇur devo devatā bhavanti viṣṇor devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat pravargyam upayanty ādityam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante ādityo devo devatā bhavanti ādityasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad upasadam upayanti svadhām eva tad devīṃ devatāṃ yajante svadhā devī devatā bhavanti svadhāyā devyāḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad aupavasathyam ahar upayanty agnīṣomāv eva tad devau devate yajante agnīṣomau devau devate bhavanti agnīṣomayor devatayoḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ye etad upayanti atha yat prātaranuvākam upayanti prātaryāvṇa eva tad devān devatā yajante prātaryāvāṇo devā devatā bhavanti prātaryāvṇāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat prātaḥsavanamupayanti vasūn eva tad devān devatā yajante vasavo devā devatā bhavanti vasūnāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yan mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam upayanti rudrān eva tad devān devatā yajante rudrā devā devatā bhavanti rudrāṇāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yattṛtīyasavanam upayanty ādityān eva tad devān devatā yajante ādityā devā devatā bhavanti ādityānāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad avabhṛtham upayanti varuṇam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante varuṇo devo devatā bhavanti varuṇasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad udayanīyayā yajante 'ditim eva tad devīṃ devatāṃ yajante aditir devī devatā bhavanti adityā devyāḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad anūbandhyayā yajante mitrāvaruṇāv eva tad devau devate yajante mitrāvaruṇau devau devate bhavanti mitrāvaruṇayor devayoḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat tvāṣṭreṇa paśunā yajante tvaṣṭāram eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante tvaṣṭā devo devatā bhavanti tvaṣṭur devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad devikāhavirbhiś caranti yā etā upasatsu bhavanty agniḥ somo viṣṇur iti devyo devikā devatā bhavanti devīnāṃ devikānāṃ devatānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad daśātirātram upayanti kāmam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante kāmo devo devatā bhavanti kāmasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad udavasānīyayā yajante svargam eva tal lokaṃ devaṃ devatāṃ yajante svargo loko devo devatā bhavanti svargasya lokasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti tad vā etad agniṣṭomasya janma sa ya evam etad agniṣṭomasya janma vedāptvaiva tad agniṣṭomaṃ svarge loke pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda agniṣṭomena sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apy etīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथ यद् दीक्षणीयया यजन्ते श्रद्धाम् एव तद् देवीं देवतां यजन्ते श्रद्धा देवी देवता भवन्ति श्रद्धाया देव्याः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् प्रायणीयया यजन्ते ऽदितिम् एव तद् देवीं देवतां यजन्ते अदितिर् देवी देवता भवन्ति अदित्या देव्याः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् क्रयम् उपयन्ति सोमम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते सोमो देवो देवता भवन्ति सोमस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं आदित्यम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते आदित्यो देवो देवता भवन्ति आदित्यस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् उपसदम् उपयन्ति स्वधाम् एव तद् देवीं देवतां यजन्ते स्वधा देवी देवता भवन्ति एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् प्रातरनुवाकम् उपयन्ति प्रातर्याव्ण एव तद् देवान् देवता यजन्ते प्रातर्यावाणो देवा देवता भवन्ति प्रातर्याव्णां देवानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् प्रातःसवनमुपयन्ति
