भवन्ति रुद्राणां देवानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत्तृतीयसवनम् उपयन्त्य् आदित्यान् एव तद् देवान् देवता यजन्ते आदित्या देवा देवता भवन्ति आदित्यानां देवानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् अवभृथम् उपयन्ति वरुणम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते वरुणो देवो देवता भवन्ति वरुणस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् उदयनीयया यजन्ते ऽदितिम् एव तद् देवीं देवतां यजन्ते अदितिर् देवी देवता भवन्ति अदित्या देव्याः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् अनूबन्ध्यया यजन्ते मित्रावरुणाव् एव तद् देवौ देवते यजन्ते मित्रावरुणौ देवौ देवते भवन्ति मित्रावरुणयोर् देवयोः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् त्वाष्ट्रेण पशुना यजन्ते त्वष्टारम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते त्वष्टा देवो देवता भवन्ति त्वष्टुर् देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् देविकाहविर्भिश् चरन्ति या एता उपसत्सु भवन्त्य् अग्निः सोमो विष्णुर् इति देव्यो देविका देवता भवन्ति देवीनां देविकानां देवतानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् दशातिरात्रम् उपयन्ति कामम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते कामो देवो देवता भवन्ति कामस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् उदवसानीयया यजन्ते स्वर्गम् एव तल् लोकं देवं देवतां यजन्ते स्वर्गो लोको देवो देवता भवन्ति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति तद् वा एतद् अग्निष्टोमस्य जन्म स य एवम् एतद् अग्निष्टोमस्य जन्म वेदाप्त्वैव तद् अग्निष्टोमं स्वर्गे लोके प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं वेद अग्निष्टोमेन सात्मा सलोको भूत्वा देवान् अप्य् एतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Now, when they sacrifice with the consecration offering, it is faith, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become faith, the divine deity.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with faith, the divine deity.
Now, when they sacrifice with the introductory offering, it is Aditi, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become Aditi, the divine deity.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Aditi, the divine deity.
Now, when they undertake the purchase, it is Soma, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become Soma, the divine deity.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Soma, the divine deity.
Now, when they sacrifice with the hospitality offering, it is Viṣṇu, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become Viṣṇu, the divine deity.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Viṣṇu, the divine deity.
Now, when they undertake the Pravargya, it is the Āditya, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become the Āditya, the divine deity.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with the Āditya, the divine deity.
Now, when they undertake the Upasad, it is Svadhā, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become Svadhā, the divine deity.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Svadhā, the divine deity.
Now, when they undertake the day of fasting, it is Agni and Soma, the two divine deities, that they sacrifice to.
They become Agni and Soma, the two divine deities.
Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Agni and Soma, the two divine deities.
Now, when they undertake the morning recitation, it is the early-faring gods, the deity, that they sacrifice to.
They become the early-faring gods, the deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with the early-faring gods.

Now, when they undertake the morning soma-pressing, it is the Vasus, the gods, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become the Vasus, the gods, as deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with the Vasus, the gods.

Now, when they undertake the midday soma-pressing, it is the Rudras, the gods, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become the Rudras, the gods, as deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with the Rudras, the gods.

Now, when they undertake the evening soma-pressing, it is the Ādityas, the gods, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become the Ādityas, the gods, as deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with the Ādityas, the gods.

Now, when they undertake the purificatory bath, it is Varuṇa, the god, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become Varuṇa, the god, as deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Varuṇa, the god.

Now, when they sacrifice with the concluding offering, it is Aditi, the divine deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become Aditi, the divine deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Aditi, the divine deity.

Now, when they sacrifice with the barren cow offering, it is Mitra and Varuṇa, the two divine deities, that they sacrifice to.

They become Mitra and Varuṇa, the two divine deities.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Mitra and Varuṇa, the two gods.

Now, when they sacrifice with the animal victim for Tvaṣṭṛ, it is Tvaṣṭṛ, the god, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become Tvaṣṭṛ, the god, as deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Tvaṣṭṛ, the god.

Now, when they perform [the sacrifice] with the oblations to the minor goddesses, which are present at the Upasads—namely, Agni, Soma, and Viṣṇu—they become the divine minor goddesses, as deities.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with the divine minor goddesses, the deities.

Now, when they undertake the ten-day Atirātra, it is Desire, the god, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become Desire, the god, as deity.

Those who undertake this attain union and the same world with Desire, the god.

Now, when they sacrifice with the final departure offering, it is the heavenly world, the god, as deity, that they sacrifice to.

They become the heavenly world, the god, as deity.

sanskrit_iast: ahorātrābhyāṃ vai devāḥ prāyaṇīyam atirātraṃ niramimata ardhamāsebhyaś caturviṃśam ahaḥ brahmaṇo 'bhiplavam kṣatrāt pṛṣṭhyam agner abhijitam adbhyaḥ svarasāmnaḥ sūryād viṣuvantam uktā āvṛttāḥ svarasāmānaḥ indrād viśvajitam uktau pṛṣṭhyabhiplavau mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ gavāyuṣī viśvebhyo devebhyo daśarātram digbhyo dāśarātrikaṃ pṛṣṭhyaṃ ṣaḍaham ebhyo lokebhyaś chandomaṃ tryaham saṃvatsarād daśamam ahaḥ prajāpater mahāvratam svargāl lokād udayanīyam atirātram tad vā etat saṃvatsarasya janma sa ya evam etat saṃvatsarasya janma veda saṃvatsareṇa sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apy etīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अहोरात्राभ्यां वै देवाः प्रायणीयम् अतिरात्रं निरमिमत अर्धमासेभ्यश् चतुर्विंशम् अहः ब्रह्मणो ऽभिप्लवम् क्षत्रात् पृष्ठ्यम् अग्नेर् अभिजितम् अद्भ्यः स्वरसाम्नः सूर्याद् विषुवन्तम् उक्ता आवृत्ताः स्वरसामानः इन्द्राद् विश्वजितम् उक्तौ पृष्ठ्यभिप्लवौ मित्रावरुणाभ्यां गवायुषी विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो दशरात्रम् दिग्भ्यो दाशरात्रिकं पृष्ठ्यं षडहम् एभ्यो लोकेभ्यश् छन्दोमं त्र्यहम् संवत्सराद् दशमम् अहः प्रजापतेर् महाव्रतम् स्वर्गाल् लोकाद् उदयनीयम् अतिरात्रम् तद् वा एतत् संवत्सरस्य जन्म स य एवम् एतत् संवत्सरस्य जन्म वेद संवत्सरेण सात्मा सलोको भूत्वा देवान् अप्य् एतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||

sanskrit_iast: atha yat prāyaṇīyam atirātram upayanty ahorātrāv eva tad devau devate yajante ahorātrau devau devate bhavanti ahorātrayor devayoḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yac caturviṃśam ahar upayanty ardhamāsān eva tad devān devatā yajante ardhamāsā devā devatā bhavanti ardhamāsānāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad abhiplavam upayanti brahmāṇam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante brahmā devo devatā bhavanti brahmaṇo devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat pṛṣṭhyam upayanti kṣatram eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante kṣatraṃ devo devatā bhavanti kṣatrasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad abhijitam upayanty agnim eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante agnir devo devatā bhavanti agner devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yat svarasāmna upayanty eva tad devīr devatā yajanta āpo devyo devatā bhavanti apāṃ devīnāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad viṣuvantam upayanti sūryam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante sūryo devo devatā bhavanti sūryasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti uktā āvṛttāḥ svarasāmānaḥ atha yad viśvajita mupayantīndram eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante indro devo devatā bhavanti indrasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti uktau pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau atha yad gavāyuṣī upayanti mitrāvaruṇāv eva tad devau devate yajante mitrāvaruṇau devau devate bhavanti mitrāvaruṇayor devayoḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad daśarātram upayanti viśvān eva tad devān devatā yajante viśve devā devatā bhavanti viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad dāśarātrikaṃ pṛṣṭhyaṃ ṣaḍaham upayanti diśa eva tad devīr devatā yajante diśo devyo devatā bhavanti diśāṃ devīnāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yac chandomaṃ tryaham upayantīmān eva tal lokān devān devatā yajante ime lokā devā devatā bhavanti eṣāṃ lokānāṃ devānāṃ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad daśamam ahar upayanti saṃvatsaram eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante saṃvatsaro devo devatā bhavanti saṃvatsarasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yan mahāvratam upayanti prajāpatim eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante prajāpatir devo devatā bhavanti prajāpater devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti atha yad udayanīyam atirātram upayanti svargam eva tal lokaṃ devaṃ devatāṃ yajante svargo loko devo devatā bhavanti svargasya lokasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti tad vā etat saṃvatsarasya janma sa ya evam etat saṃvatsarasya janma vedāptvaiva tat saṃvatsaraṃ svarge loke pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda saṃvatsareṇa sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apy etīti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथ यत् प्रायणीयम् अतिरात्रम् उपयन्त्य् अहोरात्राव् एव तद् देवौ देवते यजन्ते अहोरात्रौ देवौ देवते भवन्ति अहोरात्रयोर् देवयोः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यच् चतुर्विंशम् अहर् उपयन्त्य् अर्धमासान् एव तद् देवान् देवता यजन्ते अर्धमासा देवा देवता भवन्ति अर्धमासानां देवानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् अभिप्लवम् उपयन्ति ब्रह्माणम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते ब्रह्मा देवो देवता भवन्ति ब्रह्मणो देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् पृष्ठ्यम् उपयन्ति क्षत्रम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते क्षत्रं देवो देवता भवन्ति क्षत्रस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् अभिजितम् उपयन्त्य् अग्निम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते अग्निर् देवो देवता भवन्ति अग्नेर् देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यत् स्वरसाम्न उपयन्त्य् एव तद् देवीर् देवता यजन्त आपो देव्यो देवता भवन्ति अपां देवीनां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् विषुवन्तम् उपयन्ति सूर्यम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते सूर्यो देवो देवता भवन्ति सूर्यस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति उक्ता आवृत्ताः स्वरसामानः अथ यद् विश्वजित मुपयन्तीन्द्रम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते इन्द्रो देवो देवता भवन्ति इन्द्रस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति उक्तौ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ अथ यद् गवायुषी उपयन्ति मित्रावरुणाव् एव तद् देवौ देवते यजन्ते मित्रावरुणौ देवौ देवते भवन्ति मित्रावरुणयोर् देवयोः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् दशरात्रम् उपयन्ति विश्वान् एव तद् देवान् देवता यजन्ते विश्वे देवा देवता भवन्ति विश्वेषां देवानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् दाशरात्रिकं पृष्ठ्यं षडहम् उपयन्ति दिश एव तद् देवीर् देवता यजन्ते दिशो देव्यो देवता भवन्ति दिशां देवीनां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यच् छन्दोमं त्र्यहम् उपयन्तीमान् एव तल् लोकान् देवान् देवता यजन्ते इमे लोका देवा देवता भवन्ति एषां लोकानां देवानां सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् दशमम् अहर् उपयन्ति संवत्सरम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते संवत्सरो देवो देवता भवन्ति संवत्सरस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यन् महाव्रतम् उपयन्ति प्रजापतिम् एव तद् देवं देवतां यजन्ते प्रजापतिर् देवो देवता भवन्ति प्रजापतेर् देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति अथ यद् उदयनीयम् अतिरात्रम् उपयन्ति स्वर्गम् एव तल् लोकं देवं देवतां यजन्ते स्वर्गो लोको देवो देवता भवन्ति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य देवस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति तद् वा एतत् संवत्सरस्य जन्म स य एवम् एतत् संवत्सरस्य जन्म वेदाप्त्वैव तत् संवत्सरं स्वर्गे लोके प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं वेद संवत्सरेण सात्मा सलोको भूत्वा देवान् अप्य् एतीति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Now, when they undertake the introductory atirātra, they thereby sacrifice to Day and Night as two divine deities. Day and Night become their divine deities. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the two divine deities Day and Night.
Now, when they undertake the twenty-fourth day, they thereby sacrifice to the Half-months as divine deities. The Half-months become their divine deities. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deities, the Half-months.
Now, when they undertake the abhiplava, they thereby sacrifice to Brahman as a divine deity. Brahman becomes their divine deity. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity Brahman.
Now, when they undertake the pṛṣṭhya, they thereby sacrifice to Dominion as a divine deity. Dominion becomes their divine deity. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity Dominion.
Now, when they undertake the abhijit, they thereby sacrifice to Agni as a divine deity. Agni becomes their divine deity. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity Agni.
Now, when they undertake the svarasāman [days], they thereby sacrifice to the Waters as divine deities. The Waters become their divine deities. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deities, the Waters.
Now, when they undertake the viṣuvant, they thereby sacrifice to Sūrya as a divine deity. Sūrya becomes their divine deity. Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity Sūrya.
The reversed svarasāman [days] have been explained.
Now, when they undertake the viśvajit, they thereby sacrifice to Indra as a divine deity. Indra becomes their divine deity.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity Indra.

The pṛṣṭhya and abhiplava have been explained.

Now, when they undertake the go and āyus [days], they thereby sacrifice to Mitra and Varuṇa as two divine deities.

Mitra and Varuṇa become their two divine deities.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the two divine deities Mitra and Varuṇa.

Now, when they undertake the ten-day period, they thereby sacrifice to the All-Gods as divine deities.

The All-Gods become their divine deities.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deities, the All-Gods.

Now, when they undertake the pṛṣṭhya six-day period belonging to the ten-day rite, they thereby sacrifice to the Quarters as divine deities.

The Quarters become their divine deities.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deities, the Quarters.

Now, when they undertake the chandoma three-day period, they thereby sacrifice to these worlds as divine deities.

These worlds become their divine deities.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deities, these worlds.

Now, when they undertake the tenth day, they thereby sacrifice to the year as a divine deity.

The year becomes their divine deity.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity, the year.

Now, when they undertake the mahāvrata, they thereby sacrifice to Prajāpati as a divine deity.

Prajāpati becomes their divine deity.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity Prajāpati.

Now, when they undertake the concluding atirātra, they thereby sacrifice to the heavenly world as a divine deity.

The heavenly world becomes their divine deity.

Those who undertake this attain union with and co-residence in the world of the divine deity, the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣa saṃvastaro 'dhidaivaṃ cādhyātmaṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ sa ya evam etat saṃvatsaram adhidaivaṃ cādhyātmaṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: स वा एष संवस्तरो ऽधिदैवं चाध्यात्मं च प्रतिष्ठितः स य एवम् एतत् संवत्सरम् अधिदैवं चाध्यात्मं च प्रतिष्ठितं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
That indeed is this birth of the year.

He who thus knows this birth of the year, having obtained that very year, establishes himself firmly in the heavenly world.

He establishes himself firmly with offspring and cattle, who knows thus.

Having become of the same self and of the same world with the year, he goes to the gods: such is the Brāhmaṇa. [10]

That very year is established with regard to the divine and with regard to the self.
He who thus knows this year established with regard to the divine and with regard to the self stands firm.
He stands firm with offspring and cattle, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣa saṃvatsaro bṛhatīm abhisaṃpannaḥ dvāv akṣarāv ahnāṃ ṣaḍahau dvau pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau gavāyuṣī daśarātras tathā khalu ṣaṭtriṃśad saṃpadyante ṣaṭtriṃśadavadānā gauḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣarā bṛhatī bārhato vai svargo lokaḥ bṛhatyā vai devāḥ svarge loke yajante bṛhatyā svarge loke pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: स वा एष संवत्सरो बृहतीम् अभिसंपन्नः द्वाव् अक्षराव् अह्नां षडहौ द्वौ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ गवायुषी दशरात्रस् तथा खलु षट्त्रिंशद् संपद्यन्ते षट्त्रिंशदवदाना गौः षट्त्रिंशदक्षरा बृहती बार्हतो वै स्वर्गो लोकः बृहत्या वै देवाः स्वर्गे लोके यजन्ते बृहत्या स्वर्गे लोके प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
That very year corresponds to the bṛhatī [metre].
Two syllables are the two six-day periods of days, the pṛṣṭhya and abhiplava,
the go and āyus, and the ten-day period.
Thus indeed thirty-six are made up.
The cow has thirty-six portions of offering.
The bṛhatī has thirty-six syllables.
The heavenly world indeed belongs to the bṛhatī.
By means of the bṛhatī, the gods sacrifice in the heavenly world.
By means of the bṛhatī, he stands firm in the heavenly world.
He stands firm with offspring and cattle, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣa saṃvatsaras trimahāvrataḥ caturviṃśe mahāvrataṃ viṣuvati mahāvrataṃ mahāvrata eva mahāvratam taṃ ha smaitam evaṃvidvāṃsaḥ pūrve trimahāvratam upayanti te tejasvina āsaṃt satyavādinaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ ya enam adya tathopeyur yathāmapātram udaka āsikte nirmṛtyed evaṃ yajamānā nirmṛtyerann upary upayanti tathā hāsya satyena tapasā vratena cābhijitam avaruddhaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: स वा एष संवत्सरस् त्रिमहाव्रतः चतुर्विंशे महाव्रतं विषुवति महाव्रतं महाव्रत एव महाव्रतम् तं ह स्मैतम् एवंविद्वांसः पूर्वे त्रिमहाव्रतम् उपयन्ति ते तेजस्विन आसंत् सत्यवादिनः संशितव्रताः य एनम् अद्य तथोपेयुर् यथामपात्रम् उदक आसिक्ते निर्मृत्येद् एवं यजमाना निर्मृत्येरन्न् उपर्य् उपयन्ति तथा हास्य सत्येन तपसा व्रतेन चाभिजितम् अवरुद्धं भवति य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
That very year has three Mahāvratas:
a Mahāvrata on the twenty-fourth [day], a Mahāvrata on the viṣuvant, and a Mahāvrata on the Mahāvrata [day] itself.
Ancient people, knowing thus, used to undertake it as having three Mahāvratas.
They were radiant, truthful in speech, and strict in observances.
If people today were to undertake it thus, just as an unbaked pot dissolves when water is poured into it, so the sacrificers would dissolve; they undertake [it] on top [of each other].
Thus, by truth, ascetic heat, and observance, it is won and secured for him who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: atha yac caturviṃśam ahar upetyānupetya viṣuvantaṃ mahāvratam upeyāt katham anāgūrtyai bhavatīti yam evāmuṃ purastād viṣuvato 'tirātram upayanti teneti brūyāt abhiplavāt pṛṣṭhyo nirmitaḥ pṛṣṭhyād abhijit abhijitaḥ svarasāmānaḥ svarasāmabhyo viṣuvān viṣuvataḥ svarasāmānaḥ svarasāmabhyo viśvajit viśvajitaḥ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau pṛṣṭhyābhiplavābhyāṃ gavāyuṣī gavāyurbhyāṃ daśarātraḥ daśarātrān mahāvratam mahāvratād udayanīyo 'tirātraḥ udayanīyo 'tirātraḥ svargāya lokāyānnādyāya pratiṣṭhityai ||
meaning: अथ यच् चतुर्विंशम् अहर् उपेत्यानुपेत्य विषुवन्तं महाव्रतम् उपेयात् कथम् अनागूर्त्यै भवतीति यम् एवामुं पुरस्ताद् विषुवतो ऽतिरात्रम् उपयन्ति तेनेति ब्रूयात् अभिप्लवात् पृष्ठ्यो निर्मितः पृष्ठ्याद् अभिजित् अभिजितः स्वरसामानः स्वरसामभ्यो विषुवान् विषुवतः स्वरसामानः स्वरसामभ्यो विश्वजित् विश्वजितः पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवाभ्यां गवायुषी गवायुर्भ्यां दशरात्रः दशरात्रान् महाव्रतम् महाव्रताद् उदयनीयो ऽतिरात्रः उदयनीयो ऽतिरात्रः स्वर्गाय लोकायान्नाद्याय प्रतिष्ठित्यै ||

sanskrit_iast: atha yac caturviṃśam ahar upetyānupetya viṣuvantaṃ mahāvratam upeyāt katham anāgūrtyai bhavatīti yam evāmuṃ purastād viṣuvato 'tirātram upayanti teneti brūyāt abhiplavāt pṛṣṭhyo nirmitaḥ pṛṣṭhyād abhijit abhijitaḥ svarasāmānaḥ svarasāmabhyo viṣuvān viṣuvataḥ svarasamānaḥ svarasāmabhyo viśvajit viśvajitaḥ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau pṛṣṭhyābhiplavābhyāṃ gavāyuṣī gavāyurbhyāṃ daśarātraḥ atha ha devebhyo mahāvrataṃ na tasthe katham ūrdhvai stomair viṣuvantam upāgātāvṛttair mām iti te devā ihasāmivāsur upa taṃ yajñakratuṃ jānīmo ca ūrdhvastomo yenaitad ahar avāpnuyāmeti tata etaṃ dvādaśarātram ūrdhvastomaṃ dadṛśus tam āharan tenāyajanta tata ebhyo 'tiṣṭhan tiṣṭhati hāsmai mahāvratam pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: अथ यच् चतुर्विंशम् अहर् उपेत्यानुपेत्य विषुवन्तं महाव्रतम् उपेयात् कथम् अनागूर्त्यै भवतीति यम् एवामुं पुरस्ताद् विषुवतो ऽतिरात्रम् उपयन्ति तेनेति ब्रूयात् अभिप्लवात् पृष्ठ्यो निर्मितः पृष्ठ्याद् अभिजित् अभिजितः स्वरसामानः स्वरसामभ्यो विषुवान् विषुवतः स्वरसमानः स्वरसामभ्यो विश्वजित् विश्वजितः पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवाभ्यां गवायुषी गवायुर्भ्यां दशरात्रः अथ ह देवेभ्यो महाव्रतं न तस्थे कथम् ऊर्ध्वै स्तोमैर् विषुवन्तम् उपागातावृत्तैर् माम् इति ते देवा इहसामिवासुर् उप तं यज्ञक्रतुं जानीमो च ऊर्ध्वस्तोमो येनैतद् अहर् अवाप्नुयामेति तत एतं द्वादशरात्रम् ऊर्ध्वस्तोमं ददृशुस् तम् आहरन् तेनायजन्त तत एभ्यो ऽतिष्ठन् तिष्ठति हास्मै महाव्रतम् प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं वेद ||

sanskrit_iast: atha yac caturviṃśam ahar upetyānupetya viṣuvantaṃ mahāvratam upeyāt katham anāgūrtyai bhavatīti yam evāmuṃ purastād viṣuvato 'tirātram upayanti teneti brūyāt tad āhuḥ kati saṃvatsarasya parāñcy ahāni bhavanti katy arvāñci tad yāni sakṛtsakṛd upayanti tāni parāñci atha yāni punaḥpunar upayanti tāny arvāñcīty evaināny upāsīran ṣaḍahayor hy āvṛttim anvāvartante ||
meaning: अथ यच् चतुर्विंशम् अहर् उपेत्यानुपेत्य विषुवन्तं महाव्रतम् उपेयात् कथम् अनागूर्त्यै भवतीति यम् एवामुं पुरस्ताद् विषुवतो ऽतिरात्रम् उपयन्ति तेनेति ब्रूयात् तद् आहुः कति संवत्सरस्य पराञ्च्य् अहानि भवन्ति कत्य् अर्वाञ्चि तद् यानि सकृत्सकृद् उपयन्ति तानि पराञ्चि अथ यानि पुनःपुनर् उपयन्ति तान्य् अर्वाञ्चीत्य् एवैनान्य् उपासीरन् षडहयोर् ह्य् आवृत्तिम् अन्वावर्तन्ते ||
text_mt:
Now, as to this: when one undertakes the twenty-fourth day, and not undertaking the viṣuvant, undertakes the Mahāvrata, how does it not result in an incomplete vow?
One should say: 'By that very atirātra which they undertake before the viṣuvant.'
Regarding this they say: 'How many days of the year face forward, how many face backward?'
In that regard, those which they undertake only once, those face forward;
and those which they undertake again and again, those face backward; thus they should regard them,
for they turn following the repetition of the two six-day periods.

sanskrit_iast: atha yac caturviṃśam ahar upetyānupetya viṣuvantaṃ mahāvratam upeyāt katham anāgūrtyai bhavatīti yam evāmuṃ purastād viṣuvato 'tirātram upayanti teneti brūyāt abhiplavaṃ purastād viṣuvataḥ pūrvam upayanti pṛṣṭyam upariṣṭāt pitā vā abhiplavaḥ putraḥ pṛṣṭhyas tasmāt pūrve vayasi putrāḥ pitaram upajīvanti pṛṣṭhyaṃ paścād viṣuvataḥ pūrvam upayanty abhiplavam upariṣṭāt pitā vā abhiplavaḥ putraḥ pṛṣṭhyas tasmād uttame vayasi putrān pitopajīvati ya evaṃ veda tad apy etad ṛcoktaṃ śatam in nu śarado anti devā yatrā naś cakrā jarasaṃ tanūnām | putrāso yatra pitaro bhavanti mā no madhyā rīriṣatāyur gantoḥ iti upa ha vā enaṃ pūrve vayasi putrāḥ pitaram upajīvanty upottame vayasi putrān pitopajīvati ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: अथ यच् चतुर्विंशम् अहर् उपेत्यानुपेत्य विषुवन्तं महाव्रतम् उपेयात् कथम् अनागूर्त्यै भवतीति यम् एवामुं पुरस्ताद् विषुवतो ऽतिरात्रम् उपयन्ति तेनेति ब्रूयात् अभिप्लवं पुरस्ताद् विषुवतः पूर्वम् उपयन्ति पृष्ट्यम् उपरिष्टात् पिता वा अभिप्लवः पुत्रः पृष्ठ्यस् तस्मात् पूर्वे वयसि पुत्राः पितरम् उपजीवन्ति पृष्ठ्यं पश्चाद् विषुवतः पूर्वम् उपयन्त्य् अभिप्लवम् उपरिष्टात् पिता वा अभिप्लवः पुत्रः पृष्ठ्यस् तस्माद् उत्तमे वयसि पुत्रान् पितोपजीवति य एवं वेद तद् अप्य् एतद् ऋचोक्तं शतम् इन् नु शरदो अन्ति देवा यत्रा नश् चक्रा जरसं तनूनाम् | पुत्रासो यत्र पितरो भवन्ति मा नो मध्या रीरिषतायुर् गन्तोः इति उप ह वा एनं पूर्वे वयसि पुत्राः पितरम् उपजीवन्त्य् उपोत्तमे वयसि पुत्रान् पितोपजीवति य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
Now, as to this: when one undertakes the twenty-fourth day, and not undertaking the viṣuvant, undertakes the Mahāvrata, how does it not result in an incomplete vow?
One should say: 'By that very atirātra which they undertake before the viṣuvant.'
Before the viṣuvant, they undertake the abhiplava first,
and the pṛṣṭhya later.
The abhiplava is the father, the pṛṣṭhya the son;
therefore in early age, sons live dependent upon the father.
After the viṣuvant, they undertake the pṛṣṭhya first, and the abhiplava later.
The abhiplava is the father, the pṛṣṭhya the son;
therefore in later age, the father lives dependent upon the sons, for him who knows thus.
Regarding this, it is also said by the Ṛgvedic verse:
'A hundred autumns indeed are before us, O gods, wherein you have ordained the aging of our bodies, / where sons become fathers; do not harm our life-span midway in our journey.'
Indeed, in early age the sons live dependent upon him, the father, and in later age he, the father, lives dependent upon the sons, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: atha haiṣa mahāsuparṇas tasya yān purastād viṣuvataḥ ṣaṇmāsān upayanti sa dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ atha yān āvṛttān upariṣṭāt ṣaḍ upayanti sa uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ ātmā vai saṃvatsarasya viṣuvān aṅgāni pakṣau yatra vā ātmā tat pakṣau yatra vai pakṣau tad ātmā na vā ātmā pakṣāv atiricyate no pakṣāv ātmānam atiricyete iti evam u haiva tad apareṣāṃ sviditamahnāṃ pareṣām ity apareṣāṃ caiva pareṣāṃ ceti brūyāt ||
meaning: अथ हैष महासुपर्णस् तस्य यान् पुरस्ताद् विषुवतः षण्मासान् उपयन्ति स दक्षिणः पक्षः अथ यान् आवृत्तान् उपरिष्टात् षड् उपयन्ति स उत्तरः पक्षः आत्मा वै संवत्सरस्य विषुवान् अङ्गानि पक्षौ यत्र वा आत्मा तत् पक्षौ यत्र वै पक्षौ तद् आत्मा न वा आत्मा पक्षाव् अतिरिच्यते नो पक्षाव् आत्मानम् अतिरिच्येते इति एवम् उ हैव तद् अपरेषां स्विदितमह्नां परेषाम् इत्य् अपरेषां चैव परेषां चेति ब्रूयात् ||

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaro 'tha haitad ahar avāpnuyāmeti yad vaiṣuvatam apareṣāṃ sviditamahāṃ pareṣām iti apareṣāṃ caiva pareṣāṃ ceti brūyāt ātmā vai saṃvatsarasya viṣuvān aṅgāni māsāḥ yatra vā ātmā tad aṅgāni yatrāṅgāni tad ātmā na vā ātmāṅgāny atiricyate no 'ṅgāny ātmānam atiricyanta iti evam u haiva tad apareṣāṃ sviditamahnāṃ pareṣām ity apareṣāṃ caiva pareṣāṃ ceti brūyāt sa vā eṣa saṃvatsaraḥ ||
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरो ऽथ हैतद् अहर् अवाप्नुयामेति यद् वैषुवतम् अपरेषां स्विदितमहां परेषाम् इति अपरेषां चैव परेषां चेति ब्रूयात् आत्मा वै संवत्सरस्य विषुवान् अङ्गानि मासाः यत्र वा आत्मा तद् अङ्गानि यत्राङ्गानि तद् आत्मा न वा आत्माङ्गान्य् अतिरिच्यते नो ऽङ्गान्य् आत्मानम् अतिरिच्यन्त इति एवम् उ हैव तद् अपरेषां स्विदितमह्नां परेषाम् इत्य् अपरेषां चैव परेषां चेति ब्रूयात् स वा एष संवत्सरः ||
text_mt:
Regarding this they say: 'Since the year consists of twelve months, how then may we reach this day?
Does the day of the viṣuvant belong to the earlier days or to the later?'
One should say: 'It belongs both to the earlier and to the later.'
The viṣuvant is the body of the year, the months are its limbs.
Where the body is, there are the limbs;
where the limbs are, there is the body;
the body does not exceed the limbs, nor do the limbs exceed the body.
Just so, [if asked] whether it belongs to the earlier or later days, one should say: 'It belongs both to the earlier and to the later.'
Such indeed is this year.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ katham ubhayatojyotiṣo 'bhiplavā anyataratojyotiḥ pṛṣṭhya iti ubhayatojyotiṣo vā ime lokā agnineta ādityenāmuta iti eṣa ha vā eteṣāṃ jyotir ya enaṃ pramṛdīva tapati devacakre ha vā ete pṛṣṭhyapratiṣṭhite pāpmānaṃ tṛṃhatī pariplavete tad ya evaṃviduṣāṃ dīkṣitānāṃ pāpakaṃ kīrtayad ete evāsya tad devacakre śiraś chindataḥ daśarātram uddhiḥ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau cakre daśarātram uddhiṃ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau cakre tantraṃ kurvīteti ha smāha vāsyus tayo stotrāṇi ca śastrāṇi ca saṃcāreyat yaḥ saṃcārayet tasmād ime puruṣe prāṇā nānā santa ekodayāc charīram adhivasati yan na saṃcārayet pramāyuko ha yajamānaḥ syāt eṣa ha vai pramāyuko yo 'ndho vā badhiro vā navāgniṣṭomā māsi saṃpadyante nava vai prāṇāḥ prāṇair yajñas tāyate ekaviṃśatir ukthyāḥ eka ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśī annaṃ vā ukthyaḥ vīryaṃ ṣoḍaśy eva tathā rūḍhvā svargaṃ lokam adhyārohanti ||
meaning: तद् आहुः कथम् उभयतोज्योतिषो ऽभिप्लवा अन्यतरतोज्योतिः पृष्ठ्य इति उभयतोज्योतिषो वा इमे लोका अग्निनेत आदित्येनामुत इति एष ह वा एतेषां ज्योतिर् य एनं प्रमृदीव तपति देवचक्रे ह वा एते पृष्ठ्यप्रतिष्ठिते पाप्मानं तृंहती परिप्लवेते तद् य एवंविदुषां दीक्षितानां पापकं कीर्तयद् एते एवास्य तद् देवचक्रे शिरश् छिन्दतः दशरात्रम् उद्धिः पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ चक्रे दशरात्रम् उद्धिं पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ चक्रे तन्त्रं कुर्वीतेति ह स्माह वास्युस् तयो स्तोत्राणि च शस्त्राणि च संचारेयत् यः संचारयेत् तस्माद् इमे पुरुषे प्राणा नाना सन्त एकोदयाच् छरीरम् अधिवसति यन् न संचारयेत् प्रमायुको ह यजमानः स्यात् एष ह वै प्रमायुको यो ऽन्धो वा बधिरो वा नवाग्निष्टोमा मासि संपद्यन्ते नव वै प्राणाः प्राणैर् यज्ञस् तायते एकविंशतिर् उक्थ्याः एक उक्थ्यः षोडशी अन्नं वा उक्थ्यः वीर्यं षोडश्य् एव तथा रूढ्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् अध्यारोहन्ति ||
text_mt:
Regarding this they say: 'Why do the abhiplavas have light on both sides, while the pṛṣṭhya has light on only one side?'
[The answer is:] 'These worlds have light on both sides—by Agni on this side, by Āditya on that side.'
This indeed is their light, which burns him as if crushing him.
These two are divine wheels resting upon the pṛṣṭhya, which revolve crushing evil.
Therefore, if anyone speaks ill of consecrated persons who know thus, these two divine wheels sever his head.
The ten-night rite is the frame;
the pṛṣṭhya and the abhiplava are the two wheels.
'One should make the ten-night rite the frame, and the pṛṣṭhya and abhiplava the two wheels of the ritual arrangement,' so Vāsyu used to say.
One should cause the stotras and śastras of the two to interchange.
Whoever causes them to interchange—therefore these breaths in man, being distinct, dwell within the body arising from a single source; if he should not cause them to interchange, the sacrificer would likely perish.
Likely to perish indeed is he who is blind or deaf.
Nine agniṣṭomas are completed in a month;
nine indeed are the breaths;
the sacrifice is spread by the breaths.
There are twenty-one ukthyas;
one ukthya is a ṣoḍaśin.
The ukthya is food;
the ṣoḍaśin is vigor.
Thus having ascended, they mount up to the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: athāto 'hnām adhyārohaḥ prāyaṇīyenātirātreṇodayanīyam atirātram adhyārohanti caturviṃśena mahāvratam abhiplavena param abhiplavam pṛṣṭhyena paraṃ pṛṣṭhyam abhijitābhijitaṃ svarasāmabhiḥ parānt svarasāmānaḥ athaitad ahar avāpnuyāmeti yad vaiṣuvatam apareṣāṃ sviditamahnāṃ pareṣām ity apareṣāṃ caiva pareṣāṃ ceti brūyāt sa vā eṣa saṃvatsaraḥ ||
meaning: अथातो ऽह्नाम् अध्यारोहः प्रायणीयेनातिरात्रेणोदयनीयम् अतिरात्रम् अध्यारोहन्ति चतुर्विंशेन महाव्रतम् अभिप्लवेन परम् अभिप्लवम् पृष्ठ्येन परं पृष्ठ्यम् अभिजिताभिजितं स्वरसामभिः परान्त् स्वरसामानः अथैतद् अहर् अवाप्नुयामेति यद् वैषुवतम् अपरेषां स्विदितमह्नां परेषाम् इत्य् अपरेषां चैव परेषां चेति ब्रूयात् स वा एष संवत्सरः ||

sanskrit_iast: athāto 'hnāṃ nivāhaḥ prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraś caturviṃśāyāhne nivahati caturviṃśam ahar abhiplavāya abhiplavaḥ pṛṣṭhyāya pṛṣṭhyo 'bhijite abhijit svarasāmabhyaḥ svarasāmāno viṣuvate viṣuvānt svarasāmabhyaḥ svarasāmano viśvajite viśvajit pṛṣṭhyābhiplavābhyām pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau gavāyurbhyām gavāyuṣī daśarātrāya daśarātro mahāvratāya mahāvratam udanīyāyātirātrāya udayanīyo 'tirātraḥ svargāya lokāyānnādyāya pratiṣṭhityai ||
meaning: अथातो ऽह्नां निवाहः प्रायणीयो ऽतिरात्रश् चतुर्विंशायाह्ने निवहति चतुर्विंशम् अहर् अभिप्लवाय अभिप्लवः पृष्ठ्याय पृष्ठ्यो ऽभिजिते अभिजित् स्वरसामभ्यः स्वरसामानो विषुवते विषुवान्त् स्वरसामभ्यः स्वरसामनो विश्वजिते विश्वजित् पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवाभ्याम् पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवौ गवायुर्भ्याम् गवायुषी दशरात्राय दशरात्रो महाव्रताय महाव्रतम् उदनीयायातिरात्राय उदयनीयो ऽतिरात्रः स्वर्गाय लोकायान्नाद्याय प्रतिष्ठित्यै ||

sanskrit_iast: ādityāś ca ha vā aṅgirasaś ca svarge loke 'spardhanta vayaṃ pūrve svar eṣyāmo vayaṃ pūrva iti ta ādityā laghubhiḥ sāmabhiś caturbhi stomair dvābhyāṃ pṛṣṭhyābhyāṃ svargaṃ lokam abhyaplavanta yad abhyaplavanta tasmād abhiplavaḥ anvañca evāṅgiraso gurubhiḥ sāmabhiḥ sarvai stomaiḥ sarvaiḥ pṛṣṭhyaiḥ svargaṃ lokam abhyaspṛśanta yad abhyaspṛśanta tasmāt spṛśyas taṃ vā etaṃ spṛśyaṃ santaṃ pṛṣṭhya ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ abhiplavāt pṛṣṭhyo nirmitaḥ pṛṣṭhyād abhijit abhijitaḥ svarasāmānaḥ svarasāmabhyo viṣuvān viṣuvataḥ svarasāmānaḥ svarasāmabhyo viśvajit viśvajitaḥ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavau pṛṣṭhyābhiplavābhyāṃ gavāyuṣī gavāyurbhyāṃ daśarātras tāni ha vā etāni yajñāraṇyāni yajñakṛntatrāṇi teṣāṃ śataṃśataṃ rathānānyantaraṃ tad yathāraṇyāny ārūḍhā aśanāpipāse te pāpmānaṃ tṛṃhatī pariplavete evaṃ haivaite praplavante ye 'vidvāṃsa upayantyi atha ye vidvāṃsa upayanti tad yathā pravāhāt pravāhaṃ sthalāt sthalaṃ samāt samaṃ sukhāt sukham abhayād abhayam upasaṃkrāmantīty evaṃ haivaite saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ samaśnavāmahā iti brāhmaṇam ||

text_mt:
Predi Kausurubindu of Kauśāmbī dwelt as a student of sacred knowledge with Uddālaka Āruṇi.
The teacher asked him: "Boy, how many days of the year did your father consider there to be?"
"How many indeed?"
"Ten," he said.
"Ten indeed!" he said.
"The virāj has ten syllables; the sacrifice belongs to the virāj."
"How many indeed?"
"Nine," he said.
"Nine indeed!" he said.
"Nine indeed are the vital breaths;
by the vital breaths the sacrifice is extended."
"How many indeed?"
"Eight," he said.
"Eight indeed!" he said.
"The gāyatrī has eight syllables;
the sacrifice is the gāyatrī."
"How many indeed?"
"Seven," he said.
"Seven indeed!" he said.
"Seven are the metres;
by the metres the sacrifice is extended."
"How many indeed?"
"Six," he said.

text_mt:
"Day by day—so is the entire year." [24]

Thus ends the fourth prapāṭhaka in the first part of the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa in the Atharvaveda.

Oṃ. The abhiplava is a six-day rite,
for there are six days: Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Go, Āyus, Jyotis.
The abhiplava is a five-day rite,
for there are five days,
because the first day is the last day.
The abhiplava is a four-day rite,
for there are four stomas: the trivṛt, the fifteenfold, the seventeenfold, and the twenty-onefold.
The abhiplava is a three-day rite:
the repetition of three: Jyotis, Go, Āyus.
The abhiplava is a two-day rite,
for there are only two sāmans: the bṛhat and the rathantara.
The abhiplava is a one-day rite,
for it is extended by the stomas of a one-day rite.
Of the four ukthya rites, twelve stotras are left over.
That is the seventh agniṣṭoma.
Thus indeed seven agniṣṭomas are completed in a month. Thus the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: athāto gādhapratiṣṭhā samudraṃ vā ete prataranti ye saṃvatsarāya dīkṣante teṣāṃ tīrtham eva prāyaṇīyo 'tirātras tīrthena hi prataranti tad yathā samudraṃ tīrthena pratareyus tādṛk tat gādhaṃ pratiṣṭhā caturviṃśam ahar yathopakakṣadagdhaṃ vā kaṇṭhadagdhaṃ vā yato viśramya prasnāyeyus tādṛk tat prasnayo 'bhiplavaḥ prasneyaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ gādhaṃ pratiṣṭhābhijid yathopakakṣadagdhaṃ vā kaṇṭhadagdhaṃ vā yato viśramya prasnāyeyus tādṛk tat nīvidagdha eva prathamaḥ svarasāmā jānudagdho dvitīyaḥ kulphadagdhas tṛtīyaḥ dvīpaḥ pratiṣṭhā viṣuvān yathopakakṣadagdhaṃ vā kaṇṭhadanghaṃ vā yato viśramya prasnāyeyus tādṛk tat kulphadagdha eva prathamo 'rvāk svarasāmā jānudagdho dvitīyaḥ nīvidagdhas tṛtīyaḥ gādhaṃ pratiṣṭhā viśvajid yathopakakṣadagdhaṃ vā kaṇṭhadagdhaṃ vā yato viśramya prasnāyeyus tādṛk tat prasneyaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ prasneyo 'bhiplavaḥ prasneye gavāyuṣī prasneyo daśarātraḥ gādhaṃ pratiṣṭhā mahāvrataṃ yathopakakṣadagdhaṃ vā kṇṭhadagdhaṃ vā yato viśramya prasnāyeyus tādṛk tat teṣāṃ tīrtham evodayanīyo 'tirātras tīrthena hy udyanti tad yathā samudraṃ tīrthenodeyus tādṛk tat atha ha smāha śvetaketur āruṇeyaḥ saṃvatsarāya nv ahaṃ dīkṣā iti tasya ha pitā mukham udīkṣyovāca vettha nu tvam āyuṣmant saṃvatsarasya gādhapratiṣṭhe iti vedeti etad dha smaitad vidvānāheti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अथातो गाधप्रतिष्ठा समुद्रं वा एते प्रतरन्ति ये संवत्सराय दीक्षन्ते तेषां तीर्थम् एव प्रायणीयो ऽतिरात्रस् तीर्थेन हि प्रतरन्ति तद् यथा समुद्रं तीर्थेन प्रतरेयुस् तादृक् तत् गाधं प्रतिष्ठा चतुर्विंशम् अहर् यथोपकक्षदग्धं वा कण्ठदग्धं वा यतो विश्रम्य प्रस्नायेयुस् तादृक् तत् प्रस्नयो ऽभिप्लवः प्रस्नेयः पृष्ठ्यः गाधं प्रतिष्ठाभिजिद् यथोपकक्षदग्धं वा कण्ठदग्धं वा यतो विश्रम्य प्रस्नायेयुस् तादृक् तत् नीविदग्ध एव प्रथमः स्वरसामा जानुदग्धो द्वितीयः कुल्फदग्धस् तृतीयः द्वीपः प्रतिष्ठा विषुवान् यथोपकक्षदग्धं वा कण्ठदन्घं वा यतो विश्रम्य प्रस्नायेयुस् तादृक् तत् कुल्फदग्ध एव प्रथमो ऽर्वाक् स्वरसामा जानुदग्धो द्वितीयः नीविदग्धस् तृतीयः गाधं प्रतिष्ठा विश्वजिद् यथोपकक्षदग्धं वा कण्ठदग्धं वा यतो विश्रम्य प्रस्नायेयुस् तादृक् तत् प्रस्नेयः पृष्ठ्यः प्रस्नेयो ऽभिप्लवः प्रस्नेये गवायुषी प्रस्नेयो दशरात्रः गाधं प्रतिष्ठा महाव्रतं यथोपकक्षदग्धं वा क्ण्ठदग्धं वा यतो विश्रम्य प्रस्नायेयुस् तादृक् तत् तेषां तीर्थम् एवोदयनीयो ऽतिरात्रस् तीर्थेन ह्य् उद्यन्ति तद् यथा समुद्रं तीर्थेनोदेयुस् तादृक् तत् अथ ह स्माह श्वेतकेतुर् आरुणेयः संवत्सराय न्व् अहं दीक्षा इति तस्य ह पिता मुखम् उदीक्ष्योवाच वेत्थ नु त्वम् आयुष्मन्त् संवत्सरस्य गाधप्रतिष्ठे इति वेदेति एतद् ध स्मैतद् विद्वानाहेति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Now therefore, the shallow ford and the firm standing: Truly, they cross an ocean, those who undergo consecration for a year. Their ford is the introductory Atirātra sacrifice, for it is by a ford that people cross. Just as they would cross an ocean by a ford, such is that. A shallow ford and a firm standing is the twenty-fourth day: just as [water reaching] armpit-deep or neck-deep, from which they might swim forward after resting, such is that. The swimming course is the Abhiplava; the swimming course is the Pṛṣṭhya. A shallow ford and a firm standing is the Abhijit day: just as [water reaching] armpit-deep or neck-deep, from which they might swim forward after resting, such is that. Reaching waist-deep is the first Svarasāman; reaching knee-deep is the second; reaching ankle-deep is the third. An island and a firm standing is the Viṣuvant day: just as [water reaching] armpit-deep or neck-deep, from which they might swim forward after resting, such is that. Reaching ankle-deep is the first reversed Svarasāman; reaching knee-deep is the second; reaching waist-deep is the third. A shallow ford and a firm standing is the Viśvajit day: just as [water reaching] armpit-deep or neck-deep, from which they might swim forward after resting, such is that. The swimming course is the Pṛṣṭhya; the swimming course is the Abhiplava; the swimming course is the Go and Āyus days; the swimming course is the ten-day period. A shallow ford and a firm standing is the Mahāvrata: just as [water reaching] armpit-deep or neck-deep, from which they might swim forward after resting, such is that. Their ford is the concluding Atirātra sacrifice, for it is by a ford that they emerge. Just as they would emerge from an ocean by a ford, such is that. Now, Śvetaketu Āruṇeya used to say: 'I shall undergo consecration for a year.'

His father looked at his face and said: 'Do you know, long-lived one, the shallow ford and the firm standing of the year?'

text_mt:
'Knowing this, he spoke thus'—so says the Brāhmaṇa.

The year is indeed the Puruṣa. His feet are the introductory Atirātra sacrifice, for with the feet people go forward. What is white in them is the form of the day; what is black is of the night; the nails are the form of the constellations; the hair is of the plants and trees. The thighs are the twenty-fourth day. The chest is the Abhiplava. The back is the Pṛṣṭhya. The head is the Trivṛt [stoma], for the head is threefold: skin, bone, and marrow or brain. The neck is the Pañcadaśa [stoma], for there are fourteen cervical vertebrae in it, and the strength is the fifteenth; therefore, though these are small, one bears a heavy load; therefore the neck is the Pañcadaśa. The chest is the Saptadaśa [stoma]: eight collarbones on one side, eight on the other, and the chest is the seventeenth; therefore the chest is the Saptadaśa. The belly is the Ekaviṃśa [stoma], for there are twenty abdominal viscera in it, and the belly is the twenty-first; therefore the belly is the Ekaviṃśa. The two sides are the Triṇava [stoma]: thirteen ribs on one side, thirteen on the other side—the two sides are the Triṇava; therefore the two sides are the Triṇava.

For there are thirty-two vertebrae in his back;

therefore the spine is the Trayastriṃśa.

His right arm is the Abhijit.

His three breaths on the right side are the Svarasāmans.

His three breaths on the left side are the reversed Svarasāmans.

His left arm is the Viśvajit.

The Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava have been explained.

The two downward breaths are the Go and Āyus days.

श्रमाद् अन्यत्र परिवर्तमानश् चरन् वासीनो यदि वा स्वपन्न् अपि | अहोरात्राभ्यां पुरुषः क्षणेन कति कृत्वः प्राणिति चापानीति च शतं शतानि परिवत्सराणाम् अष्टौ च शतानि संवत्सरस्य मुहूर्तान् यान् वदन्त्य् अहोरात्राभ्यां पुरुषः समेन कति कृत्वः प्राणिति चापानीति च इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
The Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava have been explained.

The two downward breaths are the Go and Āyus days.

His upward breath is the concluding Atirātra sacrifice,

The Puruṣa indeed is the year.
'Puruṣa' is one;
'the year' is one.
In this respect it is equal.
Two are the day and night of the year;
two are these vital breaths in the Puruṣa.
In this respect it is equal.
Three indeed are the seasons of the year;
three are these vital breaths in the Puruṣa.
In this respect it is equal.
Six indeed are the seasons of the year;
six are these vital breaths in the Puruṣa.
In this respect it is equal.
Seven indeed are the seasons of the year;
seven are these vital breaths in the Puruṣa.
In this respect it is equal.
Twelve are the months of the year;
twelve are these vital breaths in the Puruṣa.
In this respect it is equal.
Thirteen are the months of the year;
thirteen are these vital breaths in the Puruṣa.
In this respect it is equal.
Twenty-four are the half-months of the year;

twenty-fourfold is this Puruṣa:

having twenty fingers and toes, and four limbs.

Twenty-six are the half-months of the year;

with the two firm standings as the twenty-sixth.

Three hundred and sixty indeed are the days and nights of the year;

just so many are the vital breaths of the Puruṣa.

Seven hundred and twenty indeed are the days and nights of the year;

just so many are the bones and marrows of the Puruṣa.

Fourteen hundred and forty indeed are the half-days and half-nights of the year;

just so many are the thick pieces of flesh of the Puruṣa.

Twenty-eight hundred and eighty indeed are the quarter-days and quarter-nights of the year;

just so many are the sinews and joints of the Puruṣa.

Ten thousand and eight hundred indeed are the muhūrtas of the year;

just so many are the tissues and veins of the Puruṣa.

As many muhūrtas as there are, fifteen times that many are the out-breathings.

As many out-breathings as there are, fifteen times that many are the in-breathings.

As many in-breathings as there are, fifteen times that many are the diffused breathings.

As many diffused breathings as there are, fifteen times that many are the middle breathings.

As many middle breathings as there are, fifteen times that many are the upward breathings.

As many upward breathings as there are, fifteen times that many are the etādis.

As many etādis as there are, so many are the etarhis.

As many as are the etarhis, so many are the sweat-pores.

As many as are the sweat-pores, so many are the kṣiprāyaṇas.

As many as are the kṣiprāyaṇas, so many are the pores of the body-hairs.

As many as are the pores of the body-hairs fifteen times, so many are the streams of rain when it rains.

That is this measure of a hundred krośas.

This has also been stated in a verse:
'Turning about away from weariness, moving or sitting or even sleeping, / by days and nights, how many times in a moment does a person breathe out and breathe in? A hundred hundreds of parivatsaras, and eight hundred muhūrtas of the year as they call them: by days and nights, in equal measure, how many times does a person breathe out and breathe in?' Thus the Brāhmaṇa. || 5

text_mt:
Vāsyu used to say: 'The equality of the year should be known.
They perform only one atirātra before the viṣuvant, one after.
They perform fifty-three agniṣṭomas before the viṣuvant, fifty-three after.
They perform one hundred and twenty ukthyas before the viṣuvant, one hundred and twenty after.
They perform six ṣoḍaśins before the viṣuvant, six after.
They perform thirty six-day periods before the viṣuvant, thirty after.
That is the equality of the year.
He who thus knows this equality of the year, having become of the same self and dwelling in the same world with the year, merges into the gods.' Thus the Brāhmaṇa. || 6

text_mt:
Prajāpati desired: 'May I attain endlessness.' Having established the fires, he sacrificed with the full offering: he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Agnihotra, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the first-fruits sacrifice, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Cāturmāsyas, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the animal sacrifice, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Agniṣṭoma, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Rājasūya, he assumed the name 'King': he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Vājapeya, he assumed the name 'Emperor': he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Aśvamedha, he assumed the name 'Sovereign': he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Puruṣamedha, he assumed the name 'Ruler': he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with the Sarvamedha, he assumed the name 'All-Ruler': he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with Ahīna sacrifices accompanied by sacrificial fees, he saw only an end. Having sacrificed with Ahīna sacrifices not accompanied by sacrificial fees, he saw only an end. In the end, he sacrificed with a sacrificial session having an Atirātra on both sides. He gave voice to the Hotṛ;

out-breath to the Adhvaryu, sight to the Udgātṛ, mind to the brahman priest, the limbs to the subordinate Hotṛ priests, and his self to the members of the assembly.

Thus, having given himself as endlessness, he attained endlessness.

Then, having bought back himself by means of the sacrificial fees that he brought,

therefore one should hasten to perform this Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, which is the buying back of oneself, has a thousand [cows as] sacrificial fee, and is a pacifier of the back.

text_mt:
For whoever dies without having sacrificed with the pacifier of the back, dies without having bought back himself—thus states the Brāhmaṇa.

When year-sitters consecrate themselves for a year, how is their Agnihotra not interrupted?
'By the observance milk,' one should say.
How is their New-Moon sacrifice not interrupted?
'By curd and sacrificial cake,' one should say.
How is their Full-Moon sacrifice not interrupted?
'By clarified butter and sacrificial cake,' one should say.
How is their first-fruits sacrifice not interrupted?
'By an oblation pot dedicated to Soma,' one should say.
How are their four-month sacrifices not interrupted?
'By curds,' one should say.
How is their animal sacrifice not interrupted?
'By the animal and sacrificial cake,' one should say.
How is their Soma sacrifice not interrupted?
'By the libation cups,' one should say.
How is their domestic sacrifice not interrupted?
'By parched grains and porridge,' one should say.
How is their sacrifice to the ancestors not interrupted?
'By domestic offerings,' one should say.
How is their mating not interrupted?
'By the hiṃ-sound,' one should say.
This is the absorption of sacrificial rites into the year.
He who thus knows this absorption of sacrificial rites into the year, becoming of the same self and having the same world through sacrifice, merges into the gods—thus the Brāhmaṇa.

text_mt:
The gods consecrated themselves for a thousand-year session. When five hundred of their years had passed, then all this became exhausted—the chants, the back-lauds, the recitations. Those gods were halfway exhausted here; [they said:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice-rite which is the counterpart of the thousand-year session. For who is the mortal that could sacrifice with a thousand-year session?' Then they saw the unfatigued [essence] in the middle of the sacrifice. By that unfatigued [essence], they saw in five parts the manifestation that was in the Veda: in the verse, in the sacrificial formula, in the chant, in the pacified, and in the terrible. These indeed become the five sacred utterances: 'Make hear!', 'May he hear!', 'Śrauṣaṭ!', 'Recite!', 'We who sacrifice!', 'Vauṣaṭ!' Those gods were halfway exhausted here; [they said:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice-rite which is the counterpart of the thousand-year session. For who is the mortal that could sacrifice with a thousand-year session?' Then they saw this Tāpaścita rite as the direct manifestation of the thousand-year session. For they are indeed those very chants, those back-lauds, those recitations. It indeed proceeds for twelve months with consecrations, twelve months with upasads, twelve months with soma-pressings. Now, in that it proceeds for twelve months with consecrations and twelve months with upasads, thereby one reaches these two, fire and the sun. And in that it proceeds for twelve months with soma-pressings, thereby one obtains this Great Uktha. Those gods were halfway exhausted here; [they said:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice-rite which is the counterpart of the thousand-year session. For who is the mortal that could sacrifice with a thousand-year session?' Then they saw this year as the direct manifestation of the Tāpaścita rite. For they are indeed those very chants, those back-lauds, those recitations. Those gods were halfway exhausted here; [they said:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice-rite which is the counterpart of the thousand-year session. For who is the mortal that could sacrifice with a thousand-year session?' Then they saw this twelve-day rite as the direct manifestation of the year. For they are indeed those very chants, those back-lauds, those recitations. It indeed proceeds for twelve days with consecrations, twelve days with upasads, twelve days with soma-pressings.

Now, in that it proceeds for twelve days with consecrations and twelve days with upasads, thereby one reaches these two, fire and the sun.

And in that it proceeds for twelve days with soma-pressings, thereby one obtains this Great Uktha.

Those gods resided here for half [the time, saying:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice which is the counterpart of the thousand-year [sacrifice].

For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?'

Then they saw this pṛṣṭhya six-day rite as the direct route of the twelve-day rite.

For those very stomā-chants they are, those pṛṣṭha-chants, those recitations.

Those gods resided here for half [the time, saying:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice which is the counterpart of the thousand-year [sacrifice].

For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?'

Then they saw this Viśvajit as the direct route of the pṛṣṭhya six-day rite.

For those very stomā-chants they are, those pṛṣṭha-chants, those recitations.

Those gods resided here for half [the time, saying:] 'Let us discover that sacrifice which is the counterpart of the thousand-year [sacrifice].

meaning: पुरुषं ह वै नारायणं प्रजापतिर् उवाच यजस्य यजस्वेति स होवाच यजस्व यजस्वेत्य् एवं हात्थ मा त्रिर् अपि क्षत मे वसवः प्रातःसवनेनागू रुद्रा माध्यंदिनसवनेनादित्यास् तृतीयसवनेन यज्ञवास्तुन्य् एव पर्यशिषो यज्ञवास्तुम् इत्य् एवम् आशिषो ऽहं वा एतद् वेद यज्ञे वसवः प्रातःसवनेनागू रुद्रा माध्यंदिनसवनेनादित्यास् तृतीयसवनेन यज्ञवास्तुन्य् एव पर्यशिषो यज्ञवास्तुम् इत्य् एवम् आशिषो विद्वांसो नूनं त्वा याजयेयुः एते ह वा अविद्वांसो यत्रानृग्विद् धोता भवत्य् अयजुर्विद् अध्वर्युर् असामविद् उद्गाताभृग्वङ्गिरोविद् ब्रह्मा यजस्वैव हन्त तु ते तद् वक्ष्यामि यथा सूत्रे मणिर् इव सूत्रम् एतान्य् उक्थाहानि भवन्ति सूत्रम् इव वा मणाव् इति तस्माद् य एव सर्ववित् स्यात् तं ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत एष ह वै विद्वांत् सर्वविद् ब्रह्मा यद् भृग्वङ्गिरोवित् एते ह वा अस्य सर्वस्य शमयितारः पालयितारस् तमाद् ब्रह्मा स्तुते बहिःपवमाने वाचयति ||
text_mt:
For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?'

It is indeed this Viśvajit which is the counterpart of the thousand-year [sacrifice].

This Viśvajit is Prajāpati of the creatures—thus the Brāhmaṇa.

Prajāpati said to Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa: 'Sacrifice, sacrifice!'
He said: ''Sacrifice, sacrifice!'—thus indeed you speak to me.
Three times they have destroyed me: the Vasus departed with the morning pressing, the Rudras with the midday pressing, and the Ādityas with the evening soma-pressing.
You have left behind in the sacrificial site alone the blessings, as 'the sacrificial site!' I indeed know this in the sacrifice: the Vasus departed with the morning pressing, the Rudras with the midday pressing, and the Ādityas with the evening soma-pressing, and you have left behind in the sacrificial site alone the blessings, as 'the sacrificial site!' Let knowing ones surely officiate for you.
Indeed, those are unlearned where the Hotṛ does not know the Ṛgveda, the Adhvaryu does not know the Yajurveda, the Udgātṛ does not know the Sāmaveda, and the brahman priest does not know the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases.
Do sacrifice! Come, I will tell that to you:
just as a jewel is on a string, or a string in a jewel, so are these uktha-days.
Therefore, whosoever is all-knowing, him one should make the brahman priest.
This is indeed the knowing, all-knowing brahman priest: one who knows the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases.
These indeed are the pacifiers and protectors of all this.
Therefore, while the Bahiṣpavamāna hymn is being praised, the brahman priest makes [the sacrificer] recite.

sanskrit_iast: atha mādhyaṃdine pavamāne vācayati samrāḍ asi triṣṭupchandā anu tvārabhe svasti mā saṃpārayeti sa yad āha samrāḍ asīti somaṃ vā etad āha eṣa ha vai vāyurbhūtvāntarikṣaloke samrājati tad yat samrājati tasmāt samrāṭ tat samrājasya samrāṭtvam sa yad āha triṣṭupchandā anu tvārabha iti traiṣṭubhena chandasā rudrair devair mādhyaṃdine savane 'ntarikṣaloke vāyuṃ santam anvārabhate sa yad āha svasti mā saṃpārayeti traiṣṭubhenaiva chandasā rudrair devair mādhyaṃdine savane antarikṣaloke vāyunā devena svasti mā saṃpārayeti traiṣṭubhenaivainaṃ tac chandasā rudrair devair mādhyaṃdine savane antarikṣaloke vāyunā devena svasti saṃpadyate ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: अथ माध्यंदिने पवमाने वाचयति सम्राड् असि त्रिष्टुप्छन्दा अनु त्वारभे स्वस्ति मा संपारयेति स यद् आह सम्राड् असीति सोमं वा एतद् आह एष ह वै वायुर्भूत्वान्तरिक्षलोके सम्राजति तद् यत् सम्राजति तस्मात् सम्राट् तत् सम्राजस्य सम्राट्त्वम् स यद् आह त्रिष्टुप्छन्दा अनु त्वारभ इति त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसा रुद्रैर् देवैर् माध्यंदिने सवने ऽन्तरिक्षलोके वायुं सन्तम् अन्वारभते स यद् आह स्वस्ति मा संपारयेति त्रैष्टुभेनैव छन्दसा रुद्रैर् देवैर् माध्यंदिने सवने अन्तरिक्षलोके वायुना देवेन स्वस्ति मा संपारयेति त्रैष्टुभेनैवैनं तच् छन्दसा रुद्रैर् देवैर् माध्यंदिने सवने अन्तरिक्षलोके वायुना देवेन स्वस्ति संपद्यते य एवं वेद ||

sanskrit_iast: athārbhave pavamāne vācayati svaro 'si gayo 'si jagacchandā anu tvārabhe svasti mā saṃpārayeti sa yad āha svaro 'sīti somaṃ vā etad āha eṣa ha vai sūryo bhūtvāmuṣmiṃl loke svarati tad yat svarati tasmāt svaras tat svarasya svaratvam sa yad āha gayo 'sīti somaṃ vā etad āha eṣa ha vai candramā bhūtvā sarvāṃl lokān gacchati tad yad gacchati tasmād gayas tad gayasya gayatvam sa yad āha jagacchandā anu tvārabha iti jāgatena chandasādityair devais tṛtīyasavane 'muṣmiṃl loke sūryaṃ santam anvārabhate sa yad āha svasti mā saṃpārayeti jāgatenaiva chandasādityair devais tṛtīyasavane 'muṣmiṃl loke sūryeṇa devena svasti mā saṃpārayeti jāgatenaivainaṃ tac chandasādityair devais tṛtīyasavane 'muṣmiṃl loke sūryeṇa devena svasti saṃpadyate ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: अथार्भवे पवमाने वाचयति स्वरो ऽसि गयो ऽसि जगच्छन्दा अनु त्वारभे स्वस्ति मा संपारयेति स यद् आह स्वरो ऽसीति सोमं वा एतद् आह एष ह वै सूर्यो भूत्वामुष्मिंल् लोके स्वरति तद् यत् स्वरति तस्मात् स्वरस् तत् स्वरस्य स्वरत्वम् स यद् आह गयो ऽसीति सोमं वा एतद् आह एष ह वै चन्द्रमा भूत्वा सर्वांल् लोकान् गच्छति तद् यद् गच्छति तस्माद् गयस् तद् गयस्य गयत्वम् स यद् आह जगच्छन्दा अनु त्वारभ इति जागतेन छन्दसादित्यैर् देवैस् तृतीयसवने ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके सूर्यं सन्तम् अन्वारभते स यद् आह स्वस्ति मा संपारयेति जागतेनैव छन्दसादित्यैर् देवैस् तृतीयसवने ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके सूर्येण देवेन स्वस्ति मा संपारयेति जागतेनैवैनं तच् छन्दसादित्यैर् देवैस् तृतीयसवने ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके सूर्येण देवेन स्वस्ति संपद्यते य एवं वेद ||

sanskrit_iast: atha saṃsthite saṃsthite savane vācayati mayi bhargo mayi maho mayi yaśo mayi sarvam iti pṛthivy eva bhargo 'ntarikṣa eva maho dyaur eva yaśo 'pa eva sarvam agnir eva bhargo vāyur eva maha āditya eva yaśaś candramā eva sarvam vasava eva bhargo rudrā eva maha ādityā eva yaśo viśvedevā eva sarvam gāyatry eva bhargas triṣṭub eva maho jagaty eva yaśo 'nuṣṭub eva sarvam prācy eva bhargaḥ pratīcy eva maha udīcy eva yaśo dakṣiṇaiva sarvam vasanta eva bhargo grīṣma eva maho varṣā eva yaśaḥ śarad eva sarvam trivṛd eva bhargaḥ pañcadaśa eva mahaḥ saptadaśa eva yaśa ekaviṃśa eva sarvam ṛgveda eva bhargo yajurveda eva mahaḥ sāmaveda eva yaśo brahmaveda eva sarvam hotaiva bhargo 'dhvaryur eva maha udgātaiva yaśo brahmaiva sarvam vāg eva bhargaḥ prāṇa eva mahaś cakṣur eva yaśo mana eva sarvam ||
meaning: अथ संस्थिते संस्थिते सवने वाचयति मयि भर्गो मयि महो मयि यशो मयि सर्वम् इति पृथिव्य् एव भर्गो ऽन्तरिक्ष एव महो द्यौर् एव यशो ऽप एव सर्वम् अग्निर् एव भर्गो वायुर् एव मह आदित्य एव यशश् चन्द्रमा एव सर्वम् वसव एव भर्गो रुद्रा एव मह आदित्या एव यशो विश्वेदेवा एव सर्वम् गायत्र्य् एव भर्गस् त्रिष्टुब् एव महो जगत्य् एव यशो ऽनुष्टुब् एव सर्वम् प्राच्य् एव भर्गः प्रतीच्य् एव मह उदीच्य् एव यशो दक्षिणैव सर्वम् वसन्त एव भर्गो ग्रीष्म एव महो वर्षा एव यशः शरद् एव सर्वम् त्रिवृद् एव भर्गः पञ्चदश एव महः सप्तदश एव यश एकविंश एव सर्वम् ऋग्वेद एव भर्गो यजुर्वेद एव महः सामवेद एव यशो ब्रह्मवेद एव सर्वम् होतैव भर्गो ऽध्वर्युर् एव मह उद्गातैव यशो ब्रह्मैव सर्वम् वाग् एव भर्गः प्राण एव महश् चक्षुर् एव यशो मन एव सर्वम् ||
text_mt:
Then, as each pressing is concluded, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "In me be splendor; in me be greatness; in me be glory; in me be all."
The earth alone is splendor; the intermediate space alone is greatness; heaven alone is glory; the waters alone are all.
Agni alone is splendor; Vāyu alone is greatness; Āditya alone is glory; the moon alone is all.
The Vasus alone are splendor; the Rudras alone are greatness; the Ādityas alone are glory; the All-Gods alone are all.
The gāyatrī alone is splendor; the triṣṭubh alone is greatness; the jagatī alone is glory; the anuṣṭubh alone is all.
The east alone is splendor; the west alone is greatness; the north alone is glory; the south alone is all.
Spring alone is splendor; summer alone is greatness; the rainy season alone is glory; autumn alone is all.
The trivṛt alone is splendor; the pañcadaśa alone is greatness; the saptadaśa alone is glory; the ekaviṃśa alone is all.
The Ṛgveda alone is splendor; the Yajurveda alone is greatness; the Sāmaveda alone is glory; the Brahmaveda alone is all.
The Hotṛ alone is splendor; the Adhvaryu alone is greatness; the Udgātṛ alone is glory; the Brahman alone is all.
Speech alone is splendor; breath alone is greatness; sight alone is glory; mind alone is all. || 15

sanskrit_iast: sa yad āha mayi bharga iti pṛthivīm evaital lokānām ahāgniṃ devānāṃ vasūn devān devagaṇānāṃ gāyatraṃ chandasāṃ prācīṃ diśāṃ vasantam ṛtūnāṃ trivṛtaṃ stomānām ṛgvedaṃ vedānāṃ hautraṃ hotrakāṇāṃ vācam indriyāṇām ||
meaning: स यद् आह मयि भर्ग इति पृथिवीम् एवैतल् लोकानाम् अहाग्निं देवानां वसून् देवान् देवगणानां गायत्रं छन्दसां प्राचीं दिशां वसन्तम् ऋतूनां त्रिवृतं स्तोमानाम् ऋग्वेदं वेदानां हौत्रं होत्रकाणां वाचम् इन्द्रियाणाम् ||
text_mt: When he says, "In me be splendor," he means the earth among the worlds, Agni among the deities, the god-Vasus among the divine hosts, the gāyatrī among the metres, the east among the directions, spring among the seasons, the trivṛt among the stomas, the Ṛgveda among the Vedas, the Hotṛ's office among the offices of the subordinate Hotṛ priests, and speech among the senses. || 16

sanskrit_iast: sa yad āha mayi maha ity antarikṣam evaital lokānām āha vāyuṃ devānāṃ rudrān devān devagaṇānāṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ chandasāṃ pratīcīṃ diśāṃ grīṣmam ṛtūnāṃ pañcadaśaṃ stomānāṃ yajurvedaṃ vedānām ādhvaryavaṃ hotrakāṇāṃ prāṇam indriyāṇām ||
meaning: स यद् आह मयि मह इत्य् अन्तरिक्षम् एवैतल् लोकानाम् आह वायुं देवानां रुद्रान् देवान् देवगणानां त्रैष्टुभं छन्दसां प्रतीचीं दिशां ग्रीष्मम् ऋतूनां पञ्चदशं स्तोमानां यजुर्वेदं वेदानाम् आध्वर्यवं होत्रकाणां प्राणम् इन्द्रियाणाम् ||
text_mt: When he says, "In me be greatness," he means the intermediate space among the worlds, Vāyu among the deities, the god-Rudras among the divine hosts, the triṣṭubh among the metres, the west among the directions, summer among the seasons, the pañcadaśa among the stomas, the Yajurveda among the Vedas, the Adhvaryu's office among the offices of the subordinate Hotṛ priests, and breath among the senses. || 17

sanskrit_iast: sa yad āha mayi yaśa iti divam evaital lokānām āhādityaṃ devānām ādityān devagaṇānāṃ jāgataṃ chandasām udīcīṃ diśāṃ varṣā ṛtūnāṃ saptadaśaṃ stomānāṃ sāmavedaṃ vedānām audgātraṃ hotrakāṇāṃ cakṣur indriyāṇām ||
meaning: स यद् आह मयि यश इति दिवम् एवैतल् लोकानाम् आहादित्यं देवानाम् आदित्यान् देवगणानां जागतं छन्दसाम् उदीचीं दिशां वर्षा ऋतूनां सप्तदशं स्तोमानां सामवेदं वेदानाम् औद्गात्रं होत्रकाणां चक्षुर् इन्द्रियाणाम् ||
text_mt: When he says, "In me be glory," he means heaven among the worlds, Āditya among the deities, the Ādityas among the divine hosts, the jagatī among the metres, the north among the directions, the rainy season among the seasons, the saptadaśa among the stomas, the Sāmaveda among the Vedas, the Udgātṛ's office among the offices of the subordinate Hotṛ priests, and sight among the senses. || 17

sanskrit_iast: sa yad āha mayi sarvam ity apa evaital lokānām āha candramasaṃ devānāṃ viśvān devān devagaṇānām ānuṣṭubhaṃ chandasāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśāṃ śaradam ṛtūnām ekaviṃśaṃ stomānāṃ brahmavedaṃ vedānāṃ brahmatvaṃ hotrakāṇāṃ mana indriyāṇām ||
meaning: स यद् आह मयि सर्वम् इत्य् अप एवैतल् लोकानाम् आह चन्द्रमसं देवानां विश्वान् देवान् देवगणानाम् आनुष्टुभं छन्दसां दक्षिणां दिशां शरदम् ऋतूनाम् एकविंशं स्तोमानां ब्रह्मवेदं वेदानां ब्रह्मत्वं होत्रकाणां मन इन्द्रियाणाम् ||
text_mt: When he says, "In me be all," he means the waters among the worlds, the moon among the deities, the All-Gods among the divine hosts, the anuṣṭubh among the metres, the south among the directions, autumn among the seasons, the ekaviṃśa among the stomas, the Brahmaveda among the Vedas, the Brahman's office among the offices of the subordinate Hotṛ priests, and mind among the senses. || 18

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣa daśadhā catuḥ saṃpadyate daśa ca ha vai catur virājo 'kṣarāṇi taṃ garbhā upajīvanti śrīr vai virāḍ yaśo 'nnādyam śriyam eva tad virājaṃ yaśasy annādyo pratiṣṭhāpayati pratiṣṭhantīr idaṃ sarvam anupratiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: स वा एष दशधा चतुः संपद्यते दश च ह वै चतुर् विराजो ऽक्षराणि तं गर्भा उपजीवन्ति श्रीर् वै विराड् यशो ऽन्नाद्यम् श्रियम् एव तद् विराजं यशस्य् अन्नाद्यो प्रतिष्ठापयति प्रतिष्ठन्तीर् इदं सर्वम् अनुप्रतिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति प्रजया पशुभिर् य एवं वेद ||
text_mt:
sa vā eṣa daśadhā catuḥ saṃpadyate
daśa ca ha vai catur virājo 'kṣarāṇi
taṃ garbhā upajīvanti
śrīr vai virāḍ
yaśo 'nnādyam_
śriyam eva tad virājaṃ yaśasy annādyo pratiṣṭhāpayati
pratiṣṭhantīr idaṃ sarvam anupratiṣṭhati
pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda || 20

sanskrit_iast: anarvāṇaṃ ha vai devaṃ dadhyaṅṅ āṅgirasa upasīdaṃ ha yajñasya śnuṣṭiṃ samaśnavāmaha iti sa dadhyaṅṅ āṅgiraso 'bravīd yo vai saptadaśaṃ prajāpatiṃ yajñe 'nvitaṃ veda nāsya yajño riṣyate na yajñapatiṃ riṣyanta iti tā vā etāḥ pañca vyāhṛtayo bhavanty o śrāvayāstu śrauṣaḍ yaja ye yajāmahe vauṣaḍ iti sa dadhyaṅṅ āṅgiraso 'bravīn na vayaṃ vidmo yadi brāhmaṇāḥ smo yady abrāhmaṇāḥ smo yadi tasyarṣeḥ smo vānyasyeti anarvāṇaś ca ha vā ṛtāvantaś ca pitaraḥ svadhāyām āvṛṣāyanta vayaṃ vadāmahai vayaṃ vadāmahā iti so 'yāt svāyaṃbhuvo vā ṛtāvanto madayātāṃ na vayaṃ vadāmahā iti tasmāt pravare pravriyamāṇe vācayed devāḥ pitara iti tisraḥ ya eti saṃyajati sa bhavati yaś ca na brūte yaś ca na brūta iti brāhmaṇam ||
meaning: अनर्वाणं ह वै देवं दध्यङ्ङ् आङ्गिरस उपसीदं ह यज्ञस्य श्नुष्टिं समश्नवामह इति स दध्यङ्ङ् आङ्गिरसो ऽब्रवीद् यो वै सप्तदशं प्रजापतिं यज्ञे ऽन्वितं वेद नास्य यज्ञो रिष्यते न यज्ञपतिं रिष्यन्त इति ता वा एताः पञ्च व्याहृतयो भवन्त्य् ओ श्रावयास्तु श्रौषड् यज ये यजामहे वौषड् इति स दध्यङ्ङ् आङ्गिरसो ऽब्रवीन् न वयं विद्मो यदि ब्राह्मणाः स्मो यद्य् अब्राह्मणाः स्मो यदि तस्यर्षेः स्मो वान्यस्येति अनर्वाणश् च ह वा ऋतावन्तश् च पितरः स्वधायाम् आवृषायन्त वयं वदामहै वयं वदामहा इति सो ऽयात् स्वायंभुवो वा ऋतावन्तो मदयातां न वयं वदामहा इति तस्मात् प्रवरे प्रव्रियमाणे वाचयेद् देवाः पितर इति तिस्रः य एति संयजति स भवति यश् च न ब्रूते यश् च न ब्रूत इति ब्राह्मणम् ||
text_mt:
Dadhyañc Āṅgirasa approached the divine Anarvan, saying: "May we attain the successful conclusion of the sacrifice."
Dadhyañc Āṅgirasa said: "He who knows Prajāpati as the seventeenfold one accompanied in the sacrifice—his sacrifice is not harmed;
nor are the sacrificers harmed."
These are the five sacred utterances: 'Oṃ, cause to hear', 'Be it heard', 'Sacrifice', 'We who sacrifice', 'Vauṣaṭ'.
That Dadhyañc Āṅgirasa said: "We do not know whether we are brahmins or whether we are non-brahmins, whether we belong to this seer or to another."
Both the Anarvans and the truth-holding ancestors acted like bulls over the svadhā call, [saying,] 'We shall speak! We shall speak!'
He went: 'Either the self-existent ones or the truth-holding ones shall gladden; we shall not speak.'
Therefore, when the lineage-invocation is being chosen, he should make [him] recite the three [verses beginning] 'The divine ancestors...'
He who goes thus and sacrifices together, he thrives; and he who does not recite, and he who does not recite—so says the Brāhmaṇa. || 21

sanskrit_iast: sāvitraṃ ha smaitaṃ pūrve purastāt paśum ālabhanta ity etarhi prājāpatyam yo hy eva savitā sa prajāpatir iti vadantas tasmād u samupyāgnīṃs tena yajeran te samānadhiṣṇyā eva syur okhāsaṃbharaṇīyāyāḥ ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyāyāṃ vinyupayāgnīṃs tayā yajeran te nānādhiṣṇyā eva syur ā dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ dīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ saṃnyupyāgnīṃs tayā yajeran te samānadhiṣṇyā eva syur odavasānīyāyāḥ udavasānīyāyāṃ vinyupyāgnīṃs tayā yajeran te nānādhiṣṇyā eva syuḥ atha yadi yajamānasyopatapet pārśvato 'gnīn ādhāya tāvad āsīta yāvad agadaḥ syāt yadi preyāt svair eva tam agnibhir dahet aśavāgnibhir itare yajamānā āsata iti vadantas tasya tad eva brāhmaṇaṃ yad adaḥ puraḥsavane pitṛmedha āśiṣo vyākhyātāḥ ||
meaning: सावित्रं ह स्मैतं पूर्वे पुरस्तात् पशुम् आलभन्त इत्य् एतर्हि प्राजापत्यम् यो ह्य् एव सविता स प्रजापतिर् इति वदन्तस् तस्माद् उ समुप्याग्नींस् तेन यजेरन् ते समानधिष्ण्या एव स्युर् ओखासंभरणीयायाः उखासंभरणीयायां विन्युपयाग्नींस् तया यजेरन् ते नानाधिष्ण्या एव स्युर् आ दीक्षणीयायाः दीक्षणीयायां संन्युप्याग्नींस् तया यजेरन् ते समानधिष्ण्या एव स्युर् ओदवसानीयायाः उदवसानीयायां विन्युप्याग्नींस् तया यजेरन् ते नानाधिष्ण्या एव स्युः अथ यदि यजमानस्योपतपेत् पार्श्वतो ऽग्नीन् आधाय तावद् आसीत यावद् अगदः स्यात् यदि प्रेयात् स्वैर् एव तम् अग्निभिर् दहेत् अशवाग्निभिर् इतरे यजमाना आसत इति वदन्तस् तस्य तद् एव ब्राह्मणं यद् अदः पुरःसवने पितृमेध आशिषो व्याख्याताः ||
text_mt: "The ancients used to seize this victim for Savitṛ beforehand, but now [it is] for Prajāpati," saying, "for he who is Savitṛ is Prajāpati." Therefore, heaping the fires together, they should sacrifice with it. They should have the same hearths until the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyā. Having scattered the fires apart at the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyā, they should sacrifice with it. They should have separate hearths until the Dīkṣaṇīyā. Having heaped the fires together at the Dīkṣaṇīyā, they should sacrifice with it. They should have the same hearths until the Udavasānīyā. Having scattered the fires apart at the Udavasānīyā, they should sacrifice with it. They should have separate hearths. Now, if the sacrificer should fall ill, having placed the fires at his side, he should remain as long as he is not cured. If he should die, he should burn him with his very own fires, saying, "The other sacrificers sit with non-corpse fires." Its explanation is the very same as that there in the morning pressing; the blessings in the ancestral sacrifice have been explained.

sanskrit_iast: sāyaṃprātarhomau sthālīpāko navaś ca yaḥ | baliś ca pitṛyajñaś cāṣṭakā saptamaḥ paśuḥ || ity ete pākayajñāḥ agnyādheyam agnihotraṃ paurṇamāsyamāvāsye | naveṣṭiś cāturmāsyāni paśubandho 'tra saptamaḥ || ity ete haviryajñāḥ agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśimāṃs tataḥ | vājapeyo 'tirātraś cāptoryāmātra saptamaḥ || ity ete sutyāḥ ke svid devā pravovājāḥ ke svid devā abhidyavaḥ | ke svid devā haviṣmantaḥ kiṃ svij jigāti sumnayuḥ || ṛtava eva pravovājā māsā devā abhidyavaḥ | ardhamāsā haviṣmantas taj jigāti sunmayuḥ || kati svid rātrayaḥ katy ahāni kati stotrāṇi kati śastrāṇy asya | kati svit savanāḥ saṃvatsarasya stotriyāḥ padākṣarāṇi katy asya || dvāv atirātrau ṣaṭ śatam agniṣṭomā dve viṃśatiśate ukthyānāṃ | dvādaśa ṣoḍaśinaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ ṣaḍahā vaiṣuvataṃ ca || ahānyasya viṃśatiśatāni trīṇy ahaś caikaṃ tāvad asya | saṃvatsarasya savanāḥ sahasram asīti trīṇi ca saṃstutasya || ṣaṭṣaṣṭiś ca dve ca śate bhavata stutaśastrāṇām ayutaṃ caikam asya | stotriyāś ca navatisahasrā dve niyute navatiś cāti ṣaṭ ca || aṣṭau śatāny ayutāni triṃśac caturnavatiś ca padāny asya | saṃvatsarasya kavibhir mitasyaitāvatī madhyamā devamātrā || ayutam ekaṃ prayutāni triṃśad dve niyute tathā hy anusṛṣṭāḥ | aṣṭau śatāni nava cākṣarāṇy etāvān ātmā paramaḥ prajāpateḥ || ādyaṃ vaṣaṭkāraḥ pradānāntam etam agniṣṭome parvaśaḥ sādhu kḷptam | saubheṣajaṃ chanda īpsan yad agnau catuḥśataṃ bahudhā hūyate yat || prātaḥsavana stuta ekaviṃśo gāyatrastomamita eka eva | mādhyaṃdinaḥ saptadaśena kḷptas trayastriṃśena savanaṃ tṛtīyam ||
meaning: सायंप्रातर्होमौ स्थालीपाको नवश् च यः | बलिश् च पितृयज्ञश् चाष्टका सप्तमः पशुः || इत्य् एते पाकयज्ञाः अग्न्याधेयम् अग्निहोत्रं पौर्णमास्यमावास्ये | नवेष्टिश् चातुर्मास्यानि पशुबन्धो ऽत्र सप्तमः || इत्य् एते हविर्यज्ञाः अग्निष्टोमो ऽत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः षोडशिमांस् ततः | वाजपेयो ऽतिरात्रश् चाप्तोर्यामात्र सप्तमः || इत्य् एते सुत्याः के स्विद् देवा प्रवोवाजाः के स्विद् देवा अभिद्यवः | के स्विद् देवा हविष्मन्तः किं स्विज् जिगाति सुम्नयुः || ऋतव एव प्रवोवाजा मासा देवा अभिद्यवः | अर्धमासा हविष्मन्तस् तज् जिगाति सुन्मयुः || कति स्विद् रात्रयः कत्य् अहानि कति स्तोत्राणि कति शस्त्राण्य् अस्य | कति स्वित् सवनाः संवत्सरस्य स्तोत्रियाः पदाक्षराणि कत्य् अस्य || द्वाव् अतिरात्रौ षट् शतम् अग्निष्टोमा द्वे विंशतिशते उक्थ्यानां | द्वादश षोडशिनः षष्टिः षडहा वैषुवतं च || अहान्यस्य विंशतिशतानि त्रीण्य् अहश् चैकं तावद् अस्य | संवत्सरस्य सवनाः सहस्रम् असीति त्रीणि च संस्तुतस्य || षट्षष्टिश् च द्वे च शते भवत स्तुतशस्त्राणाम् अयुतं चैकम् अस्य | स्तोत्रियाश् च नवतिसहस्रा द्वे नियुते नवतिश् चाति षट् च || अष्टौ शतान्य् अयुतानि त्रिंशच् चतुर्नवतिश् च पदान्य् अस्य | संवत्सरस्य कविभिर् मितस्यैतावती मध्यमा देवमात्रा || अयुतम् एकं प्रयुतानि त्रिंशद् द्वे नियुते तथा ह्य् अनुसृष्टाः | अष्टौ शतानि नव चाक्षराण्य् एतावान् आत्मा परमः प्रजापतेः || आद्यं वषट्कारः प्रदानान्तम् एतम् अग्निष्टोमे पर्वशः साधु कॢप्तम् | सौभेषजं छन्द ईप्सन् यद् अग्नौ चतुःशतं बहुधा हूयते यत् || प्रातःसवन स्तुत एकविंशो गायत्रस्तोममित एक एव | माध्यंदिनः सप्तदशेन कॢप्तस् त्रयस्त्रिंशेन सवनं तृतीयम् ||
text_mt:
"The evening and morning oblations, the boiled mess of grain, the new-harvest [rite], / the bali-offering, the Ancestor-sacrifice, the aṣṭakā, and the seventh is the animal sacrifice"—these are the pākayajñas.
"The establishment of the fires, the agnihotra, the new- and full-moon rites, / the first-fruits sacrifice, the seasonal sacrifices, and the animal sacrifice is here the seventh"—these are the haviryajñas.
"The agniṣṭoma, the atyagniṣṭoma, the ukthya, then the one having the ṣoḍaśin, / the vājapeya, the atirātra, and the aptoryāma is here the seventh"—these are the soma-pressings.
"Who are the gods possessed of superior vigour? Who are the gods turned towards heaven? / Who are the gods possessing oblations? Whither does the seeker of favor go?"
"The seasons indeed are possessed of superior vigour; the months are the gods turned towards heaven; / the half-months are those possessing oblations; thither goes the seeker of favor."
"How many nights are there? How many days? How many are its chants? How many its recitations? / How many are the pressings of the year? How many are its strophic verses, words, and syllables?"
Two atirātras, one hundred and six agniṣṭomas, two hundred and twenty ukthyas, / twelve ṣoḍaśins, sixty six-day periods, and the central day.
Its days are three hundred and twenty, plus one day; so many are its [days]. / Of the fully-praised year, the pressings are one thousand and eighty-three.
And the chanted recitations are ten thousand two hundred and sixty-six of it; / and the strophic verses are two hundred and ninety thousand and ninety-six.
Its words are thirty myriad, eight hundred and ninety-four / of the year measured by the poets; such is the intermediate divine measure.
Thirty myriad, one ten-thousand, and two hundred thousand, thus indeed they are created; / eight hundred and nine syllables—such is the supreme self of Prajāpati.
The first is the vaṣaṭ-call ending in the presentation, well fashioned in the agniṣṭoma section by section; / seeking the metre which has healing, that which is offered in many ways into the fire four hundred times.
At the morning pressing, the chant is twenty-one-fold, the only one measured with the gāyatrī-stoma; / the midday [pressing] is fashioned with the seventeen-fold, the third pressing with the thirty-three-fold. || 23

sanskrit_iast: śraddhāyāṃ retas tapasā tapasvī vaiśvānaraḥ siṣice 'patyam īpsan | tato jajñe lokajit somajambhā ṛṣer ṛṣir aṅgirāḥ saṃnabhūva || ṛṣer yajñasya caturvidhasya śraddhāṃ yaḥ śreyasīṃ lokam amuṃ jigāya | yasmai vedāḥ prasṛtāḥ somabindu yuktā vahanti sukṛtām u lokam || ṛco 'sya bhāgāṃś caturo vahanty ukthaśastraiḥ pramudo modamānāḥ | grahair havirbhiś ca kṛtākṛtaś ca yajūṃṣi bhāgāṃś caturo vahanti || audumbaryāṃ sāmaghoṣeṇa tāvat saviṣṭutibhiś ca stomaiḥ chandasā | sāmāni bhāgāṃś caturo vahanti gītyā stomena saha prastāvena ca || prāyaścittair bheṣajaiḥ saṃstuvanto 'tharvāṇo 'ṅgirasaś ca śāntāḥ | brahmā brahmatvena pramudo modamānā asaṃsṛṣṭān bhāgāṃś caturo vahanti || yo brahmavit so 'bhikaro 'stu vaḥ śivo dhiyā dhīro rakṣatu dharmam etam | mā vaḥ pramattām amṛtāc ca yajñāt karmāc ca yenān aṅgiraso 'piyāsīt || māyuṃ daśaṃ māruśastāḥ prameṣṭā mā me bhūr yuktā vidahātha lokān | divyaṃ bhayaṃ rakṣata dharmam udyataṃ yajñaṃ kālāśa stutigopanāyanam || hotā ca maitrāvaruṇaś ca pādam acchāvākaḥ saha grāvastutaikam | ṛgbhi stuvanto 'harahaḥ pṛthivyā agniṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti || adhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātā neṣṭonnetā nihitaṃ pādam ekam | sam antarikṣaṃ yajuṣā stuvanto vāyuṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti || sāmnodgātā chādayann apramatta audumbaryāṃ stobhadeyaḥ sagadgadaḥ | vidvān prastotā vidahātha suṣṭutiṃ subrahmaṇyaḥ pratihartātha yajñe || sāmnā divy ekaṃ nihitaṃ stuvantaḥ sūryaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti | brahmā haikaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ saha potāgnīdhro nihitaṃ pādam ekam || atharvabhir aṅgirobhiś ca gupto 'psu candraṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti | ṣoḍaśikaṃ hotrakā abhiṣṭuvanti vedeṣu yuktāḥ prapṛthak caturdhā || manīṣiṇo dīkṣitāḥ śraddadhānā hotāro guptā abhivahanti yajñam | dakṣiṇato brahmaṇasyoṃ janad ity etāṃ vyāhṛtiṃ japan || saptadaśaṃ sadasyaṃ taṃ kīrtayanti purā viduḥ | aṣṭādaśī dīkṣitā dīkṣitānāṃ yajñe patnī śraddadhāneha yuktā || ekonaviṃśaḥ śamitā babhūva viṃśo yajñe gṛhapatir eva sunvan | ekaviṃśatir evaiṣāṃ saṃsthāyām aṅgiro vaha || vedair abhiṣṭuto loko nānāveśāparājitaḥ | ||
meaning: श्रद्धायां रेतस् तपसा तपस्वी वैश्वानरः सिषिचे ऽपत्यम् ईप्सन् | ततो जज्ञे लोकजित् सोमजम्भा ऋषेर् ऋषिर् अङ्गिराः संनभूव || ऋषेर् यज्ञस्य चतुर्विधस्य श्रद्धां यः श्रेयसीं लोकम् अमुं जिगाय | यस्मै वेदाः प्रसृताः सोमबिन्दु युक्ता वहन्ति सुकृताम् उ लोकम् || ऋचो ऽस्य भागांश् चतुरो वहन्त्य् उक्थशस्त्रैः प्रमुदो मोदमानाः | ग्रहैर् हविर्भिश् च कृताकृतश् च यजूंषि भागांश् चतुरो वहन्ति || औदुम्बर्यां सामघोषेण तावत् सविष्टुतिभिश् च स्तोमैः छन्दसा | सामानि भागांश् चतुरो वहन्ति गीत्या स्तोमेन सह प्रस्तावेन च || प्रायश्चित्तैर् भेषजैः संस्तुवन्तो ऽथर्वाणो ऽङ्गिरसश् च शान्ताः | ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मत्वेन प्रमुदो मोदमाना असंसृष्टान् भागांश् चतुरो वहन्ति || यो ब्रह्मवित् सो ऽभिकरो ऽस्तु वः शिवो धिया धीरो रक्षतु धर्मम् एतम् | मा वः प्रमत्ताम् अमृताच् च यज्ञात् कर्माच् च येनान् अङ्गिरसो ऽपियासीत् || मायुं दशं मारुशस्ताः प्रमेष्टा मा मे भूर् युक्ता विदहाथ लोकान् | दिव्यं भयं रक्षत धर्मम् उद्यतं यज्ञं कालाश स्तुतिगोपनायनम् || होता च मैत्रावरुणश् च पादम् अच्छावाकः सह ग्रावस्तुतैकम् | ऋग्भि स्तुवन्तो ऽहरहः पृथिव्या अग्निं पादं ब्रह्मणा धारयन्ति || अध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाता नेष्टोन्नेता निहितं पादम् एकम् | सम् अन्तरिक्षं यजुषा स्तुवन्तो वायुं पादं ब्रह्मणा धारयन्ति || साम्नोद्गाता छादयन्न् अप्रमत्त औदुम्बर्यां स्तोभदेयः सगद्गदः | विद्वान् प्रस्तोता विदहाथ सुष्टुतिं सुब्रह्मण्यः प्रतिहर्ताथ यज्ञे || साम्ना दिव्य् एकं निहितं स्तुवन्तः सूर्यं पादं ब्रह्मणा धारयन्ति | ब्रह्मा हैकं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः सह पोताग्नीध्रो निहितं पादम् एकम् || अथर्वभिर् अङ्गिरोभिश् च गुप्तो ऽप्सु चन्द्रं पादं ब्रह्मणा धारयन्ति | षोडशिकं होत्रका अभिष्टुवन्ति वेदेषु युक्ताः प्रपृथक् चतुर्धा || मनीषिणो दीक्षिताः श्रद्दधाना होतारो गुप्ता अभिवहन्ति यज्ञम् | दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मणस्यों जनद् इत्य् एतां व्याहृतिं जपन् || सप्तदशं सदस्यं तं कीर्तयन्ति पुरा विदुः | अष्टादशी दीक्षिता दीक्षितानां यज्ञे पत्नी श्रद्दधानेह युक्ता || एकोनविंशः शमिता बभूव विंशो यज्ञे गृहपतिर् एव सुन्वन् | एकविंशतिर् एवैषां संस्थायाम् अङ्गिरो वह || वेदैर् अभिष्टुतो लोको नानावेशापराजितः | ||
text_mt:
Seeking offspring, ascetic Vaiśvānara through ascetic heat shed semen into faith; / thence was born the conqueror of worlds, Soma-devouring; from the ṛṣi the ṛṣi Aṅgiras arose.
He who won faith, better than the fourfold sacrifice of the ṛṣi, [won] that world, / for whom the spread Vedas bearing drops of Soma carry him to the world of the well-doers.
Four portions of this [sacrifice] the Ṛg-verses bear, rejoicing with delights through uktha-recitations; / and through cups and oblations, what is done and undone, the Yajus-formulas bear four portions.
Near the audumbarī post, with the sound of the Sāman so long, and with hymns, stomas, and metre, / the Sāmans bear four portions, along with song, stoma, and prelude.
Exalting with expiations and healings, the Atharvans and pacified Aṅgirases, / the brahman priest through the office of brahman, rejoicing with delights, bear four unmixed portions.
May he who knows Brahman be your benefactor, auspicious; wise in thought, let him protect this sacred order; / do not become heedless of the immortal sacrifice and of the ritual act by which Aṅgiras passed beyond.
[Do not bring] bleating, a decade, destructive commands, death; do not, conjoined with my earth, burn up the worlds; / protect from heavenly fear the raised sacred order, the sacrifice, whose end is time, a shield of praise.
